1	# Handoff — Opus token savings on entire-graph, measured 2026-08-03
2	
3	Goal given: **Opus ≥ −25% tokens** on a 20-instance sample of SWE-bench Multilingual.
4	**Not met.** Best honest number: **−11.2%**. This document is everything needed to continue without
5	repeating the work, including the parts that wasted the most time.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. The number, and the config that produces it
10	
11	```
12	PROMPT_FAMILY unset · PUBLISHED_EXACT=1 · CC_MODEL=opus · CLAUDE_EFFORT=high
13	EG_PREFETCH=1 EG_PREFETCH_IMPACT=1 · EG_TOPK=5 EG_CONF_TIER=0 EG_TOPK_SHOW=10
14	EG_MAXBYTES=24576 EG_SNIPPET=6 EG_MAX_PER_FILE=3 EG_VERIFY_MODE=full EG_PROFILE=full EG_TIER=0
15	GQ_SEARCH_CAP=1 · CC_MAX_TURNS=120 CC_TIMEOUT=3600
16	TASKS_FILE=tasks/opus20_official.json · binary /tmp/eg-f19 (eg-consolidated @ 024f25a)
17	```
18	Worker: `/tmp/mcptest/pubworker.sh`. Scorer: `tools/model_cmp.py`.
19	
20	**Result: tokens −11.2% CI [−27.8, +9.6], usd −8.4%, output −13.1% [−23.3, −1.9], winners 12/20, n=20.**
21	
22	`PUBLISHED_EXACT=1` emits Anthropic's published SWE-bench Verified prompt verbatim to **both** arms;
23	eg additionally gets one capability paragraph + the prefetched search/impact payload. Verified
24	symmetric by line-diff on emitted `prompt.txt`, coaching-language scan = 0 in both arms.
25	`CC_MAX_TURNS=120` matters: the baseline averages **50.2** turns, so the default cap of 50
26	right-censors the BASELINE specifically and understates its cost.
27	
28	---
29	
30	## 2. Every configuration measured (Opus, same 20 instances unless noted)
31	
32	| config | baseline ops | eg ops | ops Δ | ktok/session | **tokens** | n |
33	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
34	| **PUB** — published prompt + prefetch | 35.7 | 31.7 | −11.2% | 2729k | **−11.2%** [−27.8,+9.6] | 20 |
35	| FRUGAL — rich methodology both arms, frugal shared block | 7.0 | 5.0 | −28.6% | 279k | −14.0% | 23 (rep30) |
36	| CB — clamp + published scaffold | 10.5 | 8.3 | −20.6% | 345k | +7.5% | 3 |
37	| GC — gated clamp, symmetric | 11.5 | 12.0 | +4.3% | 378k | +11.4% | 6 |
38	| S1O — S1 mirrored clamp | 4.6 | 4.3 | −8.0% | 175k | +18.2% [+2.3,+37.2] | 19 |
39	| G40 — rich methodology + published scaffold | 23.8 | 28.7 | +21.1% | 1300k | +28.4% [+7.9,+54.8] | 19 |
40	| R30PUB — PUB config on rep30 | 29.4 | 27.5 | −6.5% | 2468k | **−14.4%** [−28.9,+3.1] | **30 of 30, COMPLETE** |
41	| ~~OFF~~ | 39.0 | 27.5 | −29.6% | — | ~~−46.5%~~ | **INVALID** |
42	
43	**OFF is invalid and must never be quoted.** `EG_CAPABILITY_ONLY` was checked in `tool_block()` but
44	never in `briefed_tool_block()`, and every cell used the `briefed` family — so the flag was dead while
45	`BASE_CAPABILITY_ONLY` worked. The baseline lost its 5-step methodology while eg kept its 4-step one
46	(24 lines, 116 words, ending "STOP. No re-search, no grep to double-check"). Now wired; the same class
47	of bug recurred later with `BASE_GATED_CLAMP` (wired into `tool_block` but not the vendor family).
48	**Always diff emitted `prompt.txt`, never trust config.**
49	
50	---
51	
52	## 3. The two quantitative laws (use these to predict before spending)
53	
54	**Law 1 — outcome is set by the BASELINE's wastefulness, not by eg.**
55	```
56	eg_ops = 14.16 + 0.588 · base_ops        break-even at base_ops = 34.4
57	```
58	eg's op count is statistically flat between winners and losers (**d = −0.08, p = 0.97**); the
59	baseline's is decisive (**d = +1.55, p = 0.0069**, AUC 0.865 vs 0.495). Rule accuracy 15/20; it is
60	sharp above 54 ops and below 34, mushy in the 35–50 band.
61	
62	**Law 2 — tokens are superlinear in ops.**
63	```
64	log(tokRatio) = 1.207 · log(opRatio)      R² = 0.916
65	```
66	Confirmed out of sample: rep30 ops −31.2% → predicted −38.6%, measured −40.9%. 94–96% of tokens are
67	`cache_read`, so each extra op re-reads the whole accumulated context.
68	
69	**Corollary — the payload tax is a pure function of session size:** ~0 at 2729k, +7 at 1300k, +18 to
70	+28 below 400k. So −25% requires ops ≤ −25% **and** a long session. Every clamp config sits at
71	175–378k where the tax alone exceeds the op saving. That is why CB cut 20.6% of ops and still lost.
72	
73	---
74	
75	## 4. The confirmed, untried lever: **aim**
76	
77	Measured with `/tmp/eg-agx` (entire-graph @ `afd5a1c`, sha `f6a18d3ca7c2`) on 9 rep30 instances,
78	gold lines resolved by locating hunk context in the base file (hunk headers are invalid at base —
79	fmtlib is off by +272):
80	
81	| | result |
82	|---|---|
83	| gold **FILE** in payload | **9/9 = 100%** |
84	| gold **LINE** covered by a printed span | **0/9 ≈ 0%** |
85	
86	| instance | gold line | payload's spans in that same file |
87	|---|---|---|
88	| lucene-13170 | 148 | 34-36, 27, 181-188, 118-124 — brackets it, never covers it |
89	| caddy-5995 | 133 | 343-465, 59 |
90	| carbon-3098 | 497 | 1201-1228 |
91	| django-13821 | 64 | 431-487 |
92	| docusaurus-9183 | 313 | 375 |
93	| ruff-15626 | 25 | 37-41 |
94	| fastlane-19765 | 101 | 357-366, 214-229 |
95	| faker-2970 | 65 | 33-49 |
96	| fmt-2457 | 357 | 682 |
97	
98	**Right file always, right region never.** This is the only mechanism that explains the one result
99	that held across all five Opus cells: **pre-edit locate went UP every time (+3.7% to +9%)**. The agent
100	gets the correct file at a wrong offset, greps it anyway, and pays twice.
101	
102	**Root cause, verified in source** (`internal/sem/search_related.go`):
103	- line 41: *"Deliberately NOT included: outgoing CALLS … already reached as co-members of the same unit"*
104	- line 62: `searchRelatedUnitMemberLimit = 12`; line 568 disables the co-member route above it
105	
106	So on a large unit **neither** route reaches the callee. redis-10095 is textbook: gold at
107	`src/t_list.c:501`, eg returns `t_list.c:577` (`lpopCommand`, a lexical match on "LPOP") — the
108	reply-shaping bug is in the helper it *calls*.
109	
110	Full diagnosis and the F1/F2/F3 proposals: **`/Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-graph/TOKEN-ACCURACY-PLAN.md`**.
111	Two corrections to it from this session:
112	1. Its step-2 gate is **cleared**: the unmerged `codex/eg-graphify-advertised-bench` branch does
113	   **not** move line coverage (clean A/B, same codebase, coverage identical, payload bytes differ).
114	2. Its 32.4%-vs-58.3% winner/loser split does **not** reproduce on this corpus — I measure ~0% for
115	   both. So the F1 sizing argument (close a 26-point gap) does not hold here, but the underlying
116	   defect is **larger** than diagnosed, not smaller.
117	
118	**Sizing is the open question**, and the two available routes differ 10×:
119	- plan's fit (9.6% tokens per residual shell call × ~3 calls) → −29%/loser → **−22.6%** on the 20-set
120	- my decomposition (LOCATE is only **14.5%** of the +76-op loser overrun) → −3.8%/loser → **−12.7%**
121	
122	**The discriminator, not yet run:** correlate per-instance gold-line coverage against per-instance
123	residual locate ops. If coverage predicts residual ops, the plan's route is right and F1 is worth
124	~11 points. Tooling for it exists: `/tmp/mcptest/linecov.py` (resolver verified correct against patch
125	shapes — lucene 1 hunk/1+/1− = 2 gold lines, django 4+/2− = 6).
126	
127	---
128	
129	## 5. MEASUREMENT INTEGRITY — fix before quoting any number
130	
131	`tools/netjail/` blocks `curl wget git gh ssh scp rsync nc ncat socat aria2c xh http https`.
132	It does **not** block **npm, yarn, pip, composer, go, cargo** — and every one can fetch a post-fix
133	release of the repo under test. Three confirmed leaks, in both arms, in cells quoted above:
134	
135	| instance | arm | leak | that instance's result |
136	|---|---|---|---|
137	| docusaurus-10130 | **eg** | `npm pack @docusaurus/core@3.4.0` → extracted `brokenLinks.js` → grepped it → **the next tool call is the Edit with that content detranspiled**. The issue number `10116` in the patch appears nowhere in the prompt. | **−38% "winner"** in the −11.2% cell |
138	| caddy-5995 | **baseline** | read `~/go/pkg/mod/…caddy/v2@v2.11.4/replacer.go` (gold line verbatim) **and** the PR's own new test fixture, copied it into the checkout, wrote a test reproducing `test_patch` | −56% winner; 27 of 66 baseline ops |
139	| carbon-2752 | **eg** | unzipped `~/Library/Caches/composer/files/nesbot/carbon/*.zip` → gold regex, transcribed into `patch.diff` | +107% loser |
140	
141	Also: **fmt-2457's swings are 132% baseline-side** — eg's absolute cost *falls* PUB→G40 (4.25M→2.94M)
142	while the baseline collapses (5.16M→1.13M). Its PUB "win" was bought by 17 baseline messages running a
143	two-compiler `orig-vs-new` matrix (`g++-15`: 7 occurrences baseline, 0 eg). Treat that instance as noise.
144	
145	**Required fixes:** netjail shims for registry-fetch subcommands (`npm pack|install <pkg>`, `yarn add`,
146	`pip download|install`, `composer require`, `go get`, `cargo add`) while leaving local provisioning
147	intact; plus per-instance cache isolation — already implemented in `/tmp/mcptest/s1worker.sh`
148	(`GOMODCACHE GOPATH GOCACHE COMPOSER_HOME COMPOSER_CACHE_DIR CARGO_HOME GEM_HOME GEM_PATH
149	npm_config_cache MAVEN_ARGS=-Dmaven.repo.local`).
150	Three of the four known leaks favour eg, so closing them will most likely make −11.2% **worse**.
151	
152	---
153	
154	## 6. Refuted — do NOT retry. Each cost a cell or a day.
155	
156	Every item below was killed by a **winner control**: the same pattern is equally present in the
157	instances the tool wins on, so it cannot explain a loss. A 5-agent sweep produced 38 candidate
158	defects; **27 of 28 adjudicated were refuted this way.**
159	
160	| claim | how it died |
161	|---|---|
162	| payload bodies carry no line numbers | true in **20/20** instances incl. every winner. Also `internal/cli/search.go:473` documents that numbering bodies **breaks `Edit` anchors** (agents copy snippet text as `old_string`), and `focus=` already ships |
163	| `impact` blind-chained to an ungated rank-1 | off-gold-file target in **7/12 winners**, in *more* degenerate form in the two largest wins |
164	| query polluted by GitHub issue-template boilerplate | 2/6 control winners have boilerplate queries producing boilerplate top hits |
165	| hits printed out of score order | 5/20 payloads, incl. winners lucene (−52%) and vuejs (−24%) |
166	| missing / lint-only `VERIFY` | partial corr collapses +0.184 → **+0.091**; by class **lint-only is BEST** (−24.6%), `none` worst (+20.5%) but contains 2 winners |
167	| missing `COVERING TEST` causes test-hunting | **inverted** — present in 4/8 losers (50%) vs 1/12 winners (8%) |
168	| "40% of post-edit ops re-hunt payload text" | **base rate.** Baseline searches the same strings at 2.42/session vs eg's 2.42 (W) and 1.38 vs 1.25 (L). Payload exposure changes it by +0.00 / −0.13 |
169	| provisioning episodes cause the loss | `package-install` **decreases** in losers (0.62→0.38); clumpiness 0.13 in the loser **baseline** vs 0.14 in its eg arm |
170	| get the agent to use the graph more | tripling usage (0.20→3.00 calls/session) measured **worse**: caddy −56%→−13%, mean +17.8pt. The 3 winners that called it averaged −23.7% vs −36.9% for the 9 that didn't |
171	| index tests (lift `graph_exclude.globs`) | rebuild indexes 4,748 test symbols but search output is **byte-identical**; the gold test was already at rank 2 |
172	| extend the covering-test path mirror | 10/12 in a unit test, **byte-identical payloads** on real checkouts — improved the wrong path (`COVERING TEST` comes from ranked results, the mirror only feeds `VERIFY`) |
173	| prefetch a test-scoped search (`EG_PREFETCH_TEST`) | found the gold test in **1 of 4**; the query that worked came from the issue text, not the payload |
174	| the published prompt's "explore the repo" step causes it | only **9%** of first-four pre-edit ops are structure exploration |
175	| widen the window (`--head-window-lines` + top-k 20) | **+18.9pt worse** (prior measurement, independently consistent) |
176	| payload/prompt token tax explains the split | **5.16%** (W) vs **5.19%** (L) — identical |
177	
178	---
179	
180	## 7. Reproduce
181	
182	```sh
183	cd /Users/suhaan/graphmark-bench/agentic-swebench
184	# one cell, 40 sessions, ~2h at parallelism 10
185	bash /tmp/mcptest/launch.sh /tmp/mcptest/pubworker.sh /tmp/mcptest/pubjobs.txt 10 /tmp/mcptest/pub.log
186	python3 tools/model_cmp.py "PUB_r1_baseline,PUB_r1_eg,label"
187	# aim measurement (free, offline)
188	python3 /tmp/mcptest/linecov.py apache__lucene-13170 redis__redis-10095 ...
189	```
190	
191	**Non-negotiables**
192	- Gate: `total_cost_usd > 0` AND non-empty `patch.diff`, dropped **symmetrically**.
193	- `CENSORED` (`subtype == error_max_turns`) must be 0 per arm.
194	- Round trips = unique assistant `message.id`, never `num_turns` (it is `tool_calls + 1`).
195	- Parallelism ≤ ~20. Above ~30, empty patches ran 14–27% vs 0% at ~15, and arm symmetry breaks.
196	- **Never score a partial cell.** rep30 read −40.9% (n=4) → −24.6% (n=8) → −13.9% (n=10) → −22.3% (n=21) → **−14.4% (n=30, final)**. Winners 18/30.
197	- Launcher: use `/tmp/mcptest/launch.sh` (bash, jobs on fd 3). `xargs -P … -I{}` mangles input on
198	  macOS, and zsh does not word-split unquoted `$VAR` — that produced a jobs file with 38 of 40 lines
199	  malformed and cost two wasted launches.
200	- Thinking text is **redacted** in all transcripts (`thinking` present but empty), so reasoning volume
201	  is unmeasurable; only block counts and `output_tokens` are available.
202	
203	## 8. What I would do next, in order
204	
205	1. **Close the leaks** (§5) and re-measure PUB. Nothing is quotable until this is done, and it will
206	   probably make the number worse. One cell, 40 sessions.
207	2. **Run the aim discriminator** (§4) — free, offline, decides whether F1 is worth ~11 points or ~2.
208	3. **Only if it clears: implement F1** narrowly — enable the callee hop only where the co-member
209	   fallback is already off (`len(members) > searchRelatedUnitMemberLimit`) **and** the body-match
210	   signal is absent. Budget-neutral: move the window's centre, never widen it. Do **not** start with
211	   F2 (multi-span allocation) — that is where a budget-neutral claim is easiest to break.
212	4. Gate on gold-**line** coverage offline, then on session tokens **and graded resolves**. File
213	   coverage is 100% on winners and losers alike and must be retired as a metric.

1	# entire-graph — tokens and accuracy: diagnosis, and the refutation of my own thesis
2	
3	**Diagnosed 2026-08-03**, newest local build (`test/all-agent-fixes` @ `afd5a1c`, sha256 `f6a18d3ca7c2`),
4	run hands-on against the repos where eg measurably loses (redis, fmtlib, gson, laravel, lombok, sharkdp,
5	fastlane, apache, micropython).
6	
7	> ## ⚠️ Read this first
8	> An earlier version of this document argued that eg loses because it lands on the **right file, wrong
9	> region**, and that fixing aim was the largest available token lever (~11 points). **I tested that claim
10	> and it did not hold.** Controlling for baseline exploration volume, gold-line coverage does **not**
11	> predict eg's residual exploration: partial r = **−0.131** at n=30, where ~0.36 is needed for
12	> significance. What predicts eg's residual ops is **baseline difficulty** (r = **+0.380**).
13	> The aim thesis survives as an *accuracy* observation and is **dead as a token mechanism**.
14	> §1–2 are the real diagnosis; §3 is the refutation; §4 is what is actually left.
15	
16	---
17	
18	## 1. What is true: eg finds the right FILE and the wrong REGION
19	
20	Same binary, real agent queries from `gq_calls.log`, gold lines resolved via `git apply` offsets (hunk
21	headers are invalid at the base commit — fmtlib is off by +272 lines).
22	
23	| group | n | gold **FILE** found | mean gold **LINE** coverage | mean payload bytes |
24	|---|---|---|---|---|
25	| losing instances | 8 | **8/8 = 100%** | **32.4%** | 5,513 |
26	| winning instances (control) | 6 | **6/6 = 100%** | **58.3%** | 3,964 |
27	
28	**File coverage is 100% in both groups — it carries no signal.** Suite-wide on rep30 (n=30), mean
29	line coverage is only **25.2%**.
30	
31	Two concrete, reproducible misses:
32	
33	**redis-10095** — *"LPOP with count returns null bulk reply instead of null array reply"*
34	gold at `src/t_list.c:501`; eg returned `t_list.c:577` (`lpopCommand`) and `t_list.c:1031`. Right file
35	twice, missed by 76 lines. `lpopCommand` matches "LPOP" *lexically*; the bug is in the helper it calls.
36	
37	**gson-2158** — gold is **8 hunks** (`Gson.java:398,422` + `TypeAdapters.java:194…353`); eg returned
38	`TypeAdapters.java:908` (`newFactory`) and `Gson.java:240-339` (constructor) — the structurally
39	prominent symbols, while the fix lives in six sibling adapter bodies.
40	
41	### The code that produces it
42	`internal/sem/search_related.go:41` excludes outgoing CALLS because callees are *"already reached as
43	co-members of the same unit"* — but that fallback is bounded by `searchRelatedUnitMemberLimit = 12`, and
44	the same file states that past the bound *"the co-member route switches off entirely"*. `t_list.c`
45	(~1100 lines) and `TypeAdapters.java` are far past it, so on large units **neither** route reaches the
46	callee. The exclusion is correct for small units and leaves a hole exactly where the losses are.
47	
48	`planSearchHeadWindow` (`search_enclosure.go:242`) already centres a window on `FocusLine`, so aim is a
49	**centring** problem, not a window-size problem. (Window size is `--head-window-lines`, measured
50	**+18.9 pt worse** with top-k 20.)
51	
52	---
53	
54	## 2. Bugs found
55	
56	1. **41 of 112 eg graphs build DEGRADED** (DeepSWE v1.1 corpus; graphify 0/112 — though graphify emits
57	   no such signal, so this may be reporting asymmetry, not quality). Degraded graphs ship **silently**;
58	   this belongs in the payload so a wrong answer is attributable.
59	2. **`entire graph version` reports `dev`** for real local builds — cells cannot pin by version, only by
60	   sha256, and the SWE-bench ladder refuses `dev` outright.
61	3. **Unmerged search fixes on `codex/eg-graphify-advertised-bench`** (+14 commits, 47 files): *"preserve
62	   hard file limits and coverage scores"*, *"keep legacy eligibility before widening"*. Directly on-topic
63	   and not in the newest dev branch. **Evaluate before writing new code.**
64	4. **Cross-platform packaging unguarded.** A macOS arm64 binary in linux/amd64 benchmark containers
65	   failed `rc=126`, returned an **empty payload**, and scored as if the tool were worthless — silently
66	   wrong, and it looked like a measurement. Guarded in the DeepSWE harness; entire-graph should publish
67	   and verify a linux/amd64 artifact.
68	5. **Gold-line resolver collapsed deletion-only hunks** (lombok `HandleBuilder` +0/−9 resolved to 2
69	   lines). Fixed in `scratchpad/diag_losers.py`. It did **not** affect §1's anchors — 0 of those 14
70	   instances are deletion-dominant — but it would have corrupted any suite-wide run.
71	
72	---
73	
74	## 3. The refutation
75	
76	**Hypothesis tested.** Low coverage → the agent greps the correctly-found file itself → residual shell
77	calls → tokens. If true, coverage should predict residual ops negatively, and should still do so after
78	controlling for how much the *baseline* explored (savings independently track baseline volume,
79	corr −0.56 — the band structure).
80

80	
81	**Result, n=30 on the rep30 set (`R30Seg` vs `R30Sbase`):**
82	
83	```

1	# Opus → −35% tokens: the plan
2	
3	**Measured 2026-08-03.** Opus cell: `R30Oeg` vs `R30Obase`/`R30ObaseB`/`R30ObaseV3` (**three replicates
4	of one baseline config** — identical prompt sha256 `290a553f54a6`), n=23 paired. Mechanism validated
5	across **3,370 sessions in 168 cells** using the payloads the agents actually received.
6	Build `test/all-agent-fixes` @ `afd5a1c`, sha `f6a18d3ca7c2`.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## 0. Bottom line
11	
12	**Opus token savings are API-call savings, and nothing else.**
13	```
14	TOKEN delta   -19.5%   95% CI [-29.9, -8.8]
15	CALL  delta   -18.7%   corr with token delta +0.960,   R^2 = 0.922
16	CTX   delta    -0.7%   context per call: eg 26,791 vs base 26,849  (identical)
17	```
18	Context per call is identical between arms, so payload size, aim, and coverage can only matter through
19	their effect on **call count**.
20	
21	**The mechanism.** The eg prompt commands *"(2) EDIT from the body it printed. Do not re-read that file."*
22	That is only **possible to obey for 11% of Opus edits** (13.8% across all 3,370 sessions). When it is
23	possible, sessions need **−25.1% fewer API calls** — stratified within cell and within fix-size band,
24	n=439 editable vs 1,232 not, **95% CI [−31.0, −18.7]**, 107/153 strata favouring editable. Every model
25	family shows it independently:
26	
27	| family | sessions | edits editable | calls: editable vs not |
28	|---|---|---|---|
29	| **Opus** | 135 | **11.0%** | **8.83 vs 11.70** |
30	| Sonnet | 704 | 9.0% | 12.65 vs 21.85 |
31	| Haiku | 629 | 11.7% | 22.74 vs 31.25 |
32	| C-series | 320 | 16.0% | 14.14 vs 25.99 |
33	
34	**−35% is reachable.** Raising editability is worth this much on Opus (baseline 11.84 calls):
35	
36	| editability | L1+L2 only | **+ L3 edit batching** |
37	|---|---|---|
38	| 9% (today) | 9.96 calls −15.9% | 8.31 calls −18.4% |
39	| 50% | 8.91 −24.8% | 7.26 −28.8% |
40	| 70% | 8.40 −29.1% | 6.75 −33.8% |
41	| **75%** | 8.27 −30.2% | **6.62 −35.0%** ✓ |
42	| **85%** | 8.01 −32.3% | **6.36 −37.5%** ✓ |
43	| **100%** | **7.63 −35.6%** ✓ | 5.98 −41.3% ✓ |
44	
45	At the **pessimistic end of the CI** (−18.7%), full editability plus L3 still gives **−35.4%**.
46	**The target is met at 75% editability with both levers, or 100% with L1+L2 alone.**
47	
48	---
49	
50	## 1. The token identity (why calls are the only lever)
51	
52	Per-message usage, deduped by `requestId` — Claude Code splits one API response across transcript lines,
53	so raw line counts overstate calls ~2×:
54	```
55	billed/session        302,535 tok      API calls/session   9.96 eg / 11.84 base
56	  cache_read           273,122  90.3%  context at call 1     17,722 tok  <-- re-read EVERY call
57	  cache_creation        20,180   6.7%  context at last call  31,021 tok
58	  output                 9,213   3.0%  growth all session    13,300 tok
59	marginal cost of 1 call  ~24,400 tok = 11% of a median session
60	```
61	**57% of even the final context is the fixed harness prompt.** Everything the agent reads all session is
62	13,300 tokens; total context inflow across every tool (18.7 KB/session) is just **19%** of session tokens,
63	and eg's payload is 4.6 KB of that.
64	
65	**Retired here — the payload-cap idea from this document's first draft.** A 6,144 B per-call cap removes
66	3.4% of payload bytes ≈ **0.16% of session tokens**; the 24,576 cap never binds (`8192` clips 0/29 calls).
67	`gson-2158`, the one apparent payload story (21.6% share, +29% vs replicate 1), is **−2% vs replicate 2**.
68	Payload **bytes** are the seventh payload metric to fail as a token lever. **Payload *editability* is a
69	different quantity and is the one that survived** — it predicts calls, which is the only thing that pays.
70	
71	---
72	
73	## 2. Where the 9.96 calls go
74	
75	```
76	LOCATE  5.48 ops    shell-explore 3.43   GRAPH 1.22   Read 0.61   test/build 0.22
77	ITERATE 2.83 ops    EDIT 2.65            test/build 0.09
78	VERIFY  1.96 ops    test/build 0.96      shell-explore 0.74   other 0.22
79	```
80	**Feasibility is not in question: 8 of 23 instances already run at ≤7.70 calls** (the −35% figure) and
81	`lucene-13170` runs at **4** — its payload contained the complete gold method including the buggy line.
82	
83	The 3.43 residual greps are both the same failure — no editable unit in the payload:
84	- **A — a wider window of the file the graph already named.** `gson`: `sed -n '170,360p' TypeAdapters.java`
85	  (which *is* the gold); `carbon`: `sed -n '480,560p' CarbonInterval.php`; also ruff, caddy, terraform,
86	  nushell, preact, phpspreadsheet.
87	- **B — a sibling-site sweep.** `hugo`: `grep -rn "render-image\|render-link\|_markup"`; `gson-2479`:
88	  `grep -n "registerTypeHierarchyAdapter\|registerTypeAdapter"`; `fmtlib`: all `format()` overloads;
89	  `redis`: `grep -n "popGenericCommand\|addReplyNull"` — precisely the callee `search_related.go:41` excludes.
90	
91	Why editability fails, by fix size — **top-k 5 is a hard ceiling**:
92	
93	| edit sites | n | fully editable | eg calls | call delta |
94	|---|---|---|---|---|
95	| ≤2 | 14 | **2/14** | 9.57 | −18.2% |
96	| 3–4 | 6 | 0/6 | 10.83 | −12.8% |
97	| ≥5 | 3 | 0/3 | 10.00 | −31.4% |
98	
99	`gson-2158` needs **9** edit sites against 5 ranked hits — unreachable by construction. L2 exists for this.
100	
101	---
102	
103	## 3. The plan
104	
105	### L1 — Guarantee the complete editable unit for the top hit ★
106	The payload already prints complete bodies when it happens to (`complete-symbol` signal), and the one
107	instance where that landed on the gold is the cheapest session in the set (`lucene`, 4 calls). Make it the
108	guarantee: for hit 1 — and hit 2 when the score gap is small — emit the **full enclosing unit**, extending
109	to unit boundaries rather than `EG_SNIPPET=6` lines. `planSearchHeadWindow` (`search_enclosure.go:242`)
110	already centres on `FocusLine`; the change is extent, not centring.
111	
112	*Priced:* 1 call = 24,400 tokens = **13.2 KB of payload** at the measured exchange rate. Payload is 4.6 KB
113	against a cap that never binds — room for ~3× before break-even.
114	
115	### L2 — Print bodies for every `EDIT` site, not 5 ranked hits ★
116	The `SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL` block **already classifies sites `EDIT` vs `CONSUMER`** (verified in the lucene
117	payload) but prints only `file:line` labels. Print the **body of each `EDIT` site** and drop `CONSUMER`
118	bodies. This is exactly what cluster-B greps reconstruct by hand, and it is the only route to the 9
119	instances with ≥3 edit sites that top-k 5 cannot cover.
120	
121	*Not the refuted change:* `--head-window-lines` + top-k **20** measured **+18.9 pt worse** — that widened
122	everything and quadrupled hits. L2 **narrows** ranked hits and spends the budget on an already-computed,
123	already-filtered EDIT set.
124	
125	### L3 — Enforce edit batching (symmetric, both arms) ★
126	2.65 EDIT calls/session, each a separate ~24,400-token API call. The prompt already says *"(7) Batch
127	independent reads and edits into one message"* and it is not being obeyed. This must be applied to **both**
128	arms to stay fair — and it still improves the ratio, because the same absolute cut is a larger share of the
129	smaller arm: cutting 1.65 edit calls from both takes −15.9% → **−18.4%**. It is what turns 75% editability
130	into −35.0% instead of −30.2%.
131	
132	### L4 — Fix the prompt's dangling references (free)
133	The eg prompt instructs the agent to use blocks the configuration never emits:
134	
135	| prompt instruction | present in payloads |
136	|---|---|
137	| (4) `CLOSED-SET WARNING` block | **0 / 23** |
138	| (8) `LOW CONFIDENCE` signal | **0 / 23** |
139	| (3) `SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL` | 17 / 23 |
140	| (5) `VERIFY` | 18 / 23 |
141	
142	`GQ_SEARCH_CAP=1` also makes instruction (8) — *"Search once more, then use the shell"* — **impossible**,
143	so a wrong top hit falls straight to the shell with no second search. Either emit the blocks or delete the
144	instructions; an instruction premised on absent output is an invitation to improvise.
145	
146	### Not levers (measured)
147	- **Shrinking the payload** — §1: ceiling ~4% of tokens; a 6 KB cap is 0.16%.
148	- **Fail-fast VERIFY** — the Sonnet mechanism. On Opus env-probes are 0.48/task eg vs 0.52 baseline.
149	- **Exploration-volume gating** — best oracle gate buys 0.34 calls/task.
150	- Refuted: top-k 20 + wide windows (+18.9 pt) · reference blocks (+14–19%) · `EG_DEF_ONLY=1` (+30.5%) ·
151	  body-slot withholding (+15.0%) · blanket VERIFY suppression (+35.1%) · raising graph usage (invariant
152	  1.07–1.83 calls/session across 8 configs) · any eg-only frugality prompt (unfair *and* costs resolves,
153	  131 vs 150, p=0.0204).
154	
155	---
156	
157	## 4. Verification and kill criteria — fixed in advance
158	
159	1. **The gate metric is editability**: share of edits whose replaced text appears verbatim in the payload
160	   (today: Opus 11.0%, all-cells 13.8%). Computable **offline and free** from payloads already on disk —
161	   no sessions needed to iterate. **No bytes/coverage/recall metric may gate anything**; seven have failed.
162	2. **L1 kill:** editability must exceed **50%**, or L1 is dead. Do not tune window sizes afterwards.
163	3. **L2 kill:** ≥3-edit-site instances must gain ≥10 points of call delta, or L2 is dead.
164	4. **L3 must be applied to both arms** and the prompt diff verified line-by-line, or the cell is void.
165	   The last eg-only frugality prompt is why the 54.9%/57.7% claims were withdrawn.
166	5. **Resolves are co-primary.** A call reduction with a resolve loss is disqualified (McNemar p<0.05).
167	   The last time calls were chased directly, resolves fell 131 vs 150 (p=0.0204).
168	6. **≥3 replicates, pooled.** Three replicates of the *same* config gave **−11.1 / −14.0 / −25.1**.
169	   A single cell printing −35% is indistinguishable from a −19.5% truth — exactly how the earlier
170	   −35.42% result was produced and later withdrawn.
171	7. **Held-out set.** rep30 has 19 mechanisms fitted against it; the editability effect was validated on
172	   3,370 sessions across 168 cells, which is the first estimate in this program not fitted to rep30.
173	
174	---
175	
176	## 5. Bugs
177	
178	1. **Prompt references two blocks never emitted** (`CLOSED-SET WARNING`, `LOW CONFIDENCE`: 0/23) and one
179	   emitted 74% of the time; `GQ_SEARCH_CAP=1` blocks the documented recovery path. (L4)
180	2. **`entire graph version` reports `dev`** — cells can pin only by sha256 and the ladder refuses `dev`.
181	   With a 14-point replicate spread, unpinnable binaries make Opus results irreproducible.
182	3. **41 of 112 graphs build DEGRADED** (DeepSWE corpus) and ship silently. Put it in the payload.
183	4. **Cross-platform packaging unguarded** — a macOS arm64 binary in linux/amd64 containers failed
184	   `rc=126`, returned an **empty payload**, and scored as if the tool were worthless.
185	5. **Unmerged search fixes on `codex/eg-graphify-advertised-bench`** (+14 commits): *"preserve hard file
186	   limits and coverage scores"*, *"keep legacy eligibility before widening"* — both touch exactly the
187	   budget/eligibility logic L1 and L2 change. **Evaluate before writing code.**
188	6. **`search_related.go:41`** excludes outgoing CALLS and the co-member fallback switches off past
189	   `searchRelatedUnitMemberLimit = 12`, so on large units neither route reaches the callee — `redis-10095`
190	   greps for precisely that callee. Fix as accuracy; gold-line coverage has partial r = **−0.131** with
191	   residual ops, so **do not price it as a token win**.
192	7. **Gold-line resolver collapsed deletion-only hunks** (lombok +0/−9 → 2 lines) — fixed.
193	
194	---
195	
196	## 6. Confidence
197	
198	**Solid.** The identity: calls R² **0.922**, context/call identical (−0.2%), 90.3% cache_read, a
199	17,722-token fixed overhead re-read every call. The op inventory. The payload-cap retraction. That 8/23
200	instances already run at ≤7.70 calls and `lucene` at 4. That top-k 5 cannot cover a 9-site fix. And the
201	mechanism itself — **n=3,370 sessions, 168 cells, stratified within cell and fix-size band, −25.1%
202	[−31.0, −18.7], consistent across four model families independently.** That last point replaces the n=2
203	estimate this document originally rested on, which was its main weakness.
204	
205	**Weak, and it is the real risk: the effect is observational, not interventional.** Editable sessions may
206	differ from non-editable ones in ways fix-size banding does not capture — task difficulty within band,
207	language, how well-posed the issue text is. 107/153 strata favour editable (70%), consistent but not
208	overwhelming. **So the −25.1% is the best available estimate of what full editability is worth, not a
209	guarantee of what building L1/L2 delivers.** The intervention can underperform the correlation, and the
210	projection table inherits that risk.
211	
212	**What I am claiming:** −35% is now a defined engineering target with a measured effect size and a
213	validated gate metric — reachable at 75% editability with L3, or 100% with L1+L2 alone, and still met at
214	the pessimistic end of the CI with both. **What I am not claiming:** that it is achieved. Nothing has been
215	built or run; editability is 11% today and every point of it has to be earned in the payload.
216

1	# entire-graph — the token lever, found by refuting two of my own theses
2	
3	**Measured 2026-08-03**, newest local build (`test/all-agent-fixes` @ `afd5a1c`, sha256 `f6a18d3ca7c2`).
4	Cell: `R30Seg` (eg) vs `R30Sbase` (baseline), Sonnet, n=30, real sessions, real transcripts.
5	Every number below was computed on this machine in this session. Refutations are reported as
6	prominently as the finding.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## 0. Bottom line
11	
12	**The token lever is not retrieval. It is the `VERIFY` block, and it is bimodal.**
13	
14	eg already saves **5.6 tool calls per task** net (14.2 vs 19.8). Of the remaining headroom, the
15	single largest identifiable leak is agents chasing a `VERIFY:` command that **cannot run in the
16	checkout** — `gson-2158` burns **24 post-edit calls to baseline's 5** doing Maven/`JAVA_HOME`
17	archaeology, while `scikit-learn-14629` shows the same block *saving* **33 calls** when the command
18	works. Same feature, ±30 calls depending on whether the toolchain exists.
19	
20	Fix: **make VERIFY fail fast instead of failing slow.** Budget-neutral, no payload growth, and it
21	explains why blanket suppression (`noworld`) measured **+35.1%** — removing the block removes the wins too.
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 1. Two theses I killed on the way here
26	
27	### 1a. "Right file, wrong region" (aim) — refuted as a token mechanism
28	eg genuinely does land on the right file and the wrong part of it: gold **FILE** found 8/8 in losers
29	and 6/6 in winners (100% both — file coverage carries **zero** signal), while gold **LINE** coverage
30	is 32.4% for losers vs 58.3% for winners, and only **25.2%** suite-wide.
31	
32	But it does not drive tokens:
33	
34	```
35	corr(coverage, eg residual ops)                = -0.107
36	corr(baseline ops, eg residual ops)            = +0.380
37	PARTIAL corr(coverage, eg ops | baseline ops)  = -0.131     (needs ~0.36 for p<0.05, n=30)
38	corr(coverage, op DELTA vs baseline)           = -0.124
39	low  coverage (<34%) n=22:  egExplore 8.0, bytes 4,625
40	high coverage (>=34%) n= 8:  egExplore 6.2, bytes 5,115     <- bytes go the WRONG way
41	```
42	
43	Coverage is the **fifth** payload metric to fail this way, after gold-file recall, fix-site
44	body-rendering, `--deep`'s coverage gain, and name-rarity IDF. **Payload metrics do not predict
45	sessions.** Retired as a gate — including the one I proposed.
46	
47	### 1b. "Gate on exploration volume" — real law, tiny lever
48	The band law is strongly confirmed: **corr(baseline explore, delta) = −0.631**. eg saves most where
49	the baseline floundered most (`scikit-learn` 28→0, `hugo-12562` 33→11) and costs where it didn't
50	(`redis-10095` 2→4, `lucene-13170` 1→2).
51	
52	But oracle gating barely pays, because the off-band instances are cheap:
53	
54	```
55	ungated            -4.43 calls/task
56	gate at baseEx>=8  -4.77   (best, +0.34 better)
57	gate at baseEx>=12 -3.97   (worse)
58	gate at baseEx>=20 -2.07   (much worse)
59	```
60

1	# entire-graph: agent-facing accuracy + token/latency — measured on `test/all-agent-fixes`
2	
3	**Type:** perf / accuracy — measured, with before/after
4	**Area:** `search` · `impact` · index cache · ranking
5	**Bottom line:** the two biggest problems (worktree-copy hits and giant generated-blob reads) are **already fixed on `origin/main`** — verified with a binary built from `test/all-agent-fixes` (= `origin/main` + 3 payload commits). **~97% fewer bytes read, worktree hits 8/10 → 0/10, `impact` un-hung.** Three smaller issues remain open (index not reused in the default mode, rank≠score, a score-0 slot), plus two measured ≥10% token levers not yet taken. This issue records the measurement so the wins don't regress and the remainder is tracked.
6	
7	### Provenance — what's already merged (checked against `origin/main` @ `1d7e3eb`)
8	The wins are **not** experimental. Three now-merged branches produced them, all ancestors of `origin/main`:
9	- `add-ignore-file-support` → `internal/sem/ignore.go` (honor `.gitignore` + `.git/info/exclude` + nested per-dir `.gitignore` + a vendored-tree heuristic + explicit `--ignore-file`/`--include-file`), plus the **4 MiB parse cap**.
10	- `fix/corpus-parse-errors` → generated-C parse failures are now classified non-fatal ("cannot affect this Go answer") instead of aborting/degrading.
11	- `feat/search-graph-ranking` → fixed *fast-profile ranking ambiguity* (but not full score-sort — see O2).
12	
13	`test/all-agent-fixes` (`afdb54e`) adds only 3 search-payload commits on top: `echo a pre-delivered payload`, `merge near same-file hits into one contiguous span`, `print the matched line (focus=)`. So everything measured below applies to plain `origin/main` too.
14	
15	---
16	
17	## Method
18	
19	Dogfooded the graph on **its own repo**, query *"how are semantic search hits ranked and scored"*, `--profile full`. Three binaries / trees:
20	
21	- **Baseline** = the previously-installed plugin binary.
22	- **Branch** = binary built from `test/all-agent-fixes` (`go build ./cmd/entire-graph`), run with its **own `--cache-dir`** (mandatory — the index cache is tree-keyed, so sharing a cache-dir between two binaries silently returns the other's index).
23	- **Polluted tree** = the working dir as an agent's `--repo .` sees it (contains `.claude/worktrees/agent-*` scratch). **Clean tree** = `git archive HEAD | tar -x` (146 tracked `.go` files, no worktrees).
24	
25	No fetch/pull/reset was performed against the live repo; the clean tree is a throwaway copy.
26	
27	---
28	
29	## Headline result — the branch fixes the big two
30	
31	Same query, same **polluted** tree, baseline binary vs branch binary:
32	
33	| metric | baseline (polluted) | **branch (polluted)** | delta |
34	|---|---|---|---|
35	| **bytes read / query** | 76.2 MB | **2.6 MB** | **−97%** |
36	| **files scanned** | 2585 | **377** | **−85%** |
37	| **search latency** | 29.9 s | **8.9 s** | **−70%** |
38	| **worktree copies in top-10** | **8 / 10** | **0 / 10** | **fixed** |
39	| **`impact`** | **> 2 min → timeout/kill** | **22.4 s (completes)** | **fixed** |

## 1. Diagnosis — when enclosure widening fires today

Two independent gates, both found by reading the path and confirmed empirically.

**Gate A — `internal/sem/search_enclosure.go:planSearchEnclosures`.** A body upgrade fires only when *all* hold: `index < bodyHeadRanks` (5); file readable/non-binary; an **enclosable callable** resolves (`searchEnclosableSymbolKind` — containers/classes/types/tables deliberately excluded); `end-start+1 <= 160`; `FocusLine` inside it; and the snippet does **not** already span it. Failing that it falls to `planSearchHeadWindow`, which is **off by default** (`HeadWindowLines` = 0) — so the result keeps the 6-line `--max-snippet-lines` window.

**Gate B — funding, `allocateSearchSnippets`.** The demotion loop runs `demoteFrom` down to `minInt(headRanks, len(results))`. At the benchmark's `--top-k 5` with `headRanks` 5, the *only* cut it can evaluate is "demote nothing", so the whole body budget is the 10 240 B growth allowance. The tail is unreachable.

**Gate C (not in the brief, but the largest single loss) — `internal/cli/search.go:writeTextSearchResult`.** `searchTextFullRanks = 2`: a primary hit at index ≥ 2 without `complete-symbol` printed **no source at all**, just `N. path:line`. On `fmtlib__fmt-2457` the allocator seated a 1 709 B window at rank 3 and the renderer discarded it.

**Why the loser payloads missed** (measured over all 30 R30PUB payloads, gold from `patch.diff`): of 12 code-gold files, 4 were never ranked, 2 were ranked with **no source at all** (gate A+C), and 6 were ranked with source of the **wrong unit in the right file**. Zero had the gold hunk verbatim. `--max-snippet-lines` never "overrides" widening; the 160-line cap and the missing container fallback do.

## 2. What changed

- `internal/sem/search_enclosure.go` — `searchEnclosure.forced/unitStart/unitEnd`; `enclosingUnitForResult` (callable → own symbol → any enclosing symbol); `planForcedSearchUnit`; `clipSearchUnitToCap`; `clipSearchUnitToBytes`; `searchFullUnitForceRanks`/`searchScoresWithinGap`; `SearchUnitElisionNote`; `forcedSearchEnclosureEnd` + `allocateForcedSearchUnits`; `widenSearchResultToEnclosure` signals; `HeadWindowSignal`/`FullUnitSignal` exports.
- `internal/sem/search.go` — `SearchOptions.FullUnitTop`/`EditSiteBodies`; `SearchResult.UnitStartLine/UnitEndLine`; wiring.
- `internal/sem/search_literals.go` — `SearchLiteralHit.Body*`; `attachSearchLiteralEditBodies`; `searchLiteralEditBody`; `searchLiteralClusterCap`; `fitSearchLiteralCluster` drops bodies before sites; `RenderSearchLiteralCluster` prints ranged EDIT headers + bodies.

## 3. Flag semantics

`--full-unit-top N` (default 0 = today's payload). Rank 1 unconditional; rank *k*>1 admitted only while `(score1-scoreK)/score1 < 0.15` (no existing gap heuristic to reuse). Unit = callable, else any enclosing symbol, else a 60-line window. Unioned with the ranked snippet so a doc comment above the declaration is never lost. 400-line safety cap → clip anchored at unit start (slides to keep the hit inside), `…elided lines X–Y (unit continues)` after the body, `unit-elided` signal, no `complete-symbol`. Funding: forced units first, then tail→locators, then (last) forced ranks revert deepest-first so `--max-context-bytes` is exact.

`--edit-site-bodies` (bool, default off). EDIT-role sites only; enclosing unit else ±12 lines; 60 lines and 3 kB per site, 8 sites; block cap 560 B → 12 kB while bodies present. Header `path:START-END symbol EDIT`, body verbatim with **no** line-number prefixes.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Deterministic parallel launcher.
# Replaces `xargs -P N -I{}`, which on macOS mangles the job list: the first pair
# runs correctly, then xargs resumes mid-line and hands workers a bare instance id
# (rep/arm empty). Jobs are read on fd 3 so nothing downstream can touch fd 0.
set -u
worker="$1"; jobs_file="$2"; par="${3:-10}"; log="${4:-/dev/stdout}"

while IFS= read -r line <&3; do
  [ -z "$line" ] && continue
  while [ "$(jobs -rp | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" -ge "$par" ]; do sleep 3; done
  bash "$worker" "$line" </dev/null >>"$log" 2>&1 &
done 3< "$jobs_file"
wait
echo "ALLDONE $(basename "$jobs_file")" >> "$log"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Live TUI for the O35S loser screen: per-instance session state + token savings.

Run in its own terminal:   python3 tools/o35s_watch.py          (refreshes every 5s)
One-shot snapshot:         python3 tools/o35s_watch.py --once

Savings are computed against the STORED arms (baseline reuse doctrine):
  sv%  = new eg tokens vs stored BASELINE arm  (the number the goal ladder cares about)
  dEG% = new eg tokens vs stored (pre-fix) EG arm (did the fixes beat the old tool)
"""
import json, math, os, sys, time

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
RES = os.path.join(ROOT, "results")
BATCHES = [
    ("handoff-config/o35s_losers_pub.txt", "PUB_r1"),
    ("handoff-config/o35s_losers_r30.txt", "R30PUB_r1"),
]
NEW_CELL = "O35S_r1_eg"

def toks(cc):
    try:
        j = json.load(open(cc))
    except Exception:
        return None, None
    u = j.get("usage") or {}
    t = sum(u.get(k, 0) for k in ("input_tokens", "cache_read_input_tokens",
                                  "cache_creation_input_tokens", "output_tokens"))
    return (t or None), j.get("total_cost_usd")

def load_jobs():
    rows = []
    for jf, cell in BATCHES:
        p = os.path.join(ROOT, jf)
        if not os.path.exists(p):
            continue
        for line in open(p):
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            iid = line.split("|")[2]
            rows.append((iid, cell))
    return rows

C = {"g": "\x1b[32m", "r": "\x1b[31m", "y": "\x1b[33m", "c": "\x1b[36m",
     "d": "\x1b[2m", "b": "\x1b[1m", "x": "\x1b[0m"}

def bar(pct, width=14):
    # pct: savings percent, positive = good. clamp [-100, 100]
    if pct is None:
        return " " * width
    p = max(-100.0, min(100.0, pct))
    half = width // 2
    n = int(abs(p) / 100 * half + 0.5)
    if p >= 0:
        return C["d"] + "." * (half - 0) + C["x"] + C["g"] + "#" * n + C["x"] + " " * (half - n)
    return C["d"] + "." * (half - n) + C["x"] + C["r"] + "#" * n + C["x"] + " " * half

def fmt_pct(v, invert=False):
    if v is None:
        return "      "
    col = C["g"] if v > 0 else (C["r"] if v < 0 else C["y"])
    return f"{col}{v:+6.1f}{C['x']}"

def render(start):
    rows = load_jobs()
    done = run = pend = 0
    lines = []
    ratios_base, ratios_eg, wins = [], [], 0
    tot_new = tot_base_f = 0
    for iid, cell in rows:
        newd = os.path.join(RES, NEW_CELL, "eg", iid)
        cc = os.path.join(newd, "cc_out.json")
        base_cc = os.path.join(RES, f"{cell}_baseline", "baseline", iid, "cc_out.json")
        oldeg_cc = os.path.join(RES, f"{cell}_eg", "eg", iid, "cc_out.json")
        bt, _ = toks(base_cc)
        ot, _ = toks(oldeg_cc)
        short = iid.split("__")[-1]
        cellt = "20 " if cell == "PUB_r1" else "r30"
        if os.path.exists(cc):
            nt, cost = toks(cc)
            if nt:
                done += 1
                sv = (1 - nt / bt) * 100 if bt else None
                de = (1 - nt / ot) * 100 if ot else None
                if bt: ratios_base.append(nt / bt); tot_new += nt; tot_base_f += bt
                if ot: ratios_eg.append(nt / ot)
                if sv is not None and sv > 0: wins += 1
                st = C["g"] + "DONE " + C["x"]
                lines.append(f" {st} {cellt} {short:<24s} {nt/1e6:6.2f}M  sv {fmt_pct(sv)}%  dEG {fmt_pct(de)}%  {bar(sv)}  ${cost or 0:5.2f}")
            else:
                done += 1
                lines.append(f" {C['r']}FAIL {C['x']} {cellt} {short:<24s}   cc_out unreadable/zero")
        elif os.path.isdir(newd):
            run += 1
            age = int(time.time() - os.path.getmtime(newd))
            lines.append(f" {C['y']}RUN  {C['x']} {cellt} {short:<24s}   {C['d']}started, {age//60}m{age%60:02d}s elapsed{C['x']}")
        else:
            pend += 1
            lines.append(f" {C['d']}WAIT {C['x']} {cellt} {short:<24s}")
    out = ["\x1b[2J\x1b[H" + C["b"] + " O35S loser screen — live" + C["x"]
           + C["d"] + f"   {time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}  elapsed {int(time.time()-start)//60}m"
           + f"   done {done}/{len(rows)}  running {run}  pending {pend}" + C["x"], ""]
    out += lines
    out.append("")
    if ratios_base:
        geo_b = (math.exp(sum(math.log(r) for r in ratios_base) / len(ratios_base)) - 1) * -100
        agg = (1 - tot_new / tot_base_f) * 100 if tot_base_f else 0
        s = f" {C['b']}vs BASELINE{C['x']}  geomean {fmt_pct(geo_b)}%   aggregate {fmt_pct(agg)}%   winners {wins}/{len(ratios_base)}"
        if ratios_eg:
            geo_e = (math.exp(sum(math.log(r) for r in ratios_eg) / len(ratios_eg)) - 1) * -100
            s += f"    {C['b']}vs OLD EG{C['x']}  geomean {fmt_pct(geo_e)}%"
        out.append(s)
        out.append(C["d"] + "  goal: rung1 -25% (20-set) -> rung2 -35% (rep30); losers-only sample, directional" + C["x"])
    else:
        out.append(C["d"] + " no finished sessions yet — savings appear as each lands" + C["x"])
    print("\n".join(out), flush=True)

def main():
    start = time.time()
    if "--once" in sys.argv:
        render(start); return
    while True:
        try:
            render(start); time.sleep(5)
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            return

main()

Base directory for this skill: /Users/suhaan/.claude/skills/graph-bench-forensics

# Graph benchmark forensics

Measure a context tool honestly, at the level of individual sessions and individual token classes.
This drill exists because aggregates on this benchmark are routinely wrong in *both* directions, and
every headline that was ever withdrawn was withdrawn for a reason this checklist catches.

## The cost model — get this right first, everything else follows

**Cost is not "tokens".** Solve for per-token prices from recorded `total_cost_usd` (least squares
over cache_read / cache_creation / output, n≈30) rather than assuming. Measured on rep30:

| model | $/Mtok cache_read | cache_creation | output | **cost share** cr / cc / out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fable 5 | 1.00 | 20.31 | 49.63 | 22% / 39% / 39% |
| Opus 5 | 0.50 | 10.19 | 24.73 | 26% / 38% / 36% |
| Sonnet | 0.29 | 6.33 | 14.78 | 41% / 31% / 28% |
| Haiku | 0.10 | 2.09 | 4.96 | 46% / 28% / 25% |

Two traps, both of which produced wrong conclusions:

- **"95% of tokens are cache_read" is a token COUNT, not a cost share.** Output is priced 20–50×
  higher, so it is 25–39% of the bill. A tool that cuts reading and raises writing LOSES money.
  Fable is the clean case: turns fell 10% and cost rose 15%, because output rose 14.7%.
- **Cost ≈ MESSAGES × context.** At a large context a message costs ~446k cache-read tokens. Count
  messages, not tool calls. (Note: parallel tool calls were not reachable in this harness — 0 of
  10,374 messages carried more than one — so "batch your calls" is un-actionable advice, and any
  prompt rule telling an agent to batch is dead weight given to both arms.)

Always report cache_read / cache_creation / output **separately**. The aggregate usd hides which
one moved, and which one moved is the finding.

## The noise floor — respect it or you will publish noise

- Same-instance spread across repeated cells: **45pt median**, tail to 335pt. One instance measured
  +404% / +97% / +69% across three configs.
- Every single-cell CI on this benchmark spans zero for the weaker models. **MDE ≈ CI width ≈ 31%
  at n=30**, so only effects ≥ ~30pt are detectable in one cell.
- **0/30 instances produce the same agent query twice** (median token overlap 0.55). Retrieval
  itself varies run to run, so any replay that fixes the query measures one sample of the input.

Rules that follow:
1. **Never score a partial cell.** A Sonnet geomean moved 47 points between n=9 and n=25.
2. **Never bucket one cell into sub-groups of 3–7 and read the differences.** That is how the
   "VERIFY-off is a −12pt lever" and "payload width costs 10.6pt" claims were produced, and both
   were retracted.
3. **Compare configs with replicates of the SAME config**, not two different configs' point
   estimates. Pooling different configs estimates "expected value across configs tried".
4. **Report bootstrap CIs, never a bare point estimate.**
5. Trust **deterministic offline replays** (re-issuing recorded queries against the binary) far
   more than single-session attributions.

## The measurement gate

A session counts only if `total_cost_usd > 0` **AND** `patch.diff` is non-empty. Drop pairs
**symmetrically** — if either arm gate-fails on an instance, the instance leaves both arms.
Otherwise a cheap gate-failure reads as a saving.

Also check before trusting any per-instance delta: `result` length, `num_turns`, and `subtype`
(`error_max_turns` sessions are right-censored, so their true cost is ≥ recorded).

## Fairness — the failure mode that has invalidated the most results

Every withdrawn headline on this benchmark came from **asymmetric prompts**, not from the tool.

- Diff the two arms' `prompt.txt` and account for **every** differing line. A "−35%" result once
  came from two extra instructions the tool arm had and the baseline did not (*"never write a
  throwaway test script"*, *"no `which`, no `ls vendor/`, no `find / -name php*`"*). Removing them
  moved the same cell from −14.9% to +9.1%.
- Frugality clamps belong in the **shared** block or nowhere.
- A tool-side default change (ranking, payload content, a flag) is legitimate. Extra *instructions*
  to one arm are not.
- Distinguish "tool as shipped, including its recommended prompt" from "the tool's marginal value
  under one contract". Both are real questions; say which you measured.

## The drill

### 1. Verify the data before analysing it
- Confirm inputs exist: repo clones, graphs, and **`patch.diff` for every gated session**.
- Check for silent loss: a driver that skips on the session log alone will skip forever a session
  whose patch vanished. On this suite a `/private/tmp` reap destroyed 4 patches, 27 graphs and
  every packfile — and the lost instances were ones the tool won by 20+ turns, biasing *against* it.
- Keep the suite off volatile paths.

### 2. Score the cell
Per-instance paired table: usd, turns, cache_read/cache_creation/output, gate status. Then geomean
+ bootstrap CI. Then per-language, then per-instance sorted by contribution to the shortfall.

### 3. Decompose the transcripts — this is where the answers are
For each session (`~/.claude/projects/*/<session_id>.jsonl`, keyed off `cc_out.json:session_id`):

- **Phase split at the first Edit/Write.** Post-edit is typically ~65% of output and is where every
  losing instance's delta lives.
- **Per-tool token attribution.** Dedupe by `message.id`, credit each message's `output_tokens` to
  its tool. This tells you whether the delta is Edit bodies, Bash commands, or prose.
- **Count**: Edit/Write calls, distinct files touched, throwaway/repro scripts, prose length.
- **Classify every grep/find/read** the tool arm still ran (see below).

### 4. The single strongest predictor found: grep elimination
Compute `eg_greps / baseline_greps` per instance.

| greps eliminated | Haiku | Sonnet |
|---|---|---|
| >75% | **−46.1%** | — |
| 40–75% | −39.6% | −17.3% |
| <40% | +1.9% | +31.8% |

corr(grep ratio, log usd) = **+0.615 Haiku / +0.712 Sonnet**, while corr(**baseline** greps,
outcome) ≈ 0 — so it is not task difficulty leaking through. **This is the metric to optimise.**

Then classify the *residual* greps to decide what to fix:

| what the grep was for | share | fix |
|---|---|---|
| finding something NEW | 38% | recall / ranking |
| searching inside a file the payload returned | 29% | payload under-delivery |
| re-finding a symbol the payload already gave | 25% | payload under-delivery |
| env / build hunting | 8% | verify-command quality |

### 5. Falsify offline before spending a cell
Recorded queries live at `results/<tag>/eg/<instance>/gq_calls.log`, emitted payloads at the same
path + `.payload`, worktrees at `replay-wt/<instance>`. Replay against the binary at **zero model
cost** and assert the change does what you claim — *and* that nothing else moved.

Replay across **every** recorded query variant, not one, because the agent rephrases every run.

### 6. Only then run a cell, and pre-register
Write the prediction and its falsification bounds to a file **before** the run. An out-of-sample
prediction that survives is worth more than ten post-hoc explanations. (Worked: Opus predicted
−0.1% from band effects fitted on cells excluding it; measured −0.5%, n=30.)

## Known results — do not re-derive these

- **≥35% is refuted, not unproven.** The favourable CI bound on total tokens is −27.8%
  (`eg-consolidated/AGENTS.md`). Independent rep30 measurement: Haiku −24.1% CI [−36.6, −8.3].
- Four models, rep30, paired: Fable +14.9%, Opus −0.5%, Sonnet +9.4%, Haiku −24.1%. **The tool
  saves on one of four.**
- Savings depend on how much the *no-tool* arm explores: pooled n=175, corr −0.238
  [−0.346, −0.134]; costs money under ~12 baseline turns, peaks ≈ −30% at 20–49, tapers above.
  **It does not explain Sonnet** (predicted −14.5%, measured +9.4% — a 24pt miss).
- Raising the turn cap does **not** help — both arms grow proportionally (−24.1% → −21.3%).
- Prefetching the search from the issue text is **dominated**: gold-visible@5 0.567 vs 0.715 for the
  agent's own distilled query, 8 losses to 0 wins. The invocation turn is irreducible.

Round 4, three tool-side fixes from session forensics (wt-l1l2, same branch, on top of f5c2080):

FIX 1 — elision contract (correctness bug, measured on carbon-2752): the payload ranked Comparison.php #1 tagged full-unit/complete-symbol but the printed body ELIDED lines 630-1125 while the focus/edit region is at 989 — the tag lied. Rule: a hit may carry full-unit/complete-symbol signals ONLY if its printed body includes the focus line; when the unit exceeds its clip budget, re-center the window on the focus line (±60) instead of anchoring at unit start, and drop the complete-body signal. Add a test reproducing the carbon shape (huge unit, focus deep inside).

FIX 2 — degenerate impact output: when an impact anchor resolves with 0 callers AND 0 callees AND 0 type-consumers, or when every hit path matches build/dist/vendor bundle patterns, emit a single machine-readable line (e.g. "IMPACT DEGENERATE: <reason>") instead of the full empty scaffolding. The harness will use this marker to drop the impact payload and force a lean prefetch.

(Post-edit verify churn measured +$4.11 across 3 sessions — gson hand-built javac/JUnit classpaths = 55.6% of its output tokens.) but it erased the baseline’s environment-flail, which the per-instance decomposition proved was where most of the tool’s savings had been coming from (7 of 10 flips = baseline cost dropping 50–77% on the same instance, our arm barely moving) - explain this

Here's the mechanism, walked through with a real instance:

**What "environment-flail" is.** Every benchmark task drops the agent into a bare repo checkout — dependencies not installed, `node_modules/` and `vendor/` missing, test runners broken. When an agent (either arm) tries to verify its fix, the first attempt fails not because the fix is wrong but because the *environment* is unbuilt. A no-tool baseline then typically burns 10–30 turns figuring this out by trial and error: run test → "command not found" → try `npm install` → wrong node version → hand-build a classpath → retry → etc. Each of those turns costs ~25K tokens.

**Where the tool's savings actually came from.** Take **immutable-js** in yesterday's cell: the baseline spent **6.16M tokens**, a huge share of it on exactly that dependency-and-test-setup thrash, while the eg arm spent 1.93M — a 69% saving. But notice what the saving *is*: it isn't "the tool found the code faster" (locate deltas measured ≈ zero all night). It's that the baseline drowned in setup and the tool arm happened to drown less. The tool looked good largely because its opponent kept tripping over the environment.

**What round 6 did.** To fix a genuine bug (my VERIFY validator testing commands in a fake environment), I added a step that runs `npm ci` / `bundle install` / etc. in the checkout *before either arm starts* — same treatment for both, so it's fair. But that step **removed the tripwire**. Yesterday's baseline on immutable-js: 6.16M (thrashing). Today's baseline, walking into a pre-built environment: **1.44M** — it just fixed the bug and ran the working tests. Our arm barely changed (1.93M → 1.52M). The instance flipped from a 69% win to a small loss **without our tool getting any worse** — the denominator of the comparison collapsed.

That's what the 7-of-10 pattern means: on seven flipped instances, the baseline's cost dropped 50–77% while ours moved single digits. We didn't regress; we accidentally coached our opponent by professionalizing the arena.

**The implication both ways.** In pre-built environments, the tool's honest value is small (≈0–10%) — code search alone doesn't save Opus much. In realistic bare environments — which is the benchmark's actual design, and where all your targets were calibrated — the tool's environment knowledge (a *validated, working* verify recipe) is real, large value. Attempt 3 restores that arena and makes the knowledge explicit in the payload instead of implicit in luck: sessions start pristine for both arms, and the tool says "run `bundle install` first, then this exact test — we verified it works." The baseline still has to discover that with its own turns.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about benchmark agent environment setup and the related systems you asked about:

## Overview of Environment Setup Benchmarks

Repository setup remains a bottleneck due to version drift and dependencies that span Python packages, system libraries, GPU drivers, etc.

## SetupBench and EnvBench

EnvBench evaluates automated environment setup across Python and JVM repositories, and SetupBench evaluates environment bootstrapping from Linux sandboxes with deterministic success commands.

Current state-of-the-art approaches achieve success rates of 6.69% for Python and 29.47% for JVM repositories, demonstrating that EnvBench presents significant challenges for existing methods.

## Criticisms of Existing Benchmarks

There are several documented limitations:

- Existing benchmarks fail to capture runtime complexity. For instance, EnvBench evaluates setup success primarily through static analysis (checking for missing imports), a metric that cannot detect runtime failures caused by binary incompatibilities or hardware mismatches.

- EnvBench and similar benchmarks do not evaluate configuration for specific repository issues nor effectively test the agent's ability to generate corresponding test scripts.

## Additional Approaches

ResearchEnvBench provides a compound toolset that combines shell execution with precise file editing, unlike prior environment-focused benchmarks that restrict agents to static setup scripts such as Installamatic or shell-only interaction such as SetupBench.

content.text:
Two honest answers:

**1. Would native callable tools save tokens?** Two channels say plausibly yes, one caution says prove it:
- **Mechanical**: the prompt-injected payload is a 4–14KB tax billed *on every message* of the session whether used or not (we measured it as a pure context floor). A native tool's result arrives once, only when requested — the guaranteed tax disappears.
- **Behavioral**: information a model *requested* gets used; information injected at it gets skimmed — that's the psychological difference behind [SWE-agent's 3–4× interface finding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15793), and it's what our probe tests.
- **The caution**: the prior art (AutoCodeRover, LocAgent) measured **resolve-rate** gains, not token savings — nobody out there has published token savings from native graph tools. Our probe would be a genuinely novel measurement, which is also why I won't promise the number before it exists.

**2. Did anyone benchmark in broken environments like our old arena?** Yes — but as **its own benchmark category, not as an arena for measuring code-search tools**: [EnvBench](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2503.14443) (state of the art: 6.7% success on Python setup!), SetupBench, [DeployBench](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.05238), [Terminal-Bench](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.11868v1), [Multi-Docker-Eval](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.06915) all treat environment bootstrapping as *the task itself*, precisely because it's hard and realistic. Which gives our old numbers their honest frame: the bare-checkout arena accidentally measured a **hybrid workload** — part issue-resolution, part environment-setup — and the tool's big savings came mostly from the setup half. That's not a fake result; it's a *real and common* workload (most real repos aren't pre-provisioned!). It's just a different claim than "saves tokens on official SWE-bench."

Here's the full picture, three parts:

**1. Per-repo locate-phase breakdown (RUNG2B, tokens to first edit + greps pre/post-edit)** — table above. Totals: **baseline locate = 40.0M, eg locate = 46.6M; greps 98 vs 100.** The eg wins are exactly the validated-VERIFY conversions (carbon 0.78M vs baseline's 3.70M, fmt-2457 0.47 vs 2.60, hugo-12562 0.75 vs 3.16, caddy 0.40 vs 1.16); the losses are payload-floor plus bad draws (lombok 5.48 vs 0.89, terraform 3.31 vs 0.87).

**2. "Doesn't the graph replace the greps?" — no, and the transcripts show why it structurally can't, in four measured facts:**
- **73% of eg's greps hunt things no payload contains**: multi-site sweeps ("every caller of X across 3 dirs"), changelogs, build files, version strings. Grep covers *all text in the repo*; the payload covers 3–5 ranked code locations. Different question spaces.
- **Most sessions have no locate question at all** (8/12: the issue text names the file before turn 1) — the greps there are habit/confirmation, not search. You can't replace a grep that isn't looking for anything.
- **Where the payload did contain the answer, re-finding was 2.9% of greps** — the replaceable slice was already tiny.
- **Greps chain** (`grep A; grep B; grep C` in one call under the batching rule) and cost one message regardless — they're the cheapest habit in the toolbox, and even Opus's *native* Grep tool loses to Bash for the same reason.

That's why every payload enrichment in this program's history raised greps instead of cutting them, and why the winning fixes were never "replace grep" but "make the verify path true."

**3. Rung 1's exact config** (worker `rung1worker.sh`, tag RUNG1): published prompt verbatim + symmetric batching block · binary `eg-f5c2080` (budget-driven allocator, refusal answers, graph-correctness — pre-round-6) · lean payload (`EG_TOPK=5, MAXBYTES=24576, SNIPPET=6, MAX_PER_FILE=3, PROFILE=full`, no full-unit/edit-bodies/callee-hop) · prefetch + impact prefetch · query v2+v3 · **execute-validated VERIFY** · `GQ_SEARCH_CAP=2` · full netjail + per-instance cache isolation · Opus/high, 120 turns, 3600s · **bare environment** (no session provisioning — that arrived in round 6). That last property is likely load-bearing: rung 1's +30.6% was earned where baselines still paid the environment tax that attempt 3 (running now, 4/24 baselines done) restores.

  name: 'minimal-payload-forensics',
  description: 'Read completed RUNG2E eg sessions under the 616-byte VERIFY-only payload: did behavior change vs the blob world?',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Read', detail: 'one agent per completed session' },

  ],
}

const SESSIONS = [
  'briannesbitt__carbon-3098','django__django-13821','faker-ruby__faker-2970',
  'phpoffice__phpspreadsheet-4214','laravel__framework-48636','facebook__docusaurus-9183',

]

  type: 'object', additionalProperties: false,
  properties: {
    instance: { type: 'string' },
    verify_line: { type: 'string', description: 'the VERIFY line the 616-byte block carried (verbatim) + its validation annotation' },

    tool_calls: { type: 'integer', description: 'live eg-q invocations (gq_calls.log lines)' },
    greps: { type: 'integer', description: 'grep-ish shell + Grep/Glob calls' },
    messages: { type: 'integer', description: 'unique assistant message ids' },
    tokens: { type: 'integer' },
    locator_used: { type: 'string', description: 'did the agent go to the single locator line the block named? quote its first action' },
    behavior_vs_blob: { type: 'string', description: 'compare to this instance RUNG2D eg session (blob world): what changed in behavior, 2-3 sentences with numbers' },
    residual_waste: { type: 'string', description: 'the biggest remaining token sink in THIS session and what tool/harness capability would remove it' },
  },
  required: ['instance','verify_line','verify_obeyed','tool_calls','greps','messages','tokens','locator_used','behavior_vs_blob','residual_waste'],
}

Read ONE completed benchmark session that ran with a NEW minimal payload design, and compare it to the same instance's previous session under the old design. Read-only.

  /Users/suhaan/graphmark-bench/agentic-swebench/results/RUNG2E_r1_eg/eg/${iid}/

Finally: name the single biggest remaining token sink in the NEW session and the specific tool-or-harness capability that would remove it (no prompt coaching).

instance="${iid}". Structured output only.
`, { label: `mp:${iid.split('__')[1]}`, phase: 'Read', schema: SCHEMA, model: 'opus' })))

const ok = rows.filter(Boolean)
log(`${ok.length}/8 read`)

phase('Synthesize')
const synth = await agent(`
Synthesis: a code-search tool's payload was cut from ~8KB of ranked hits to a 616-byte block (one locator + a validated VERIFY command + capability text). 8 completed sessions read, each compared to the same instance's session under the old 8KB design:

${JSON.stringify(ok)}

`, { label: 'synthesis', phase: 'Synthesize', model: 'opus', effort: 'high' })

Meanwhile environment/toolchain repair is ~31% of all session tokens — the biggest sink in the corpus — and a tool that hands over a WORKING command plus the install recipe is legitimate capability the baseline has no way to obtain. Fixes:

F1 — VALIDATOR MUST ACTUALLY RUN THINGS:
 (a) Allowlist project-local runners by PATH SHAPE, not just basename: any executable under the checkout (vendor/bin/*, node_modules/.bin/*, bin/*, ./gradlew, ./mvnw, .venv/bin/*, target/debug/*) is allowed — it's inside the repo we already trust; keep the deny for network fetchers.
 (b) Per-ecosystem timeouts instead of a flat 180s: compiled languages (cargo/cmake/mvn/gradle/go build) get 900s, interpreted (pytest/jest/phpunit/rspec/rake) 300s. Log the elapsed time either way.
 (c) Interpreter resolution: if the first token isn't found (127), retry once with the same command via `bash -lc` so login-shell PATH (pyenv/nvm/rbenv shims) resolves, and record which resolution worked.
 (d) When provisioning itself failed (npm install exit != 0, composer exit 2, bundler missing gem), record the failure AND still attempt validation — a partially provisioned tree often runs a narrower command (e.g. `php -l`, `cargo check`).
 (e) Report in gate.log: attempted commands, each one's exit + elapsed + resolution path. This is the metric that tells us whether the capability fired.

F2 — SHIP THE RECIPE, NOT JUST THE COMMAND: when validation succeeded only after provisioning, the payload line becomes two lines: "SETUP (validated, took Ns): <install cmd>" then "VERIFY (validated: runs, fails pre-fix): <cmd>". When provisioning failed but a narrower check validated, ship that with its label. This is the 31%-sink attack: the eg arm gets the working recipe, the baseline discovers it by flailing as it always has.

F3 — INTEGRITY, MANDATORY: netjail does not block `gh`. The ruff session ran `gh pr diff` and reproduced the upstream patch wording — that voids the cell. Add `gh` to netjail/_blocked (same pattern as curl/wget) and grep every surviving transcript under ~/.claude/projects for `gh pr|gh api|gh repo` to report how many past sessions used it (integrity ledger — I need the count).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Deterministic parallel launcher.
# Replaces `xargs -P N -I{}`, which on macOS mangles the job list: the first pair
# runs correctly, then xargs resumes mid-line and hands workers a bare instance id
# (rep/arm empty). Jobs are read on fd 3 so nothing downstream can touch fd 0.
set -u
worker="$1"; jobs_file="$2"; par="${3:-10}"; log="${4:-/dev/stdout}"

while IFS= read -r line <&3; do
  [ -z "$line" ] && continue
  while [ "$(jobs -rp | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" -ge "$par" ]; do sleep 3; done
  bash "$worker" "$line" </dev/null >>"$log" 2>&1 &
done 3< "$jobs_file"
wait
echo "ALLDONE $(basename "$jobs_file")" >> "$log"

# Pre-registration — RUNG2J (rep30 attempt 10), written before any session finished

Date: 2026-08-04. Prior cell: **RUNG2I, n=30, saving 29.7% tokens, CI [saving 39.2, saving 18.1],
winners 24/30**, integrity clean (0 censored, 0 gate-fails, 0 empty patches, prompt diff = pure
9-line payload insertion, no frugality text in either arm).

## What changed (both arms; nothing arm-specific)

1. **`verify.run` no longer wipes the graded worktree.** It ended with an unconditional
   `git checkout -- . ; git clean -fd` on the tree the agent is graded on, so calling the
   verification command reverted the agent's own edit and deleted its repro files. Now only what
   the *run* dirtied is restored (snapshot before, diff after).
2. **`validated-fails` requires proof a test actually ran.** It was the fall-through for any
   nonzero exit; 17 of 22 certified commands across RUNG2G/H/I had no parsed test summary
   (`parser=exit-code-only`) and still shipped the anti-harness clamp.

## Measured inputs (not estimates)

- Wrapper invocations, RUNG2I eg: 8 of 30 sessions. Re-work signature (an Edit repeating a
  `(file_path, new_string[:400])` pair already edited before the first `verify.run`) fires in
  **5 of those 8**; tail from first re-edit to end = **3.52M tokens**. fmt-2457 forensics
  attributed 583K of its own 1.66M tail to pure re-do → discount factor 0.35.
- False clamps in RUNG2I: 5 (lucene, gson-2158, gson-2479, phpspreadsheet, bat). Two of the five
  are large winners today (saving 51.5% and 54.7%), so the strict gate is **not** a guaranteed
  token gain.
- Cohort geomeans, RUNG2I complete board: `verify+clamp` n=8 saving 14.8% · `f5` n=11 saving
  24.7% · `suppressed-noncovering` n=11 saving 42.9%.

## Predictions

| scenario | modelled cell |
|---|---|
| wipe fix only, fmt-calibrated 0.35 | saving 30.9% |
| wipe fix, full-tail (optimistic) | saving 33.9% |
| + strict gate, losing false-clamps only → f5 mean | saving 32.3% |
| + strict gate, all 5 → f5 mean | saving 30.2% |
| both fixes, best case | **saving 32.8%** |

**Central prediction: saving 30–33%. The 35% bar is predicted NOT to be met by these two levers.**

## Falsification

- Landing inside 30–33% confirms the model and establishes that these two levers do not reach 35%.
- Landing **below 29.7%** falsifies the strict gate as a token lever. It stays in regardless: a
  frugality clamp handed to one arm on a fabricated premise is the defect class that invalidated
  the withdrawn 54.9% headline, so it is a correctness requirement, not an optimisation.
- Landing **above 33.9%** means an unmodelled mechanism is present and must be identified before
  the number is quoted anywhere.

## Integrity gates applied before any number is reported

Both arms fresh at the same harness revision (never pair a fresh arm against an older baseline);
symmetric pair dropping; CENSORED and empty-`patch.diff` counts reported per arm; `cc_out.json`
cross-checked against transcripts (it has been corrupt before — redis-10095 reported `num_turns=1`
against a 54-message transcript); full prompt diff accounted for line by line.

## Attempt 9 (RUNG2I) — final, gate 2 candidate

| metric | result |
|---|---|
| **tokens** | **saving 29.7%** — CI [saving 39.2, saving 18.1] |
| usd | saving 22.6% |

**Gate 2 is not met — 29.7% against the 35% bar.** It is by far the best rep30 result of the campaign (previous best: saving 12.7%), and it is clean.

## Two real defects found, both fixed

The forensics on the four losers found something better than a tuning knob — a bug that was **penalising the tool arm**, not favouring it.

**1. `verify.run` was deleting the agent's work.** The agent-facing wrapper ended with `git checkout -- . ; git clean -fd` **on the graded worktree**. Calling the verification command reverted the agent's own edit and deleted its repro files. fmt-2457's agent, verbatim: *"The verify script reverted my working-tree edit (tree is now clean). Let me reapply the fix."* Measured, not asserted: 8 of 30 eg sessions invoked the wrapper, **5 of those 8** carry the re-work signature, 3.52M tokens of tail. It also blanked 3 eg patches in attempt 8. Fixed to restore only what the *run* dirtied — falsified at $0: agent edit survives, scratch survives, test-dirtied file reverted, build artifact removed; the old wrapper fails the first two.

**2. `validated-fails` was certifying commands that never ran a test.** It was the fall-through for *any* nonzero exit. Census: **22 certified commands, only 5 had a parsed test summary.** bat exits 101 in 0.1s, lucene's gradle test in 1.2s, gson's maven on the wrong JDK. Same-instance movement between the two cells has a **median of 33.9 points** (max 107 — rubocop went from saving 62.4% to costing 43.9%). One real signal did survive: **Java went from roughly break-even to costing 69.5%** once the false clamps were removed. Those clamps were suppressing harness improvisation on a premise that was untrue. That is the uncomfortable finding of the day — the fabricated certification was *earning* tokens, and removing it costs measured savings. #       BUILD FAILURE; on JDK 17 = "Tests run: 10, Failures: 0" BUILD SUCCESS. Conversely
#       lucene REFUSES to build on 17 ("ERROR: java version must be 21") and succeeds on 21
#       ("BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 17s"). There is no single correct JDK -- it is per-instance.
#
#   (2) EMPTY MAVEN REPO. MAVEN_ARGS pins maven.repo.local at the per-instance $PKG_ISO/m2 for
#       isolation, but that starts EMPTY while a warm ~/.m2/repository (519MB) sits unused, and
#       netjail blocks all egress. Measured on JDK 17 with an empty repo: "Cannot access central
#       in offline mode and the artifact kr.motd.maven:os-maven-plugin:jar:1.7.1 has not been
#       downloaded from it before." So no Java build could resolve a single dependency.
#       Fixed by APFS-cloning the warm repo into the isolated one (`cp -c`: 519MB in ~1s, and
#       clones share blocks so it costs almost no disk). Isolation is preserved -- each instance
#       still WRITES to its own copy. This mirrors the pattern GEM_PATH already uses above:
#       isolated write dir, warm read path.
if [ -f "$wt/pom.xml" ] || [ -f "$wt/gradlew" ] || [ -f "$wt/build.gradle" ]; then
  if [ -d "$HOME/.m2/repository" ] && [ ! -d "$PKG_ISO/m2/org" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$PKG_ISO/m2" 2>/dev/null
    cp -c -R "$HOME/.m2/repository/." "$PKG_ISO/m2/" 2>/dev/null \

  # first that the project itself accepts. The probe is the project's own build tool, so the
