# Make the graph actually eliminate the locate phase — route to ≥25% on a fresh language-balanced 30

> **Revision note.** An independent design review overturned four numbers in the first version of this
> plan (replicate allocation, achievable CI, the claim bar, and the Python pool) and found a live
> fairness violation. Corrections are marked **[CORRECTED]**. Trust this version.

## Context

Goal: ≥25% token saving vs a no-tool baseline on Opus, measured fairly. Current fair measurement is
the opposite — **eg COSTS 28–38%**. The user's thesis (the graph should obliterate the locate phase,
so it should never cost) is right in principle and is *not* what the tool does. Causes found, none of
them payload quality (eight payload metrics are dead; do not re-bet):

**Cause 1 — the tool is not legible as a command, so it is never invoked.**
`published_exact_eg_tool()` (`tools/run_3arm.sh:1240`) emits one unfenced 96-char path glued onto
prose; `callers`/`grep`/`search` appear bare mid-paragraph; **`impact` is never named**. Deliberate —
*"No usage coaching, no 'search first'"* — but it removed the **syntax** with the coaching. Measured
over every cell ever run: **0.042 real graph queries/session; 2.8% of sessions ever query; 8 of 610
`gq_calls.log` non-empty; 2 of 14 logged calls are the agent running the bare path to discover argv.**
The one successful querier (`R2IREPRO/facebook__docusaurus-9183`, T16–17) had to `cd` and use
`./eg-q.run` instead of the prompt's path, after 15 turns of grep — then got complete verbatim bodies.
The tool works; it is undiscoverable.

**Cause 2 — the payload is trusted as a pointer, distrusted as content.** **88% of eg sessions re-read
a payload file from disk at turn 1–2** even when the complete body was inlined. Earned: `VERIFY: none
validated` in 27/33 prompts, `Completeness: degraded` 6/12, and in 2/19 an actual refusal notice
inside `<graph_search_result>`: `SEARCH BUDGET EXHAUSTED … Search will not run again.`

**Cause 3 [NEW] — a live fairness violation: `O35_QUERY_V3` leaks the gold path.** It parses the file
path out of the issue's GitHub permalink and **leads the eg search query with it**, eg-arm only.
Verified: lucene's query begins with the full gold path; carbon's with `CarbonInterval.php`. The tool's
doctrine says the *agent* authors that query in one sentence. **Every eg number measured today carried
this advantage — and eg still cost 29%.** Must be removed; it also makes the current negative result
stronger, not weaker.

**Headroom.** 300 first-stage locate ops over 21 eg sessions = **14.3/session**, **86% (12.2/session)
answerable by an advertised verb**. Session = 38 calls, 1 call ≈ 48,533 tok ≈ 2.6% of session. This is
a *call-count* lever.

**Retractions this plan depends on.** (a) **1094 of 1094 thinking blocks are empty** (Opus 5 encrypted
thinking) — `run_3arm.sh:657`'s "mentioned ONCE across 490 thinking blocks" measured empty strings.
(b) The 24.4% RUNG2I mark is **not one point away**. 2×2 on 12 shared instances: RUNG2I-eg/RUNG2I-base
saving 25.9%; RUNG2I-eg/fresh-base saving 4.4%; repro-eg/fresh-base COSTING 28.3%. Baseline swap ≈25pt,
eg swap ≈29pt. Fresh baselines are 27.9% cheaper on byte-identical prompts; even never-ENOSPC RUNG2I
baselines are 18.7% inflated; RUNG2I's eg arm carried an eg-only affordance (validated VERIFY 7/30,
`verify.run` 8/30, baseline 0/30). **That binary is worth ~12% on a fair baseline.**

## [CORRECTED] The claim bar — read this before designing anything

Recomputed from 241 paired Opus sessions: per-session replicate sd **s ≈ 0.27 for BOTH arms** (not
eg 6.5% / baseline 15.9%), irreducible arm×instance **τ ≈ 0.09**. `sqrt(τ²+2s²) = 0.393 → ±14.1%`,
which reproduces the observed ±14% exactly.

- **"2 eg + 4 baseline beats 3+3" is WRONG** — the arms are equally noisy, so balanced is optimal
  *within a cell*. Asymmetric allocation is right only to **amortize one baseline across several eg
  configs**.
- **±2.9% is unreachable at n=30.** Floor as R→∞ is **±3.4%**.
- **To CLAIM ≥25% with a CI you must MEASURE ≈ −31.4%** (3+3 trimmed, ±6.4%).

Pre-register both readings, no post-hoc choice:
- **PRIMARY (claim):** upper 95% bound of paired geomean ≤ −25.0%.
- **SECONDARY (progress):** point estimate ≤ −25.0% **and** CI excludes 0. Anything meeting only this
  is written as "point estimate −25%, 95% CI [−X,−Y]" with the interval in the same sentence.

## Plan

### P0 — build the instrument ($0, gates everything)
1. **`tools/phases.py` does not exist** and every gate below needs it. Classify each API call (union
   blocks by `message.id`, as `score_fullpf.py:session_stats()` already does) into LOCATE / ITERATE /
   POST, tagging in-loop shell-explore ops as failure-tied or not. **Validate by reproducing V3's
   n=445 anatomy within 0.3 calls** (LOCATE 18.92/20.17, ITERATE 17.60/21.28, POST 9.51/8.95). If it
   cannot, the numbers this plan is sized against are themselves wrong — stop.
2. **Re-estimate τ** from FIXSTACK↔R2IREPRO eg (16 shared) and RUNG2J↔RUNG2K baseline (30 shared).
   If replicate sd > 0.50, redesign to 4+8 before spending.
3. **Compute η retrospectively** from the 445 sessions (freed phase ops vs realized call delta). This
   is G4's prior; η<0.3 questions the whole route before the pilot.
4. Replace `score_fullpf.py`'s unpaired ratio-of-means (CI ±40.6%) with **paired geomean over
   replicate-averaged instances + instance-level bootstrap** (resample the 30 `L_i`, not sessions).
   Pre-register a symmetric 2-per-tail trim (×0.74 variance) and always report untrimmed alongside.

### Stage 1 — argv parity + the tool's own doctrine (primary lever)
The shipped doctrine (`internal/cli/agents.go:17`, `AGENTS.md`) is written against
`entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "…"` / `impact --repo . --symbol X` /
`capabilities --json`. The shim exposes `eg-q search|def|callers|impact|grep`. **Every doctrine string
the model has ever read is invalid against that surface.** Install the shim on PATH as `entire`,
dispatching `entire graph <verb> [--repo --profile --query --symbol --json]` onto the existing `eg-q`
bodies, then ship the tool's guide **verbatim**. Fenced block, path on every verb, `impact` included.
- **Fairness ledger, per line:** meaningless-without-the-tool (verb syntax, "query it again", group
  semantics, `impact`) → eg only. Generic methodology (read limits, "few turns", "stop", "don't grep")
  → **delete entirely** — that is the class that sank 54.9%/57.7%. Keep the doctrine's *anti*-frugality
  lines ("one signal, not an oracle", "read focused source", "widen the check"): they cost eg turns.
- Assert **per instance**: `count(validated VERIFY, eg) == count(baseline)`, `verify.run` present in
  both arms equally.

### Stage 2 — remove the three contaminations
- **`O35_QUERY_V3=0` and `O35_QUERY_V2=0`** — the gold-path leak (Cause 3). The agent authors the query.
- **`GQ_SEARCH_CAP=0`** — it is a frugality clamp on tool arms only while the baseline greps uncapped,
  and it produced the `SEARCH BUDGET EXHAUSTED` text inside 2/19 prompts. The binary now ships
  `afd5a1c` (one real search per session, echo on repeats), which prices the runaway it guarded.
- **Strip trust-poisoning strings** from the injected payload (keep on disk): `VERIFY: none validated`,
  `Completeness: degraded`, `LOW CONFIDENCE`, `SEARCH BUDGET EXHAUSTED`.

### Stage 3 — drop the prefetch
0/14 FULLPF and 1/22 R2IREPRO sessions ever queried; `published_exact_eg_tool`'s own comment names the
prefetch as the permission slip. Prompt-replay share of session tokens is only **3.0–5.1%**, so the
byte saving is the *smallest* reason — do not sell it as the mechanism. Also demote a rank-1 that
resolves to a **test file** (hugo-12204: eg 74 turns vs baseline 49, +25) via the existing
`EG_DROP_TESTS`/`_egsearch.py` detection.

### Stage 4 — [CORRECTED] `verify` is NOT shipped
`entire graph verify` (`db24f74`) lives only on branch `levers/l1-l2-editability`; `./entire-graph
verify` → `unknown command`. Do **not** put it in cell A — building an unmerged branch and changing
the workflow at once makes the cell unattributable. It becomes **cell B**, reusing cell A's baseline.

### Stage 5 — [CORRECTED] the fresh language-balanced 30
**Python is not in SWE-bench Multilingual at all** — it comes from SWE-bench Verified, where ~494
instances are untouched. My earlier "only 6 Python exist" was wrong. Eligible Multilingual pool after
excluding the 53 tune instances and all of rep100: **172 instances / 39 repos** (Rust 28, Java 27,
PHP 26, Go 24, Ruby 24, JS 20, C 15, C++ 5, **TS 3**).
- Composition: **Python 9, Java 3, Go 3, Rust 3, PHP 2, Ruby 2, JS 2, C 2, TS 2, C++ 2 = 30.**
- **Max 2 instances per repo** — without it preact (13) and lombok (13) dominate and effective n ≈ 15.
- Select by `sha256(instance_id + "GOAL25-v1")` rank within stratum; write `tasks/fresh30_tasks.json`,
  record its sha256 in the prereg, **commit before any session runs**.
- **[CORRECTED] Do NOT filter out DEGRADED graphs.** 20 of 30 rep30 graphs are degraded and the `ok`
  set is exactly the small simple repos — filtering is selection on tool quality and would inflate the
  result. Gate on *correctness* only (`truncated=False, verifiable=True, complete=True`) and treat
  `completeness_level` as a **disclosed stratum**, reporting within-`ok` and within-`degraded`
  separately. If the effect exists only in `ok`, that is the finding.

### Stage 6 — $0 pre-flight (hard gate)
Phase script validates (P0.1) · τ ≤ 0.50 (P0.2) · η reported (P0.3) · **agent-authored query recall
≥50% @top-5** (issue title + first sentence, and the baseline's own first grep string, replayed
against the 30 graphs — *the single riskiest assumption; $0 to falsify*) · `impact` returns ≥3 distinct
non-test symbols on ≥20/30 · every `agentGuide` command string executes against the shim on 30/30 ·
prompt differ shows no frugality token in one arm only and equal validated-VERIFY counts per instance ·
`SEARCH BUDGET EXHAUSTED` absent from all 30 prompts and payloads · graph correctness gate ·
grading dry-run (§7) · **binary pinned out of the session scratchpad with sha256 recorded**
(`entire graph version` reports `dev`; `EG` currently points into `/private/tmp/claude-501/...`).

### Stage 7 — pilot, then cells
- **Pilot: 10 instances × (1 eg + 1 base) = 20 sessions ($54)**, reads G0–G5. Kill here if it fails.
- **Cell A: 30 × (3 eg + 6 base) = 270 sessions ($724)** — doctrine + argv parity + `impact`, no
  prefetch. 6 baselines because the denominator is **reusable**, making cell B cost $241.
- **Cell B: 30 × 3 eg = 90 sessions ($241)** — adds `verify`, single variable, reuses cell A's baseline.

## Gates — falsifiable before the aggregate is read

| # | lever | metric | pass | kill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| G0 | tool reaches the agent | graph calls/session | **≥1.5**, ≥8/10 sessions ≥1 | ≤0.5 → Bash surface unwinnable, MCP deferred with no knob → report the negative and stop |
| G1 | LOCATE collapses | LOCATE calls (eg) | **≤15.0** (from 18.92) | ≥18.0 |
| G2 | multi-site enumeration | in-loop explore not failure-tied | **≤2.2** (from 3.71) | ≥3.3 |
| G3 | post-edit regression | POST calls (eg) | **≤8.95** (parity) | ≥9.5 → only cell B can touch it |
| G4 | transfer efficiency | η = calls removed / phase ops removed | **≥0.45** | ≤0.30 → **do not launch cell A** |
| G5 | mechanism is turns not bytes | log(token ratio)/log(call ratio) | **∈[1.15,1.90]** | outside → measuring payload bytes again |
| G6 | integrity | `SEARCH BUDGET EXHAUSTED` in prompts | **0/30** | ≥1 |
| G7 | prompt symmetry | validated-VERIFY count eg==base, per instance | **30/30** | any mismatch → cell void |

**[CORRECTED] Arithmetic these are calibrated to.** Baseline 41.61 calls, eg 37.95, elasticity ≈1.5.
Gross pool if G1–G3 pass = 6.0 calls. At η=0.45 → −22.9%; η=0.65 → −27.9%; η=1.0 → −35.5%.
**Cell A alone does not clear the *claim* bar unless η≈1.0, which has never been observed.** Realistic
landing is a point estimate of **−20% to −28%**; clearing −25% *with a CI* needs cell B. Sequencing is
arithmetic, not caution.

**Integrity sweep before quoting anything:** ENOSPC **from transcripts, not `*.log`** (RUNG2I: 1 hit in
logs vs 10 in transcripts) · tool-error rate per arm (RUNG2I base 3.87/session vs fresh 2.33) · arm
time-window overlap **≥70%** (RUNG2I overlapped 28%, arms offset +44 min) · `FOREIGN_CACHE_TOUCHED` ·
`CORRUPT_CC_OUT` · empty patches · per-instance prompt diff.

## Grading — [CORRECTED] uninstallable, not merely off
No `.venv`, no `swebench` package. `uv venv .venv --python 3.11 && uv pip install --python
.venv/bin/python datasets swebench tiktoken tabulate`. `tools/assemble_preds.py` is hardcoded to
`tasks/pilot_tasks.json` and `tools/run_eval_model.sh` to the Multilingual dataset — the 9 Python
instances need a second pass against SWE-bench Verified with a distinct `run_id`, merged on
`instance_id`. Per the user: **grade only if the token goal is met.** Power is ±12.5pp at n=30×3, so
pre-register a **−12pp non-inferiority margin** and state that anything smaller is undetectable here.

## Cost
$0 pre-flight → **$54 pilot** (kill point) → **$724 cell A** → **$241 cell B** → ~$153 rerun
contingency ≈ **$1,172 total**. Grading is $0 API (Docker only).

## Explicitly not doing
No payload-quality levers (eight dead). No single-replicate readings. No config selection over cells —
oracle-over-configs (−53.1%) **exactly equals the null** (min-of-k is invariant to label shuffling).
No size gate / skip-prefetch as a *savings* claim. No arm-asymmetric frugality language. No native MCP
— confirmed dead: `MCPPROBE` sessions carry one `deferred_tools_delta` with **no schemas** and **zero**
`mcp__eg__*` tool_use blocks, and CC 2.1.222 exposes no preload knob. No claim from `thinking` text.

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# `entire graph <verb>` — argv parity with entire-graph's OWN shipped doctrine.
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS. The tool's guide (internal/cli/agents.go const agentGuide, AGENTS.md,
# .entire/graph-agent.md) instructs agents in exactly these strings:
#
#     entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"
#     entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
#     entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
#     entire graph capabilities --json
#
# The benchmark instead exposed `eg-q search|def|callers|impact|grep <arg>`. So every doctrine string
# the model has ever read is INVALID against the surface it is given, and the two verbs the documented
# workflow turns on (`impact`, `capabilities`) are renamed or absent. Measured consequence: 0.042 real
# graph queries per session, 2.8% of sessions ever query, and 2 of 14 logged calls are the agent
# running the bare path with no verb just to discover the argv.
#
# This is NOT coaching. It is the tool's published interface, which entire-graph's own README requires
# ("each tool's normal interface") before any savings claim is valid. The baseline has no interface to
# distort, so there is no symmetric counterpart to withhold.
#
# Dispatches onto the per-instance eg-q.run wrapper (which carries the baked EG_*/GSYM/GEDGES/CACHE
# env), so behaviour, filtering and logging are byte-identical to the existing arm — only the argv
# surface changes.
#
# EG_Q_RUN must point at the instance's eg-q.run.
set -uo pipefail

die() { echo "$*" >&2; exit 2; }
GQ="${EG_Q_RUN:-}"
[ -n "$GQ" ] && [ -x "$GQ" ] || die "entire: EG_Q_RUN not set or not executable"

[ "${1:-}" = "graph" ] || die "usage: entire graph <search|impact|neighbors|def|callers|grep|capabilities> [flags]"
shift
verb="${1:-}"; shift 2>/dev/null || true

# Accept the documented flags. --repo/--profile/--json are accepted and intentionally ignored:
# the wrapper already pins the repo and profile per instance, and honouring a different --repo would
# silently query the wrong checkout.
query=""; symbol=""; relation=""; direction=""; positional=()
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --query|-q)     query="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --symbol|-s)    symbol="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --relation)     relation="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --direction)    direction="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --repo|--profile|--format|--top-k|--max-snippet-lines|--max-context-bytes|--cache-dir)
                    shift 2 ;;
    --json|--no-color|--quiet) shift ;;
    --*)            shift ;;                        # tolerate unknown flags rather than failing
    *)              positional+=("$1"); shift ;;
  esac
done
arg="${query:-${symbol:-}}"
[ -n "$arg" ] && [ ${#positional[@]} -gt 0 ] || true
if [ -z "$arg" ] && [ ${#positional[@]} -gt 0 ]; then arg="${positional[*]}"; fi

case "$verb" in
  search)   [ -n "$arg" ] || die "entire graph search: need --query"; exec "$GQ" search "$arg" ;;
  impact)   [ -n "$arg" ] || die "entire graph impact: need --symbol"; exec "$GQ" impact "$arg" ;;
  # documented `neighbors --relation CALLS --direction in` == callers; any other direction/relation
  # degrades to the same blast-radius answer rather than erroring, per the doctrine's own
  # impact -> neighbors -> edges preference order.
  neighbors)
      [ -n "$arg" ] || die "entire graph neighbors: need --symbol"
      if [ "${direction:-in}" = "in" ]; then exec "$GQ" callers "$arg"; else exec "$GQ" impact "$arg"; fi ;;
  callers)  [ -n "$arg" ] || die "entire graph callers: need --symbol"; exec "$GQ" callers "$arg" ;;
  def|show) [ -n "$arg" ] || die "entire graph def: need a symbol"; exec "$GQ" def "$arg" ;;
  grep)     [ -n "$arg" ] || die "entire graph grep: need a regex"; exec "$GQ" grep "$arg" ;;
  capabilities)
      # Feature-detect, per the doctrine's Hard rule 7. Relations are language-dependent.
      printf '{"provider":"entire-graph","verbs":["search","impact","neighbors","def","callers","grep"],"relations":["CALLS","INHERITS","OVERRIDES","USES_TYPE","RETURNS_TYPE","PARAM_TYPE","DATA_FLOWS"],"local_only":true}\n' ;;
  ""|-h|--help|help)
      cat <<'USAGE'
usage: entire graph <verb> [flags]
  search      --query "<one sentence>"     ranked code locations, with complete symbol bodies
  impact      --symbol <Symbol>            blast radius: callers, callees, type consumers, siblings
  neighbors   --symbol <Symbol> --relation CALLS --direction in
  def         <Symbol>                     whole symbol body at real line numbers
  grep        <regex>                      any in-repo text, including build files
  capabilities --json                      which relations this repo's languages support
USAGE
      ;;
  *) die "entire graph: unknown verb '$verb'" ;;
esac

Going to disk was the *correct* response to a 3-line snippet; you cannot edit against that.

Meanwhile my doctrine block asserts the search "prints the complete body of the enclosing function, verbatim… marked complete-symbol". For 5 of 14 hits that claim is false. This is the same deployment-gap pattern that has bitten this campaign twice already — the prompt advertising a block the config suppresses.

**So I'm withdrawing the redundancy line as the primary fix.** It targeted re-reading the *same span*, and the agent isn't doing that; it's reading whole files because fragments are unusable. The correct fix is to make the payload's claim true — `EG_FULL_UNIT=1` and a snippet budget that doesn't truncate a function — so "complete body" means complete body.

That's a better lever than trust-language, and it's testable: if fragments are what drive whole-file reads, then delivering real bodies should cut file reads directly, which is the substitution the −25% arithmetic needs.

Two things I'll note honestly: caddy's top hit *was* 113 lines and complete, so this isn't universal; and I should have checked what the payload actually contained before writing a prompt that described it. That's the second time today I've asserted payload content without verifying it.

Straight answers, all three tested on 139 paired observations.

**1) Is it noise? Partly — noise dominates per-instance, not the aggregate.**
```
within-instance sd across cells   0.408
between-instance sd of the mean   0.181
```
Noise is **larger than the real per-instance signal**. That's why 93% of instances flip win/lose between cells and why per-loser repair is worth 0. It does *not* wash out the aggregate — that's why n and replicates matter.

**2) Language — this is by far the biggest structured effect, and it's the answer to your question.**
```
Go           n=20   saving 24.7%
Rust         n=16   saving 21.2%
C            n=13   saving 20.5%
C++          n= 5   saving 17.0%
Ruby         n=20   saving 16.5%
Java         n=18   saving 12.0%
PHP          n=14   saving  5.6%
Python       n=14   saving  1.1%
JavaScript   n= 9   COSTING 3.7%
TypeScript   n=10   COSTING 7.0%
```
**A 32-point spread, monotone and mechanistically sensible** — static, richly-typed languages where the graph resolves real relations save 20–25%; the JS/TS family costs. rep30's 12–13% aggregate is just the mix-weighted average of these.

**3) Tool usage / payload quality — real but small.** Complete bodies save 17.5% vs fragments 12.4%, a 5.1-point gap in the right direction (corr +0.083, so weak). Worth fixing, not the lever. And `corr(baseline turns, outcome) = −0.347` — the graph wins where the baseline would have flailed.

**Now the uncomfortable tip you need before we build the fresh 30: putting 9 Python instances in it will *lower* the number.** Python measures **saving 1.1%** — essentially break-even. A "language-balanced" set with 30% Python is close to the worst composition for hitting 25%.

**So, when do we hit it?** On a Go/Rust/C-weighted set, **25% is already achievable today** — those strata measure 20–25% with the current tool. On a JS/TS-heavy set, never. The honest framing that survives review is a **language-stratified claim**: "saves 20–25% on Go/Rust/C/C++, break-even on Python, costs on JS/TS" — disclosed by stratum, not a single cherry-picked headline. Silently choosing the favourable mix is the selection bias that got prior claims withdrawn.

**Given that, I'd change the plan:** keep the language-balanced 30 as the *honest headline* set, but report per-stratum, and treat the JS/TS deficit as the real engineering target — that's where the tool is losing, and fixing TypeScript resolution is worth more than any prompt change. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""$0 A/B: does --full-unit-top actually eliminate fragment hits?

WHY. The doctrine block I ship asserts the search "prints the complete body of the enclosing
function, verbatim ... marked complete-symbol". Measured on the live pilot payloads that is false
for 5 of 14 hits (spans of 1, 3 and 6 lines), and the two instances whose top hit was a 3- and
6-line fragment are exactly the two where the agent then read the WHOLE file. Going to disk is the
correct response to a 3-line snippet.

Separately, over 134 historical paired observations, payloads that are mostly complete bodies
measure saving 17.5% vs 12.4% for fragment-heavy ones -- a +5.1 point gap. `EG_FULL_UNIT` is unset
in every launcher, so the fragments are a config defect, not a tool limitation.

This replays the SAME query against the SAME graph with EG_FULL_UNIT off vs on and reports the
fragment rate, so the fix is proven before any session is paid for.

GATE: complete-symbol rate must rise materially (target: fragments <= 10% of hits), and gold-file
rank must not regress on any instance.

Usage: tools/fragment_ab.py [--limit N]
"""
import argparse
import glob
import json
import os
import re
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys

SUITE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
EG = os.environ.get("ENTIRE_GRAPH", f"{SUITE}/bin/entire-graph-94009ef")
WTROOT = "/tmp/recall_wt"
HIT = re.compile(r"^\s*(\d+)\.\s+(\S+?):(\d+)-(\d+)")


def gold_files(patch):
    return sorted(set(re.findall(r"\+\+\+ b/(\S+)", patch or "")))


def agent_query(task):
    ps = (task.get("problem_statement") or "").strip()
    line = ps.splitlines()[0] if ps else ""
    line = re.sub(r"https?://\S+", " ", line)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line)[:200]


def run(wt, iid, q, full_unit):
    cmd = [EG, "search", "--query", q, "--repo", wt, "--profile", "full",
           "--format", "text", "--top-k", "5",
           "--max-snippet-lines", "6", "--max-context-bytes", "24576",
           "--cache-dir", f"{SUITE}/.eg_cache/{iid}"]
    if full_unit:
        cmd[6:6] = ["--full-unit-top", str(full_unit)]
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return [], []
    hits, spans = [], []
    for ln in (r.stdout or "").splitlines():
        m = HIT.match(ln)
        if m:
            hits.append((m.group(2), "complete-symbol" in ln))
            spans.append(int(m.group(4)) - int(m.group(3)) + 1)
    return hits, spans


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    os.chdir(SUITE)
    tasks = json.load(open("tasks/rep30_tasks.json"))["instances"]
    if a.limit:
        tasks = tasks[:a.limit]
    if not os.access(EG, os.X_OK):
        sys.exit(f"binary not executable: {EG}")

    agg = {0: dict(hits=0, complete=0, spans=[], goldrank=[]),
           1: dict(hits=0, complete=0, spans=[], goldrank=[])}
    print(f"{'instance':32s} {'OFF frag':>9s} {'ON frag':>8s} {'OFF med':>8s} {'ON med':>7s}  gold rank")
    for t in tasks:
        iid = t["instance_id"]
        wt = f"{WTROOT}/{iid}"
        if not os.path.isdir(wt):
            continue
        gold = set(gold_files(t.get("patch", "")))
        q = agent_query(t)
        if not q:
            continue
        out = {}
        for fu in (0, 1):
            hits, spans = run(wt, iid, q, fu)
            if not hits:
                out[fu] = None
                continue
            frag = sum(1 for _, c in hits if not c) / len(hits)
            gr = next((k for k, (p, _) in enumerate(hits, 1) if p in gold), None)
            agg[fu]["hits"] += len(hits)
            agg[fu]["complete"] += sum(1 for _, c in hits if c)
            agg[fu]["spans"] += spans
            agg[fu]["goldrank"].append(gr)
            out[fu] = (frag, statistics.median(spans), gr)
        if out.get(0) and out.get(1):
            f0, m0, g0 = out[0]
            f1, m1, g1 = out[1]
            flag = ""
            if g0 and (g1 is None or g1 > g0):
                flag = "  <-- GOLD RANK REGRESSED"
            print(f"  {iid:30s} {f0*100:8.0f}% {f1*100:7.0f}% {m0:8.0f} {m1:7.0f}  {g0}->{g1}{flag}", flush=True)

    print("\nAGGREGATE")
    for fu, lbl in ((0, "EG_FULL_UNIT=0 (today)"), (1, "EG_FULL_UNIT=1")):
        d = agg[fu]
        if not d["hits"]:
            continue
        frag = (d["hits"] - d["complete"]) / d["hits"] * 100
        found = [g for g in d["goldrank"] if g]
        print(f"  {lbl:24s} hits={d['hits']:3d}  fragments={frag:5.1f}%  "
              f"median span={statistics.median(d['spans']):5.1f} lines  "
              f"gold found {len(found)}/{len(d['goldrank'])}")
    if agg[0]["hits"] and agg[1]["hits"]:
        f0 = (agg[0]["hits"] - agg[0]["complete"]) / agg[0]["hits"] * 100
        f1 = (agg[1]["hits"] - agg[1]["complete"]) / agg[1]["hits"] * 100
        reg = sum(1 for x, y in zip(agg[0]["goldrank"], agg[1]["goldrank"])
                  if x and (y is None or y > x))
        print(f"\n  fragment rate {f0:.1f}% -> {f1:.1f}%   "
              f"GATE (fragments <=10% and 0 rank regressions): "
              f"{'PASS' if f1 <= 10 and reg == 0 else 'FAIL'}   rank regressions={reg}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

- **Argv parity fixes real usability** — graph calls 0.042 → 1.75/session — and cut in-loop enumeration 5.45 → 3.60.

# entire-graph on SWE-bench Multilingual / Opus — findings, 2026-08-05

Goal pursued: ≥25% token saving on rep30, fairly measured, then a four-arm 100-instance run.
**Neither was achieved.** This records what was measured, what was fixed, and what was withdrawn.

## 1. The headline number

Strictly gated (both arms `subtype=success` AND non-empty `patch.diff`), n=204 paired sessions
over 8 cells / 30 instances:

| metric | result |
|---|---|
| **tokens, paired geomean** | **saving 10.3%**  CI [3.8%, 16.1%] |
| tokens, total (Σeg / Σbaseline) | saving 12.0% — 478.1M → 420.9M |
| cost (USD), geomean | saving 9.1% |
| cost, total | saving 9.7% — $530.78 → $479.03 |

Total > geomean: the tool saves more on expensive instances, which is the right shape for
deployment. Cost < tokens: savings land in cache-read, ~20× cheaper than output.

**Gate everything.** Applying only "non-empty patch" without `subtype=success` inflated a
"strong strata 22.0%" reading to a true 13.3%, and let a session that finished cleanly and wrote
NO patch (ruff-15626) report as "saving 52.2%". A session that does no work always looks cheap.

## 2. The dominant variable is the machine, not the config

Same eg sessions, same prompts, same instances (n=21), scored against two different-day baselines:

```
Aug-4 machine   baseline mean 2,392,287 tok  49.1 turns
Aug-5 machine   baseline mean 1,905,390 tok  42.7 turns   (20.4% cheaper, byte-identical prompts)

SAME RUNG2I eg sessions:   vs Aug-4 baseline  saving 26.0%
                           vs Aug-5 baseline  saving  5.0%
                           --> 21.0 points is machine state
```

This explains a campaign-long mystery: cells ranged 3.5%–28.9% with configs that barely differed.
It is why one machine reports 25%+ and another reports 10%. **It is not noise and not fraud — it is
an uncontrolled variable.** Never quote a cross-cell or cross-machine comparison without recording
baseline mean tokens and turns.

The mechanism was NOT identified. A "cold package cache" explanation was proposed and **withdrawn**:
`pkg_iso` is created per-instance and isolates caches rather than warming them. Aug-4's ENOSPC
contamination (10/30 baselines) was separated out — the clean subset still measures 24.4%
CI [12.4, 35.5], so disk exhaustion is not the whole story. Because the cause is unknown the state
cannot be reproduced on demand, so **24.4% is an observation, not a claimable result.**

## 3. Defects found and fixed

**`eg-fixstack` binary is a regression — do not ship.**
−7.9 points overall (3.7% vs 11.6% for all other cells). Catastrophic on Python: django COSTING
94.9%, pylint COSTING 86.7%, against 13–47% savings in every other cell. Python stratum goes
8.2% → 14.8% with that cell excluded. Two independent lines of evidence: this, and RUNG2I (24.4%)
vs FIXSTACK (3.7%) differing in **the binary alone**. Six launchers still reference it.
Good build pinned: `bin/entire-graph-94009ef`, sha256 `3f7318a8…c0ca35e4`.

**TypeScript extraction bug — fixed, replicated.**
`internal/sem/parser.go:4399` gated `function_signature` to Dart. tree-sitter-typescript emits that
node for **every bodyless declaration** — overloads, `declare function`, ambients, `.d.ts` — so all
were silently dropped. `renderList.ts`: 6 declarations → 1 symbol; lines 10–53 unindexed.
Fixed additively (+54 lines), mutation-verified tests, 1976 pass.
Measured on docusaurus, 3 replicates: **saving 35.9%, CI [24.3%, 45.0%]** vs old binary's 9.8% —
a **+26.2 point** improvement. The only mechanism this campaign that survived replication.
Repo-wide symbol gain is modest (vuejs +1.0%, docusaurus +2.1%).

**Argv parity — the tool's documented commands did not exist.**
The shipped guide instructs `entire graph search --repo . --query "…"`; the harness exposed
`eg-q <verb> <arg>`. Every doctrine string the model had read was invalid. Measured usage: **0.042
graph calls/session, 8 of 610 call logs ever non-empty**, and 2 of 14 logged calls were the agent
running the bare path to discover the argv. With `tools/entire-frontend` giving the published
surface: **1.75 calls/session**. Usage fixed; cost was not — the calls added rather than replaced
(G5 failed), so the pilot still cost 9.5%.

**Measurement-stack repairs.** Build failure used to `SKIP; exit 0`, deleting the row — and the
baseline has no build step, so the arm whose tool fails most had its own worst instances removed.
Now: symmetric gating (any arm's failure removes the instance from all arms), `TOOL_BUILD_FAILED`
detected from the artifacts the harness itself tests, per-arm accounting
(`n_attempted | n_build_failed | n_gate_failed | n_scored`), and data-driven arms.
Graphify's shim and post-processor recovered **byte-exact**; its builder reconstructed.
**Graphify fails to build 9 of 30 instances** (`nodes=0`) — previously invisible.

## 4. What was tested and did not work

Twelve mechanisms. None moved the aggregate:

per-repo/loser repair (ceiling 14.6%, worth +1.7pt — no instance loses consistently, 93% flip sign) ·
full payload vs minimal · argv parity + doctrine · complete bodies (`EG_FULL_UNIT`: fragments
25.6%→24.2% on 30, despite 11.1%→5.6% on a 6-instance sample) · trust language · language
stratification (13.3% strong strata, strictly gated) · binary selection · **locate reduction** ·
cost-vs-tokens · prefetch removal · payload-quality metrics (8 prior) · session-length gating.

**Locate reduction deserves its own line** because the whole GOAL25 plan rested on it:
"LOCATE 13→8 calls = −25.1%" at elasticity 1.5. Tested cross-cell, `corr(LOCATE delta, token
delta) = +0.188`. RUNG2H cut LOCATE by exactly 4.74 calls and saved **7.1%**; RUNG2J made LOCATE
*worse* and saved **15.2%**. The elasticity is refuted.

## 5. Claims withdrawn during this work

Recorded because each was stated before being checked:

- "Strong strata save 22.0%" — ungated; 13.3% strictly gated.
- "ruff saving 52.2%" — the session wrote **no patch**.
- "The graph makes LOCATE longer" — generalised from one cell; 7 of 12 cells have eg's LOCATE below baseline.
- "TypeScript recovers ~10% of declarations vs 68–130% elsewhere" — from two gold files; repo-wide TS extracts *more* symbols/file than Go or Rust.
- "`O35_QUERY_V3` leaks the gold path pervasively" — 5 of 30 instances (17%).
- "Payload budgets differ 8–12×" — units error; graphify's 2000 is *tokens* (~8KB) vs eg's 16384 *bytes*.
- "Cold package caches explain the Aug-4 regime" — contradicted by `pkg_iso` semantics.
- "Prose is 80% of output tokens" — transcript dedupe artifact; one API response spans several JSONL lines sharing a `message.id`, and keeping the longest drops `tool_use`. Real figure: 3.0%.

## 6. Fairness state of the benchmark

- The prefetch/VERIFY stack is **structurally eg-only** (`run_3arm.sh:418`–`:894`). 93.3% of eg
  prompts carry a `VERIFY:` line, 21.6% a *validated* command; cmm and graphify have no code path
  that could receive any of it.
- **cmm and graphify have never run here** — n=0 each. All existing data is 2-arm.
- `verify.run` was eg-only in every cell (14/17/8/2/2/2/4/2 vs 0 baseline); fixed 2026-08-05, i.e.
  after every cell in `results/`. **Re-run, do not re-analyse.**
- Tuning asymmetry: eg has 26 shim knobs, 15 swept, 5 registered configs; cmm and graphify 0 swept.
  `EG_MAXBYTES` was amended to the value that cleared −35% by 0.7pt (`RUN-MANIFEST.md:308-319`).
- The frugality block **is** clean — byte-identical across arms, 0 eg-favouring phrases.
- Resolve grading is **uninstallable**, not merely off (no `.venv`, no `swebench`). Every number
  here is token-only and cannot detect a resolve regression.

## 7. Instrument

Per-session replicate sd **s ≈ 0.276**, arm×instance **τ ≈ 0.09** → 1+1 gives ±14.1%, 3+3 ±8.7%,
floor at n=30 is ±3.4%. **To CLAIM ≥25% you must MEASURE ≈−31.4%.** Within-instance sd across cells
(0.408) exceeds between-instance sd (0.181): per-instance results are dominated by noise, which is
why 93% of instances flip sign and per-loser repair is worth zero.

## 8. Tools added

`tools/phases.py` (LOCATE/ITERATE/POST decomposition — did not exist; the published anatomy does not
sum to its own headline, 46.03 vs 37.95 calls) · `tools/recall_agent_query.py` (agent-authored
queries reach **70% gold recall @5** with paths stripped — the permalink leak was unnecessary) ·
`tools/fragment_ab.py` · `tools/entire-frontend` · `tools/run_goal25.sh` · `tools/armcfg.py` ·
`tools/mark_build_failures.py` · `tools/arm_affordance_census.py` · `tools/graphify-q`,
`tools/_gqy.py`, `tools/build_graphify_graph.sh` (recovered) · `bin/entire-graph-94009ef` (pinned).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Where does the TOTAL-token saving actually live?

The goal admits either metric: total (sum eg / sum baseline) or paired geomean.
They are NOT the same lever. Geomean weights every instance equally, so a 30-instance
set needs broad wins. Total is dominated by the biggest baselines, so a handful of
expensive instances can carry it.

This measures the concentration and prints, for each instance, how many points of
TOTAL saving are still on the table there. That tells us which instances are worth
paying to fix and which cannot move the number no matter what.

Strict gate throughout: both arms subtype==success AND non-empty patch.diff.
"""
import json
import os
import sys
import glob
import math
import statistics
import collections

SUITE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


def tokens(u):
    if not u:
        return 0
    return (u.get("input_tokens", 0) + u.get("output_tokens", 0)
            + u.get("cache_read_input_tokens", 0)
            + u.get("cache_creation_input_tokens", 0))


def load(cell, arm):
    """instance_id -> dict(tok, usd, turns) for gated sessions only."""
    out = {}
    root = f"{SUITE}/results/{cell}_r1_{arm}"
    if not os.path.isdir(root):
        return out
    for d in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        cc = f"{root}/{d}/cc_out.json"
        pd = f"{root}/{d}/patch.diff"
        if not os.path.isfile(cc):
            continue
        try:
            j = json.load(open(cc))
        except Exception:
            continue
        if j.get("subtype") != "success":
            continue
        if not (os.path.isfile(pd) and os.path.getsize(pd) > 0):
            continue
        t = tokens(j.get("usage"))
        if t <= 0:
            continue
        out[d] = dict(tok=t, usd=j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0.0,
                      turns=j.get("num_turns") or 0)
    return out


def main():
    cells = sys.argv[1:] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else None
    if not cells:
        cells = sorted({os.path.basename(p).rsplit("_r1_", 1)[0]
                        for p in glob.glob(f"{SUITE}/results/*_r1_eg")})
    # pool every instance that has BOTH arms in the SAME cell
    pairs = collections.defaultdict(list)   # iid -> [(egtok, basetok, cell)]
    for c in cells:
        e, b = load(c, "eg"), load(c, "baseline")
        for iid in set(e) & set(b):
            pairs[iid].append((e[iid]["tok"], b[iid]["tok"], c))

    if not pairs:
        sys.exit("no gated pairs found")

    rows = []
    for iid, obs in sorted(pairs.items()):
        eg = statistics.mean(x for x, _, _ in obs)
        ba = statistics.mean(y for _, y, _ in obs)
        rows.append((iid, eg, ba, len(obs)))

    SUM_E = sum(r[1] for r in rows)
    SUM_B = sum(r[2] for r in rows)
    total_sav = 1 - SUM_E / SUM_B
    geo = math.exp(statistics.mean(math.log(r[1] / r[2]) for r in rows))
    print(f"pooled over {len(cells)} cells, {len(rows)} instances, "
          f"{sum(r[3] for r in rows)} paired obs")
    print(f"  TOTAL  saving {total_sav*100:5.1f}%   (sum eg {SUM_E/1e6:.0f}M / base {SUM_B/1e6:.0f}M)")
    print(f"  GEOMEAN saving {(1-geo)*100:5.1f}%")
    print()

    # concentration
    by_base = sorted(rows, key=lambda r: -r[2])
    print("CONCENTRATION of baseline tokens")
    cum = 0
    for k in (1, 3, 5, 8, 10, 15, 20, len(rows)):
        if k > len(rows):
            continue
        s = sum(r[2] for r in by_base[:k])
        print(f"  top {k:2d} instances hold {s/SUM_B*100:5.1f}% of all baseline tokens")
    print()

    print(f"{'instance':34s} {'base Mtok':>9s} {'%ofbase':>8s} {'saving':>8s} "
          f"{'pts of TOTAL':>13s} {'headroom':>9s} n")
    print(f"{'':34s} {'':>9s} {'':>8s} {'':>8s} {'contributed':>13s} {'to 100%':>9s}")
    for iid, eg, ba, n in by_base:
        share = ba / SUM_B
        sav = 1 - eg / ba
        contributed = (ba - eg) / SUM_B * 100      # pts of total saving this instance gives now
        headroom = ba / SUM_B * 100 - contributed  # pts if eg went to ZERO tokens (absurd ceiling)
        print(f"  {iid:32s} {ba/1e6:9.2f} {share*100:7.1f}% {sav*100:7.1f}% "
              f"{contributed:12.2f} {headroom:8.2f} {n}")

    print()
    print("WHAT WOULD REACH 25% TOTAL")
    need = 0.25 * SUM_B
    have = SUM_B - SUM_E
    print(f"  need to remove {need/1e6:8.1f}M tokens; currently removing {have/1e6:8.1f}M")
    print(f"  shortfall      {(need-have)/1e6:8.1f}M  ({(need-have)/SUM_B*100:.1f} pts)")
    print()
    # if every LOSING instance were merely neutralised (eg == baseline)
    losers = [r for r in by_base if r[1] > r[2]]
    recover = sum(r[1] - r[2] for r in losers)
    print(f"  neutralise all {len(losers)} losing instances -> "
          f"+{recover/SUM_B*100:.2f} pts  => TOTAL {(have+recover)/SUM_B*100:.1f}%")
    # if every instance hit the best observed per-instance saving
    best = max((1 - r[1] / r[2]) for r in by_base)
    print(f"  best single-instance saving observed: {best*100:.1f}%")
    # top-K uplift needed
    for k in (5, 8, 10):
        if k > len(by_base):
            continue
        topb = sum(r[2] for r in by_base[:k])
        tope = sum(r[1] for r in by_base[:k])
        restb = SUM_B - topb
        reste = SUM_E - tope
        # what saving on top-k is required so overall == 25%?
        req = 1 - (0.75 * SUM_B - reste) / topb
        print(f"  top {k:2d} ({topb/SUM_B*100:.0f}% of tokens, now saving "
              f"{(1-tope/topb)*100:.1f}%) must reach {req*100:.1f}% for 25% overall")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Handoff — reaching 25% token saving on rep30, Opus, entire-graph vs no-tool

**For: the planning model.** This is a briefing, not a plan you must follow. Its job is to stop you
re-deriving things that are already measured and to hand you the one piece of arithmetic that
determines whether any given idea can possibly work. Everything here is measured on disk at
`/Users/suhaan/graphmark-bench/agentic-swebench` unless marked otherwise.

Written 2026-08-05. Author: the executing model. Section 9 is my own proposed plan — argue with it.

---

## 1. The goal, stated precisely

≥25% token saving on the rep30 instance set, Opus, **fairly measured**, then a four-arm 100-instance
run on the winning config. The user has confirmed **either total tokens (Σeg/Σbaseline) or paired
geomean** satisfies the goal. Total currently reads higher, so total is the easier target.

**What "fairly" means here, non-negotiable:**

- A session counts only if `cc_out.json subtype == "success"` **AND** `patch.diff` exists and is
  non-empty. Pairs drop **symmetrically** — if either arm fails on an instance, the instance leaves
  both arms. Omitting the subtype check once inflated a "22.0%" reading to a true 13.3%, and let a
  session that wrote no patch at all report "saving 52.2%". A session that does no work looks cheap.
- Both arms get byte-identical prompts except for tool syntax. **Generic frugality or methodology
  instructions given to one arm are the single largest source of withdrawn results on this
  benchmark.** A "-35%" headline once came from two extra instructions on the tool side; removing
  them moved the cell from −14.9% to +9.1%.
- Tool-side default changes (ranking, payload content, flags) are legitimate. Extra *instructions*
  are not.

---

## 2. Where we actually are

Pooled over 22 cells / 30 instances / 236 strictly-gated paired sessions:

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| **total** (Σeg/Σbaseline) | **saving 12.8%** — 69M vs 80M |
| **paired geomean** | **saving 11.8%** |

Reproduce with `python3 tools/concentration.py` (written this session; it contains a correct
strictly-gated loader — reuse it rather than writing another).

Caveat that matters: pooling across 22 cells estimates *expected value across configs tried*, not
the best config. A separate agent is ranking cells by fairness and config right now. But no single
fair cell has ever read above ~15% except two contaminated ones (§4).

---

## 3. THE ARITHMETIC — read this before proposing anything

This is the most useful thing in the document. It rules out whole classes of plan.

```
CONCENTRATION of baseline tokens across the 30 instances
  top  1 instance  =   8.7% of all baseline tokens
  top  3           =  21.8%
  top  5           =  32.3%
  top 10           =  52.7%
  top 20           =  84.4%
```

Consequences, each measured:

1. **No instance can carry the number.** The largest is 8.7% of the mass. Winning 100% of it (an
   impossibility) adds 8 points.
2. **Loser repair is worth nothing.** Only 5 of 30 instances currently lose. Driving all five to
   *exactly neutral* moves the total from 12.8% to **13.2%** — **+0.35 points**. This confirms an
   earlier independent finding that 93% of instances flip win/lose sign between cells and no
   instance loses consistently. **Do not plan a per-loser repair campaign.** It has been tried; it
   is arithmetically incapable of reaching the goal.
3. **The best per-instance saving ever observed, averaged over replicates, is 32.0%** (valkey). The
   mean is 12.8%. So 25% overall requires most instances to perform at or near the historical best.
4. **The explicit target, if you go the concentration route:** the top 10 instances hold 53% of all
   tokens and currently save 13.8%. **They must reach 36.9%** for the suite to hit 25%.
   - Those ten: `lombok-3486, axum-1119, bat-2260, hugo-12204, phpspreadsheet-4214, docusaurus-9183,
     hugo-12562, fmt-2457, pylint-7080, caddy-5995`.
   - `caddy-5995` is 3.9% of all tokens and currently **loses** (−0.2%).

**Net: 25% needs a broad mechanism that roughly doubles the per-instance effect. It cannot be
reached by fixing a handful of instances.**

---

## 4. Known confounds — check these before believing any cell

- **Claude Code CLI version.** Cells span 2.1.221 and 2.1.222. Pooled: 2.1.221 n=154 → **11.7%**;
  2.1.222 n=61 → **6.6%**. The newer CLI made the *no-tool* arm ~4 turns cheaper and ate ~5 points
  of the tool's advantage. Record the version for every cell; never compare across versions.
- **`RUNG2I` (the famous "24.4%" cell) is an outlier inside its own version cohort.** Five other
  cells on the identical 2.1.221 build range from costing 2.8% to saving 15.2%, pooling to 11.7%.
  RUNG2I also has the highest baseline turn count in the campaign (54.0) and 10 of its 30 baselines
  hit ENOSPC. **Treat 24.4% as one hot cell, not a config that was lost.** (I previously attributed
  ~21 points to "machine state"; that was an overstatement — version is worth ~5, contamination
  most of the rest.)
- **`FIXSTACK` used a bad binary** — a −7.9 point regression, catastrophic on Python (django costing
  94.9%, pylint costing 86.7%, against 13–47% savings elsewhere). Exclude it from every pool.
- **ENOSPC must be detected from transcripts, not `*.log`** — RUNG2I showed 1 hit in logs vs 10 in
  transcripts.
- **Load pressure flips sign between cells.** Whichever arm runs under RAM/swap starvation looks
  worse. Cap concurrency (~8-way on 48GB, ~2.9GB/session) and check both ENOSPC and timeout markers
  per arm after every cell.

---

## 5. The noise floor — this sets the claim bar

- Per-session replicate sd **s ≈ 0.276**, arm×instance **τ ≈ 0.09**. 1 replicate per arm gives
  **±14.1%**; 3+3 trimmed gives **±6.4%**; the floor as replicates → ∞ at n=30 is **±3.4%**.
- **To CLAIM ≥25% with a confidence interval you must MEASURE ≈ 31.4%.**
- Same-instance spread across repeated cells is **45pt median**, tail to 335pt. MDE in a single
  30-instance cell is ~30pt.
- **Never score a partial cell** (a geomean moved 47 points between n=9 and n=25). **Never bucket
  one cell into sub-groups of 3–7 and read the differences** — that is how two retracted "levers"
  were produced.
- 0/30 instances produce the same agent query twice (median token overlap 0.55). Retrieval itself
  varies run to run, so any offline replay that fixes the query measures one sample of the input —
  replay across *every* recorded query variant.

---

## 6. The graveyard — do not propose these again

Each was tested and failed. Several were my own ideas.

| dead lever | evidence |
|---|---|
| **Payload-quality metrics as a causal lever** | **TEN** distinct metrics have now failed, including editability, aim, line-coverage. Treat as law: payload-quality score does not predict tokens. |
| **Per-loser / per-repo repair** | ceiling 14.6%, worth +1.7pt in the best case, +0.35pt on today's data (§3.2). Losers are not stable. |
| **LOCATE-reduction elasticity** | The whole prior GOAL25 plan rested on "LOCATE 13→8 calls = −25%". Measured cross-cell `corr(LOCATE delta, token delta) = +0.188`. RUNG2H cut LOCATE by exactly 4.74 calls and saved 7.1%; RUNG2J made LOCATE *worse* and saved 15.2%. **Refuted.** |
| **Prefetching the search from issue text** | Dominated: gold-visible@5 0.567 vs 0.715 for the agent's own query, 8 losses to 0 wins. |
| **Raising the turn cap** | Both arms grow proportionally. |
| **Native MCP delivery** | `MCPPROBE` sessions carry one `deferred_tools_delta` with no schemas and zero `mcp__eg__*` tool_use blocks; CC 2.1.222 exposes no preload knob. Also `--safe-mode` silently strips every MCP server. |
| **Oracle config selection over cells** | −53.1% "oracle" exactly equals the null; min-of-k is invariant to label shuffling. |
| **Complete bodies (`EG_FULL_UNIT`)** | 6-instance sample looked like a pass (fragments 11.1→5.6%); full 30 measured 25.6→24.2%. Withdrawn. |
| **Anything read from `thinking` text** | 1094 of 1094 Opus 5 thinking blocks are encrypted/empty. Prior claims sourced from thinking text measured empty strings. |

---

## 7. What is genuinely live

**(a) The TypeScript extraction bug — fixed and now cleanly attributable.**
`internal/sem/parser.go:4399` gated `function_signature` to Dart. tree-sitter-typescript emits that
node for *every bodyless declaration* — overloads, `declare function`, ambients, `.d.ts` — so all
were silently dropped. vue's `renderList.ts` exposed 1 symbol instead of 6.

I found and closed a confound in it this session: the previously-measured TS binary
(`bin/entire-graph-tsoverload`) was built from `afd5a1c`, which is **11 commits behind** the pinned
good build `94009ef` — missing "answer ambiguous/misspelled queries instead of refusing", "keep
fuzzy relevance order", Go interface-method indexing, C++ template specialization, `--full-unit-top`
and the payload diet. Its headline "+26.2 points on docusaurus" was the TS fix *minus eleven other
changes*, not the TS fix.

**Rebuilt clean:** patch applies to `94009ef` with zero conflicts, `+54` lines, no deletions.
Binary `entire-graph-94009ef-ts`, sha256 `d128426e3ab74663…`. Verified: full `internal/sem` suite
passes; `renderList.ts` 1 → 6 symbols; and symbol output is **byte-identical to `94009ef` on eight
non-TS repos** (django, axum, gson, carbon, bat, caddy, fmt, rubocop). So a cell measuring it is
attributable to the TS fix alone.

**But size it honestly: rep30 holds 2 TypeScript + 2 JavaScript instances of 30.** Even at the old
(confounded) +26pt magnitude that is ~1.7 points on the aggregate. **This is a correctness fix worth
shipping; it is not a route to 25%.** If the task set is rebuilt, TS/JS weighting is a lever — but
see §8 on why re-weighting the task set is dangerous.

**(b) Grep elimination is the strongest predictor found.** `eg_searches/baseline_searches` per
instance correlates with the token outcome at r ≈ +0.6 to +0.7 on other models, while
`corr(baseline greps, outcome) ≈ 0` — so it is not task difficulty leaking through. Classification
of the greps the tool arm *still* runs: 38% finding something NEW (recall/ranking), 29% searching
inside a file the payload already returned, 25% re-finding a symbol the payload already gave, 8%
env/build hunting. **~54% is payload under-delivery** — the agent was handed the answer and searched
for it anyway. This is being re-measured on current cells as I write.

**(c) The tool is barely invoked.** Measured across every cell: **0.042 graph calls/session; 2.8% of
sessions ever query; 8 of 610 `gq_calls.log` non-empty.** Cause: the shipped guide documents
`entire graph search --repo . --query "…"` but the harness exposed `eg-q <verb> <arg>` — **every
doctrine string the model ever read was invalid against the actual surface**. Installing a shim
providing the published argv raised usage to **1.75 calls/session**. Usage is fixed; cost was not —
the calls **added** rather than **replaced** grep, so that pilot still cost 9.5%. That failure mode
is the crux: *invocation is necessary but not sufficient; the payload must end the search.*

**(d) The post-edit tail.** ~65% of output tokens land after the first edit, and the post-last-edit
tail separates winners from losers at AUC 0.945. Never properly quantified. Under measurement now.

---

## 8. Constraints on the plan

- **Cost.** Roughly $2.70/session at Opus. A 30-instance cell at 1+1 is ~$160; at 3+3 ~$480. Budget
  is real; the user has said "verify and don't recklessly waste time."
- **Time.** ~8 hours from now.
- **Grading.** The resolve-grading stack is *uninstallable*, not merely off (no `.venv`, no
  `swebench` package). Every number is token-only and cannot detect a resolve regression. Per the
  user: **grade only if the token goal is met.**
- **Re-weighting the task set is legitimate only if pre-registered and disclosed.** Building a fresh
  language-balanced 30 was approved by the user. But selecting instances *after* seeing which ones
  the tool wins is selection on the outcome and will not survive the four-arm run. Pre-register the
  set, commit it, record its sha256, then run. Also: **do not filter out DEGRADED graphs** — 20 of
  30 rep30 graphs are degraded and the `ok` set is exactly the small simple repos, so filtering is
  selection on tool quality. Gate on correctness only and disclose completeness as a stratum.
- **The four-arm run is gated on the goal.** cmm and graphify have **never run** (n=0 each); all
  existing data is 2-arm. Graphify fails to build 9 of 30 instances. Fix before, not during.

---

## 9. My proposed plan — argue with it

The arithmetic in §3 says only a broad mechanism works. The only broad mechanism with a measured
causal handle is **grep elimination**, and the measured reason it fails is **payload
under-delivery**: 54% of residual searches are for content the payload already contained or for
content inside a file the payload already named. Invocation was fixed and did not convert, because
the payload answered the first question and not the second.

**Spine: make one graph call end the search, instead of starting it.**

- **P0 ($0, gates everything).** Finish the five forensic agents now running: output-token pools,
  post-edit tail + censoring, top-10 instance sinks, fair config ranking with CIs, residual-grep
  classification. Kill any lever whose pool is smaller than 5 points of total tokens — §3 says
  anything smaller cannot matter.
- **P1 ($0).** Offline replay: for every recorded query variant in `gq_calls.log`, measure what
  fraction of the *subsequent* searches in that session would have been answered by an enriched
  payload. This is a deterministic, zero-cost upper bound on the lever. **Gate: the addressable
  share must exceed 15 points of total tokens, or the route is dead before any session is paid
  for.** Prior work trusts offline replays far more than single-session attributions.
- **P2 (one cheap cell).** Ship the enriched payload, the clean TS binary, and the argv shim.
  1 eg + 1 baseline on 30 = ~$160. Read grep-ratio and total tokens. **Gate: grep ratio must fall
  below 0.5 AND total saving must clear 18%.** Below that, stop and report the negative — 25% is not
  reachable on this axis and the honest answer is the deliverable.
- **P3 (replicates).** Only if P2 clears: 3+3 on the winning config to get the interval down to
  ±6.4%, which is what a 25% *claim* requires (measure ≈31.4%).
- **P4.** Four-arm 100, with graphify's 9 build failures fixed first and symmetric gating on.

**What I will not do:** propose another payload-quality metric (ten are dead), another per-loser
campaign (+0.35pt), or any lever that requires giving one arm instructions the other lacks.

---

## 10. Open questions where I'd value your view

1. **Is the concentration route or the broad route better?** §3.4 says top-10 → 36.9% suffices.
   Is 36.9% on ten specific expensive instances more reachable than 25% on all thirty? It is a
   smaller surface but a higher bar, and those ten are the *hardest* instances.
2. **Total vs geomean.** Total is currently 1.0 point higher and weights the expensive instances the
   tool already does best on. Is there a principled reason to prefer one, or is picking the higher
   one after the fact a form of the oracle-selection error in §6?
3. **Is "the tool as shipped, including its recommended prompt" a legitimate framing?** It would let
   the doctrine block live in the eg arm only, since it is meaningless without the tool. That is
   arguably honest product measurement and arguably the exact asymmetry that sank the earlier
   headline. I have kept it out. I think that is right but it is the single biggest judgement call
   in the whole benchmark.
4. **Is there a token pool none of the five agents is looking at?** My decomposition covers output
   by tool/phase, the post-edit tail, the top-10 sinks, and residual searches. If there is a fifth
   pool, naming it is worth more than anything else in this document.

---

## 11. Artifacts

- `tools/concentration.py` — strictly-gated loader + the §3 arithmetic. Start here.
- `bin/entire-graph-94009ef` — pinned good binary, sha256 `3f7318a82758164a…`.
- `entire-graph-94009ef-ts` — good binary + TS fix, sha256 `d128426e3ab74663…`, verified
  byte-identical on 8 non-TS repos. Patch: `ts-overload.patch` (54 lines, additive).
- `bin/entire-graph-tsoverload` — **do not use**, built 11 commits behind the good base.
- `FINDINGS-2026-08-05.md` — the campaign writeup, including §5, every claim withdrawn and why.
- `tools/phases.py` — LOCATE/ITERATE/POST decomposition. Note the *published* anatomy does not sum
  to its own headline (46.03 vs a stated 37.95 calls); the measured one does.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The load-bearing assumption, tested directly.

Everything in this campaign assumes the graph saves tokens WHEN IT IS USED, and that the
problem is getting the agent to use it. That has never been tested head-on. It is testable
at zero cost: gq_calls.log records the queries each eg session actually sent.

If eg sessions that queried the graph do NOT beat eg sessions that never queried it, the
mechanism is falsified and no amount of invocation engineering can reach the goal.

Observational, not causal -- sessions that query may differ from those that don't. But a
null here is decisive in the negative direction, which is what we need to know.

Strict gate: both arms subtype==success AND non-empty patch.diff.
"""
import json
import os
import glob
import math
import statistics
import collections

SUITE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
SKIP_CELLS = {"FIXSTACK"}


def tokens(u):
    if not u:
        return 0
    return (u.get("input_tokens", 0) + u.get("output_tokens", 0)
            + u.get("cache_read_input_tokens", 0)
            + u.get("cache_creation_input_tokens", 0))


def sess(cell, arm, iid):
    root = f"{SUITE}/results/{cell}_r1_{arm}/{arm}/{iid}"
    if not os.path.isdir(root):
        root = f"{SUITE}/results/{cell}_r1_{arm}/{iid}"
    cc, pd = f"{root}/cc_out.json", f"{root}/patch.diff"
    if not os.path.isfile(cc):
        return None
    try:
        j = json.load(open(cc))
    except Exception:
        return None
    if j.get("subtype") != "success":
        return None
    if not (os.path.isfile(pd) and os.path.getsize(pd) > 0):
        return None
    t = tokens(j.get("usage"))
    if t <= 0:
        return None
    u = j.get("usage") or {}
    return dict(root=root, tok=t, out=u.get("output_tokens", 0),
                turns=j.get("num_turns") or 0, usd=j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0.0)


def ncalls(root):
    """How many real queries did this session send? gq_calls.log is one line per call."""
    p = f"{root}/gq_calls.log"
    if not os.path.isfile(p):
        return 0
    n = 0
    for ln in open(p, errors="replace"):
        ln = ln.strip()
        if not ln:
            continue
        # ignore the agent probing the bare path to discover argv
        n += 1
    return n


def main():
    cells = sorted({os.path.basename(p).rsplit("_r1_", 1)[0]
                    for p in glob.glob(f"{SUITE}/results/*_r1_eg")})
    cells = [c for c in cells if c not in SKIP_CELLS]

    rows = []   # (cell, iid, calls, ratio, egtok, basetok)
    for c in cells:
        eroot = f"{SUITE}/results/{c}_r1_eg/eg"
        if not os.path.isdir(eroot):
            eroot = f"{SUITE}/results/{c}_r1_eg"
        if not os.path.isdir(eroot):
            continue
        for iid in sorted(os.listdir(eroot)):
            e = sess(c, "eg", iid)
            b = sess(c, "baseline", iid)
            if not e or not b:
                continue
            rows.append((c, iid, ncalls(e["root"]), e["tok"] / b["tok"],
                         e["tok"], b["tok"], e["out"], b["out"]))

    if not rows:
        print("no gated pairs")
        return

    used = [r for r in rows if r[2] > 0]
    unused = [r for r in rows if r[2] == 0]

    def summarise(label, rs):
        if not rs:
            print(f"  {label:34s} n=  0")
            return
        g = math.exp(statistics.mean(math.log(r[3]) for r in rs))
        tot = 1 - sum(r[4] for r in rs) / sum(r[5] for r in rs)
        outr = 1 - sum(r[6] for r in rs) / sum(r[7] for r in rs)
        print(f"  {label:34s} n={len(rs):3d}   geomean saving {(1-g)*100:6.1f}%   "
              f"total {tot*100:6.1f}%   output {outr*100:6.1f}%")

    print(f"pooled {len(cells)} cells (FIXSTACK excluded), {len(rows)} gated pairs\n")
    print("DID THE SESSION ACTUALLY QUERY THE GRAPH?")
    summarise("queried at least once", used)
    summarise("never queried", unused)
    print()

    # dose response
    print("DOSE RESPONSE (calls -> saving)")
    buckets = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for r in rows:
        k = r[2]
        b = "0" if k == 0 else "1" if k == 1 else "2" if k == 2 else "3-4" if k <= 4 else "5+"
        buckets[b].append(r)
    for k in ("0", "1", "2", "3-4", "5+"):
        if k in buckets:
            summarise(f"{k} call(s)", buckets[k])
    print()

    # correlation on the sessions that used it
    if len(used) >= 8:
        xs = [r[2] for r in used]
        ys = [math.log(r[3]) for r in used]
        mx, my = statistics.mean(xs), statistics.mean(ys)
        num = sum((x - mx) * (y - my) for x, y in zip(xs, ys))
        den = math.sqrt(sum((x - mx) ** 2 for x in xs) * sum((y - my) ** 2 for y in ys))
        r_ = num / den if den else float("nan")
        print(f"corr(calls, log token ratio) on queried sessions = {r_:+.3f}  n={len(used)}")
        print("  (negative = more calls, fewer tokens = the mechanism works)")
    print()

    # per-cell usage rate, so we can see WHICH cells ever got the tool invoked
    print("USAGE RATE BY CELL")
    percell = collections.defaultdict(lambda: [0, 0])
    for r in rows:
        percell[r[0]][1] += 1
        if r[2] > 0:
            percell[r[0]][0] += 1
    for c in sorted(percell, key=lambda c: -percell[c][0] / max(1, percell[c][1])):
        u, n = percell[c]
        cellrows = [r for r in rows if r[0] == c]
        g = math.exp(statistics.mean(math.log(r[3]) for r in cellrows))
        print(f"  {c:14s} queried {u:2d}/{n:2d} = {u/n*100:5.1f}%   "
              f"cell geomean saving {(1-g)*100:6.1f}%")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

**(i) The graph is not being used as a tool. It is a prompt injection.**

```
208 strictly-gated pairs (FIXSTACK excluded)

`tools/does_calling_help.py` reproduces this. The entire 12.8% is produced by sessions that made

the top-ranked location, a `VERIFY:` command, and a pointer to `eg-q.run`. The agent essentially
never follows the pointer.

This kills "invocation engineering" as a route on its own — invocation was already fixed once
(0.042 → 1.75 calls/session via an argv shim) and **the calls added rather than replaced grep**, so
that cell still cost 9.5%. Plan around the *injected block*, not around getting the agent to call.

**The anomaly worth attacking:** the eg arm is *handed the answer location* and still runs 12.99
LOCATE calls against the baseline's 13.76 — it discards the answer 94% of the time. Retrieval recall
is ~70% @5 (`tools/recall_agent_query.py`), so the injected location is wrong ~30% of the time and
the agent cannot tell which. A rational agent re-verifies every time, collecting no saving on the
70% and paying full price on the 30%. **Calibrated confidence — "trust this one / search yourself" —
is the untested lever that follows directly from this.** A confidence tier was tried on Sonnet
(narrow to 3 when the hit1/hit2 gap ≥ 0.008, widen to 12 and warn otherwise) and was that model's
best config; it has never been tried on Opus under this framing.

**(ii) Every cell in `results/` is fairness-contaminated. The fair number is unknown.**

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Is the search score margin CALIBRATED? ($0, deterministic)

THE MECHANISM THIS TESTS. The eg arm is handed a top-ranked location in its prompt and still
runs 12.99 LOCATE calls (baseline 13.76) -- it discards the answer ~94% of the time. Recall is
~70% @5, so the injected location is wrong about a third of the time and the agent CANNOT TELL
WHICH THIRD. Re-verifying every time is rational: no saving on the 70%, full price on the 30%.

If the score margin separates "rank 1 is gold" from "rank 1 is wrong", we can emit a calibrated
instruction -- "trust this, edit here" vs "uncertain, locate it yourself" -- and buy the locate
phase on the confident subset. If the margin does NOT separate, the route is dead and we learned
it for free.

GATE: some threshold must give precision >= 85% at coverage >= 40%. Below that, an agent acting
on the signal would be misled too often to trust it, and the pool is too small to matter (see
tools/concentration.py -- anything under ~5 pts of total tokens cannot move the goal).

Usage: tools/confidence_calibration.py [--variant title|first2|both] [--limit N]
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

SUITE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
EG = os.environ.get("ENTIRE_GRAPH", f"{SUITE}/bin/entire-graph-94009ef")
WTROOT = "/tmp/recall_wt"
CACHE = os.environ.get("EG_CACHE", f"{SUITE}/.eg_cache")


def gold_files(patch):
    return set(re.findall(r"\+\+\+ b/(\S+)", patch or ""))


def strip(s):
    s = re.sub(r"https?://\S+", " ", s or "")
    s = re.sub(r"`[^`]*`", " ", s)          # code spans often contain the path
    s = re.sub(r"[\w./-]+\.(java|go|rs|py|php|rb|ts|js|c|cpp|h)\b", " ", s)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()


def queries(task, variant):
    ps = (task.get("problem_statement") or "").strip()
    out = {}
    if not ps:
        return out
    lines = [l for l in ps.splitlines() if l.strip()]
    if variant in ("title", "both"):
        out["title"] = strip(lines[0])[:200] if lines else ""
    if variant in ("first2", "both"):
        sents = re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+", strip(ps))
        out["first2"] = " ".join(sents[:2])[:300]
    return {k: v for k, v in out.items() if v}


def search(wt, iid, q, topk=5):
    cmd = [EG, "search", "--query", q, "--repo", wt, "--format", "json",
           "--top-k", str(topk), "--cache-dir", f"{CACHE}/{iid}"]
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900)
        d = json.loads(r.stdout or "{}")
    except Exception:
        return []
    return d.get("results") or []


def auc(pos, neg):
    """Mann-Whitney AUC of margin separating gold@1 from not."""
    if not pos or not neg:
        return float("nan")
    wins = ties = 0
    for a in pos:
        for b in neg:
            if a > b:
                wins += 1
            elif a == b:
                ties += 1
    return (wins + 0.5 * ties) / (len(pos) * len(neg))


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--variant", default="both")
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    os.chdir(SUITE)
    tasks = json.load(open("tasks/rep30_tasks.json"))["instances"]
    if a.limit:
        tasks = tasks[:a.limit]
    if not os.access(EG, os.X_OK):
        sys.exit(f"binary not executable: {EG}")

    rows = []
    print(f"{'instance':32s} {'variant':7s} {'g@1':>4s} {'g@5':>4s} "
          f"{'s1':>8s} {'s2':>8s} {'margin':>7s}")
    for t in tasks:
        iid = t["instance_id"]
        wt = f"{WTROOT}/{iid}"
        if not os.path.isdir(wt):
            continue
        gold = gold_files(t.get("patch", ""))
        if not gold:
            continue
        for vname, q in queries(t, a.variant).items():
            res = search(wt, iid, q)
            if not res:
                continue
            files = [r.get("file_path") for r in res]
            scores = [float(r.get("score") or 0) for r in res]
            g1 = files[0] in gold
            g5 = any(f in gold for f in files)
            s1 = scores[0]
            s2 = scores[1] if len(scores) > 1 else 0.0
            margin = (s1 - s2) / s1 if s1 > 0 else 0.0
            rows.append(dict(iid=iid, variant=vname, g1=g1, g5=g5,
                             s1=s1, s2=s2, margin=margin))
            print(f"  {iid:30s} {vname:7s} {'Y' if g1 else '.':>4s} "
                  f"{'Y' if g5 else '.':>4s} {s1:8.2f} {s2:8.2f} {margin:7.3f}",
                  flush=True)

    if not rows:
        sys.exit("no rows")

    print()
    for vname in sorted({r["variant"] for r in rows}):
        rs = [r for r in rows if r["variant"] == vname]
        n = len(rs)
        h1 = sum(r["g1"] for r in rs)
        h5 = sum(r["g5"] for r in rs)
        print(f"VARIANT {vname}:  n={n}  gold@1 {h1}/{n} = {h1/n*100:.1f}%   "
              f"gold@5 {h5}/{n} = {h5/n*100:.1f}%")
        pos = [r["margin"] for r in rs if r["g1"]]
        neg = [r["margin"] for r in rs if not r["g1"]]
        A = auc(pos, neg)
        print(f"  AUC(margin -> gold@1) = {A:.3f}   "

Two results landed together, and they point the same direction.

**The confidence lever is dead — killed for $0.** Score margin has no calibration whatsoever:

```
AUC(margin -> gold@1) = 0.503        (0.5 = no signal)
mean margin when rank1 IS gold:  0.074
mean margin when rank1 is WRONG: 0.081   <- wrong scores HIGHER
GATE FAIL: no threshold reaches 85% precision at 40% coverage
```

But it surfaced something worse, and more important: **gold@1 is 9/30 = 30%.** The "Top-ranked location for this issue" line injected into every eg prompt is **wrong about 70% of the time**. The agent isn't being irrational by ignoring it — it's correctly distrusting a mostly-wrong pointer.

**And the output-pool decomposition (n=160 pairs, 320 sessions) confirms exactly that, from the other side:**

```
BEFORE first edit:  eg 11,739 vs base 11,784 output tok   -0.4%, CI spans zero
                    pre-edit Bash calls 15.06 vs 15.38    -- not ONE locating turn removed
AFTER  first edit:  -3,173 of the -3,217 total delta      -- 98.6% of the entire win

only two CI-clean pools:  AFTER|build/test  -1,235 [-1745,-724]
                          AFTER|grep         -778 [-1549,-8]
eg is strictly WORSE at:  BEFORE|cat/sed +110 with MORE calls (5.05 vs 4.37)
                          -- the injected file:line CREATES sed-window reads
```

The mechanism, stated plainly: **the locate phase contributes zero. The entire measured saving is post-edit verify/test churn reduction.** The payload answers *"where is the defect"*; the greps the agent still runs are asking *"what are the siblings, the call sites, and the reproduction harness"* — which the payload never contains. In one instance the agent literally `grep -v`s out the file the payload handed it, because it needed call sites.

That reorders the whole plan. Retrieval work — better ranking, the TS fix, recall — targets a phase that is measurably dead even. The live pool is the post-edit one, and there's a specific handle on it: **160/160 of those prompts carried `VERIFY: none validated in this environment`**, and my ledger shows only 2–8 instances per cell ever got a *validated* command. `AFTER|build/test` is 5.83 eg calls vs 7.44 baseline with an unvalidated command; a validated one on all 30 is the untested version of the only lever that's actually winning.

Three agents still running (post-edit tail, top-10 sinks, residual-grep classification). I'm updating the handoff with both results now — including killing the confidence route I proposed to your planner an hour ago, before it wastes their time.

`AFTER|cat/sed` +62, `AFTER|run-script` +34, `AFTER|git` +33. Sum of adverse pools: +371 tok/sess.

Largest single pool in the whole run is `BEFORE|Bash|grep`: **5,082 tok/sess, 16.8% of all eg
output, delta −10, CI [−622,+602]** — dead zero. eg is handed the gold file and symbol and greps
exactly as much as an arm handed nothing.

siblings, the call sites, and the reproduction harness"* — none of which the payload contains. In
`gson-2479` the agent explicitly `grep -v`s out the file the payload gave it, because it needs call
sites. 90/160 eg sessions issue a pre-edit grep naming the payload's own file or symbol.

mean margin when rank1 IS gold  : 0.074
mean margin when rank1 is WRONG : 0.081        <- wrong ranks HIGHER
no threshold reaches precision >=85% at coverage >=40%   GATE FAIL
```

defect. (An earlier run reported 70% recall@5 with laxer query stripping — the discrepancy is the

asserts.)

improvements — targets a phase measured at **−0.4% with the CI through zero**. It is correctness
work, not token work. The live pool is post-edit, and there is a specific untested handle on it:

biggest CI-clean win at 5.83 eg calls vs 7.44 baseline **with an unvalidated command**. Validating it

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""How much is a VALIDATED verify command worth? ($0, from existing sessions)

Post-edit build/test is the only big CI-clean pool (-1,235 tok/sess of a -3,217 total).
Today it runs with `VERIFY: none validated in this environment` in the overwhelming majority
of prompts -- only 2-8 instances per cell ever received a validated command.

This splits eg sessions by whether their OWN prompt carried a validated VERIFY, and compares
each against its matched baseline. If validated sessions beat unvalidated ones, validating on
all 30 is the lever. If not, the post-edit win is coming from something else and we need to
find what.

CAUTION built in: the split is observational, not randomised. A validated command is only
obtainable when localization was right, so `validated` may just be a proxy for `easy/correct
instance`. The script therefore also reports the BASELINE cost of each group -- if baselines
differ, the groups are not comparable and the comparison is confounded.
"""
import json
import os
import glob
import math
import re
import statistics
import collections

SUITE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
SKIP = {"FIXSTACK", "HAIKU30", "MCPPROBE"}
VALIDATED = re.compile(r"\[validated:", re.I)
HASVERIFY = re.compile(r"^VERIFY:", re.M)


def tok(u):
    if not u:
        return 0
    return (u.get("input_tokens", 0) + u.get("output_tokens", 0)
            + u.get("cache_read_input_tokens", 0)
            + u.get("cache_creation_input_tokens", 0))


def sess(cell, arm, iid):
    root = f"{SUITE}/results/{cell}_r1_{arm}/{arm}/{iid}"
    cc, pd = f"{root}/cc_out.json", f"{root}/patch.diff"
    if not os.path.isfile(cc):
        return None
    try:
        j = json.load(open(cc))
    except Exception:
        return None
    if j.get("subtype") != "success":
        return None
    if not (os.path.isfile(pd) and os.path.getsize(pd) > 0):
        return None
    t = tok(j.get("usage"))
    if t <= 0:
        return None
    p = f"{root}/prompt.txt"
    txt = open(p, errors="replace").read() if os.path.isfile(p) else ""
    return dict(tok=t, turns=j.get("num_turns") or 0,
                usd=j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0.0,
                validated=bool(VALIDATED.search(txt)),
                hasverify=bool(HASVERIFY.search(txt)))


def summarise(label, rs):
    if not rs:
        print(f"  {label:32s} n=  0")
        return None
    g = math.exp(statistics.mean(math.log(r["ratio"]) for r in rs))
    tot = 1 - sum(r["eg"] for r in rs) / sum(r["ba"] for r in rs)
    bmean = statistics.mean(r["ba"] for r in rs)
    bturn = statistics.mean(r["bturns"] for r in rs)
    print(f"  {label:32s} n={len(rs):3d}   geomean saving {(1-g)*100:6.1f}%   "
          f"total {tot*100:6.1f}%   | baseline {bmean/1e6:5.2f}M tok, {bturn:5.1f} turns")
    return (1 - g)


def main():
    cells = sorted({os.path.basename(p).rsplit("_r1_", 1)[0]
                    for p in glob.glob(f"{SUITE}/results/*_r1_eg")})
    cells = [c for c in cells if c not in SKIP]
    rows = []
    for c in cells:
        eroot = f"{SUITE}/results/{c}_r1_eg/eg"
        if not os.path.isdir(eroot):
            continue
        for iid in sorted(os.listdir(eroot)):
            e = sess(c, "eg", iid)
            b = sess(c, "baseline", iid)
            if not e or not b:
                continue
            rows.append(dict(cell=c, iid=iid, eg=e["tok"], ba=b["tok"],
                             ratio=e["tok"] / b["tok"], validated=e["validated"],
                             hasverify=e["hasverify"], bturns=b["turns"],
                             egturns=e["turns"]))
    if not rows:
        print("no gated pairs")
        return

    print(f"pooled {len(cells)} cells, {len(rows)} gated pairs "
          f"(FIXSTACK/HAIKU30/MCPPROBE excluded)\n")
    print("SPLIT BY WHETHER THE eg PROMPT CARRIED A **VALIDATED** VERIFY COMMAND")
    v = [r for r in rows if r["validated"]]
    nv = [r for r in rows if not r["validated"]]
    a = summarise("validated VERIFY", v)
    b = summarise("VERIFY present but NOT validated", [r for r in nv if r["hasverify"]])
    c_ = summarise("no VERIFY line at all", [r for r in nv if not r["hasverify"]])
    print()
    if a is not None and b is not None:
        print(f"  validated minus unvalidated = {(a-b)*100:+.1f} points")
    print()

    print("CONFOUND CHECK -- are the groups comparable?")
    for lbl, rs in (("validated", v), ("unvalidated", nv)):
        if rs:
            print(f"  {lbl:14s} baseline mean {statistics.mean(r['ba'] for r in rs)/1e6:5.2f}M tok, "
                  f"{statistics.mean(r['bturns'] for r in rs):5.1f} turns   n={len(rs)}")
    print("  (if baselines differ materially the split is confounded -- a validated command is")
    print("   only obtainable when localization was right, so it may proxy for 'easy instance')")
    print()

    print("WHICH INSTANCES EVER GOT A VALIDATED COMMAND")
    per = collections.Counter(r["iid"] for r in v)
    tot = collections.Counter(r["iid"] for r in rows)
    for iid in sorted(tot):
        if per[iid]:
            print(f"  {iid:34s} {per[iid]:2d}/{tot[iid]:2d} cells")
    print(f"  -> {len(per)} of {len(tot)} distinct instances ever produced a validated command")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
