Four agents in. The news is bad, then genuinely good.

**The bad — the config tuning was largely an illusion.** Payload-identity check across cells:

```
RUNG2F/G/H/I/J/K/L/M + HAIKU30 are BYTE-IDENTICAL on every shared instance.
Nine "different configs" are ONE config.

RUNG2J vs RUNG2K: 29/29 byte-identical prompts, same binary, same flags,
same CLI, zero attrition in both  ->  15.2% vs 3.6%.  Same cell, twice.
```

**RUNG2I — the 28.9% cell — is contaminated in the direction that flatters us:** 14 of 28 *baseline* transcripts hit ENOSPC, 0 of 28 eg. The control arm was handicapped. Clean subset: 22.1%, n=14. (RUNG2H is contaminated the opposite way, 6/16 eg.)

**Best genuinely fair config, pooled n=80: saving 9.3%, 95% CI [−0.4%, 17.8%]** — and still inflated by the eg-only VERIFY/clamp/`verify.run` apparatus worth ~+7pt on the 19% of sessions carrying it. No fair config's point estimate is above 20%; no pooled fair CI reaches 25%.

**The good — and it's the reason I'm not stopping.** Because nine cells were one config, *the config space is essentially unexplored*. Look at what every cell ever run had set:

```
EG_TIER=0  EG_DEEP=0  EG_DEF_ONLY=0  EG_LITERALS=0  EG_CONF_TIER=0  EG_ESCALATE=0
```

**Every enrichment block was OFF in every cell.** The tool's own help says `search` returns RELATED SITES, the COVERING TEST plus ALSO-COVERING tests, and SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL — "the sweep, so you need no grep". All disabled. The eg arm got a single `Top-ranked location:` line.

Now put that against the output decomposition: the residual pre-edit greps are asking **"what are the siblings, the call sites, and the reproduction harness"** — which is *precisely* what RELATED SITES, SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL and COVERING TEST provide. The one cell that turned the full payload on, FULLPF, reads **18.0% total vs 11.0% for the minimal payload** (n=11, interval wide).

Also worth correcting: the tail lead didn't reproduce (best AUC 0.717, not 0.945), and tail is only 10–28% of the saving. Combined with agent 1, the saving lives **between the first and last edit** — the edit-iteration loop — not in locate and not in the tail.

So the route is: run the payload the tool actually ships by default, at proper n, with the clean binary. That's evidence-backed, unexplored, and cheap to gate offline first. Doing that now.

The final agent just landed the decisive result, and it **overrides the config I was about to spend on**. Two independent measurements have now converged:

```
TOP-10 instances, 67 pairs:
  validated VERIFY   n=14   saving 27.1%  CI [12.0, 39.0]
  unvalidated        n=53   saving 10.4%  CI [ 1.5, 18.6]
  within-instance:   +27.6 pt,  4/4 positive
  (my own verify_pool.py, independently: +12.2 pt within-instance)

Mechanism is DISJOINT:
  VER cells:   class-b (verify-removable) -13.15 pts   class-a (retrieval) -0.41  <- retrieval does nothing
  noVER cells: class-a -5.96              class-b -0.76                            <- verify does nothing

COVERAGE IS THE CONSTRAINT: only 20 of 97 eg prompts carry a validated VERIFY.
```

And retrieval is close to irrelevant: the injected top-1 hits a gold file in **13 of 97** sessions, HIT saves 17.4% vs MISS 13.3% — not significant. Three of the ten top-1 hits are *test files*. Pre-edit locating is only 17.9% of the money.

So I'm pivoting off payload enrichment. The smoke test ran clean ($0.49), but MAXPF as designed optimizes the lever that measurably does nothing.

**The real constraint is mechanical, and it's mostly $0 to fix.** Verdict distribution across all validation attempts:

```
unvalidatable   182 (45%)  <- command won't RUN: toolchain/env. NO gold data needed to fix.
non-covering    165 (40%)  <- runs but passes pre-fix: needs correct localization
validated-fails  56 (14%)  <- ships
```

The 45% `unvalidatable` bucket is pure provisioning engineering with no answer leak — pylint went from failing to validated purely by using `.venv/bin/python -m pytest` instead of `python -m pytest`. Named blockers: fmt (cmake), docusaurus (yarn jest), lombok (ant), hugo-12204, caddy.

One honest caveat before I chase it: that agent's own ceiling projection is **23–30%** with every mechanism firing — 25% sits inside that band, but not comfortably. Launching four parallel toolchain agents now, strictly forbidden from touching gold data:

# Pre-registration — VERCOV cell

Written **before** the cell runs. Committed so the prediction cannot be adjusted after seeing the
result. Per the benchmark's own rule: an out-of-sample prediction that survives is worth more than
ten post-hoc explanations.

## Hypothesis

Token saving on rep30/Opus is driven by **validated-VERIFY coverage**, not by payload retrieval
quality. Raising coverage from today's 20/97 (21%) toward ~all should move total saving from
~10–13% toward the 23–30% ceiling band.

Basis (both measured on existing sessions, $0, no new spend):

```
top-10 pool, 67 pairs   validated 27.1% [12.0,39.0] (n=14) vs unvalidated 10.4% [1.5,18.6] (n=53)
verify_pool.py          validated 20.0%              (n=24) vs unvalidated  9.5%           (n=165)
within-instance         +27.6 pt (4/4 positive, top-10)  |  +12.2 pt [-18.5,+42.8] (n=7, mine)
disjointness            VER cells: class-b -13.15 / class-a -0.41
                        noVER cells: class-a -5.96 / class-b -0.76
```

## Prediction

With `U` = unvalidated saving (~10%), `d` = the within-instance validated effect, `C` = achieved
coverage, predicted total saving ≈ `U + C·d`.

| coverage achieved | d = +12 pt (my low estimate) | d = +28 pt (top-10 high estimate) |
|---|---|---|
| 0.50 | 16.0% | 24.0% |
| 0.70 | 18.4% | 29.6% |
| 0.90 | 20.8% | 35.2% |
| 1.00 | 22.0% | 38.0% |

**Point prediction: coverage ~0.70 and d ~ +18 pt → total saving ≈ 22.6%.**
**Falsification band: 14% – 30%.** A result outside that band means the model is wrong, not that
the config needs tuning.

**25% requires coverage ≥ ~0.80 AND d at the upper half of its range.** I am stating in advance that
this is not the modal outcome — the honest ceiling band from the top-10 decomposition is 23–30%, and
25% sits inside it without margin.

## The decisive internal test (free of every cross-cell confound)

Within this single cell, split the eg sessions on whether their own prompt carried
`[validated: runs, fails pre-fix]`, and compare each against its own matched baseline:

- **CONFIRMS** if the validated subgroup beats the unvalidated subgroup by ≥ 8 points.
- **REFUTES** if the gap is ≤ 0 — the lever is dead regardless of what the headline says, and the
  ~+27 pt cross-cell figure was the baseline-length confound all along.

This test is what the cell is really for. The headline number is secondary, because a single
30-instance cell cannot resolve better than ~±20 pt (measured: RUNG2J vs RUNG2K, byte-identical
config, 15.2% vs 3.6%).

## Gates — checked before the aggregate is read

| # | check | pass | on fail |
|---|---|---|---|
| G0 | every eg session has non-empty `prefetch.payload` | 30/30 | void those instances — an empty payload is a mislabelled baseline |
| G1 | validated-VERIFY coverage | report actual; ≥0.50 to be worth reading | if <0.30 the cell tests nothing new |
| G2 | prompt symmetry: no generic methodology in one arm | 0 differing lines outside tool payload | cell void |
| G3 | `ANTI_HARNESS` empty; `verify.run` present in BOTH arms | yes | cell void |
| G4 | ENOSPC per arm, **counted from transcripts not `*.log`** | 0/0, or symmetric | discard contaminated arm |
| G5 | censoring (`error_max_turns`) symmetric | within 2 | note as right-censoring |
| G6 | no oracle leak: gold path / FAIL_TO_PASS absent from eg prompts | 0/30 | cell void |
| G7 | memory/swap not exhausted during run | swap < 80% | re-run; load pressure flips result signs |

## Scoring, fixed in advance

- Strict gate: both arms `subtype==success` AND non-empty `patch.diff`, dropped **symmetrically**.
- Primary: paired geomean over instances + instance-level bootstrap 95% CI. Report **total
  (Σeg/Σbaseline) alongside**, never instead.
- Report cache_read / cache_creation / output **separately** — cost is not tokens, and which class
  moved is the finding.
- No sub-group reads on n<8. No config selection across cells.
- To *claim* ≥25% needs a measured ≈31.4% at this instrument's noise. A point estimate of 25% with a
  CI spanning 5–45% is reported as exactly that, not as "goal met".

## What I will report if it fails

The negative, plainly, with the interval — plus the coverage actually achieved, so the next attempt
knows whether the lever was tested or merely approximated.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Score one cell honestly, and run the pre-registered gates.

Usage: tools/score_cell.py TAG [TAG2 ...]

Implements exactly what PREREG-VERCOV.md fixed in advance:
  - strict symmetric gate (both arms success + non-empty patch.diff)
  - paired geomean + instance-level bootstrap CI, AND total, both reported
  - token classes separately (cost is not tokens; which class moved is the finding)
  - the decisive internal test: validated-VERIFY subgroup vs unvalidated, WITHIN this cell,
    which is free of the cross-cell baseline-length confound that inflates the +27pt figure
  - gates G0-G6, including the empty-payload guard that catches an eg arm silently degraded
    to a baseline
"""
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import math
import random
import statistics

SUITE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
VALID = re.compile(r"\[validated:", re.I)
HASVER = re.compile(r"^VERIFY:", re.M)
CLASSES = ("input_tokens", "output_tokens",
           "cache_read_input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens")


def load(tag, arm):
    root = f"{SUITE}/results/{tag}_r1_{arm}/{arm}"
    if not os.path.isdir(root):
        root = f"{SUITE}/results/{tag}_r1_{arm}"
    out = {}
    if not os.path.isdir(root):
        return out
    for iid in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        d = f"{root}/{iid}"
        cc, pd = f"{d}/cc_out.json", f"{d}/patch.diff"
        if not os.path.isfile(cc):
            continue
        try:
            j = json.load(open(cc))
        except Exception:
            out[iid] = dict(bad="CORRUPT_CC_OUT")
            continue
        u = j.get("usage") or {}
        rec = dict(
            subtype=j.get("subtype"), turns=j.get("num_turns") or 0,
            usd=j.get("total_cost_usd") or 0.0,
            patch=os.path.isfile(pd) and os.path.getsize(pd) > 0,
            payload=os.path.getsize(f"{d}/prefetch.payload")
            if os.path.isfile(f"{d}/prefetch.payload") else 0,
            **{c: u.get(c, 0) for c in CLASSES})
        rec["tok"] = sum(rec[c] for c in CLASSES)
        p = f"{d}/prompt.txt"
        t = open(p, errors="replace").read() if os.path.isfile(p) else ""
        rec["validated"] = bool(VALID.search(t))
        rec["hasverify"] = bool(HASVER.search(t))
        rec["prompt"] = t
        out[iid] = rec
    return out


def boot(ratios, n=20000, seed=12345):
    if len(ratios) < 3:
        return (float("nan"), float("nan"))
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    gs = []
    for _ in range(n):
        s = [rnd.choice(ratios) for _ in ratios]
        gs.append(math.exp(sum(math.log(x) for x in s) / len(s)))
    gs.sort()
    return (1 - gs[int(.975 * n)], 1 - gs[int(.025 * n)])


def report(tag):
    eg, ba = load(tag, "eg"), load(tag, "baseline")
    all_i = sorted(set(eg) | set(ba))
    rows, dropped = [], []
    for i in all_i:
        e, b = eg.get(i), ba.get(i)
        why = None
        if not e or not b:
            why = "missing arm"
        elif e.get("bad") or b.get("bad"):
            why = "corrupt cc_out"
        elif e["subtype"] != "success" or b["subtype"] != "success":

content.text:
Scorer validates exactly against the independent read — 15.23% vs the agent's 15.2%, total 16.92% vs 16.9%, turns match. It's trustworthy for the real cell.

Two things that came out of the validation run worth noting:

**RUNG2J — the best fair cell — had validated-VERIFY coverage of just 2/29 (7%).** So the lever we're now chasing was essentially absent from every cell ever run. That's consistent with the prediction rather than undermining it: 7% coverage → 15.2%, and the model says 70% coverage → ~22.6%.

**The token class that moves is cache_read (−17.2%), with output at −14.1%.** That matters for how the result gets reported — cache_read is ~20× cheaper than output, which is why cost saving (14.3%) lands below token saving (16.9%). Any headline has to say which.

Current state, all four VERIFY agents still running:

| piece | status |
|---|---|
| Clean TS binary on the correct base | done, verified byte-identical on 8 non-TS repos |
| `run_maxpf.sh` full-payload config | built, broken flags pinned off, empty-payload guard added |
| Pre-registration with falsification band | committed — **`PREREG-VERCOV.md`**, band 14–30%, point prediction 22.6% |
| Cell scorer + decisive internal test | built and validated against a known cell |
| Validated-VERIFY coverage fixes | 4 agents in flight (JVM / JS-TS / native / Go-Py-Rb-PHP) |
| Memory headroom for the cell | **blocked** — swap at 9.1/10.2 GB while agents are resident |

The decisive test is pre-registered and independent of the headline: **within the single cell, does the validated subgroup beat the unvalidated one by ≥8 points?** If yes, the lever is real regardless of what the aggregate reads. If the gap is ≤0, the +27pt cross-cell figure was the baseline-length confound all along and I'll say so.

I'm holding the cell until the agents finish and memory recovers — starting it now would bake in the load-pressure confound that has flipped result signs on this benchmark before.

Doing the one measurement that bounds the whole plan, and that no agent is covering: **how often can the tool legitimately find the right test at all?** If the binary's own covering-test derivation can only reach the gold test 30% of the time, validated coverage is capped there and 25% is out of reach regardless of toolchain fixes.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""CEILING on legitimate validated-VERIFY coverage. ($0, deterministic)

WHY THIS BOUNDS EVERYTHING. Validated VERIFY is the measured #1 lever (+12 to +27 points), and
coverage is only 20/97. Four agents are fixing the TOOLCHAIN half of the problem (45% of failures
are `unvalidatable` -- the command will not run). But the other half is `non-covering`: the command
runs and PASSES pre-fix, i.e. it does not exercise the defect. Fixing that requires naming the RIGHT
test -- and the tool must derive that from its own coverage edges, never from FAIL_TO_PASS.

So: how often does the tool's own COVERING TEST / VERIFY output actually point at the gold test?
That is the ceiling on how far coverage can be pushed WITHOUT cheating. If it is 30%, then no amount
of toolchain engineering gets coverage above ~30% + whatever the toolchain half contributes, and the
23-30% projection collapses.

FAIL_TO_PASS is used ONLY to score the answer after the fact. It is never an input to the
derivation -- that would leak the answer into the tool arm and invalidate the benchmark.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

SUITE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
EG = os.environ.get("ENTIRE_GRAPH", f"{SUITE}/bin/entire-graph-94009ef-ts")
WTROOT = "/tmp/recall_wt"
CACHE = f"{SUITE}/.eg_cache"


def strip(s):
    s = re.sub(r"https?://\S+", " ", s or "")
    s = re.sub(r"`[^`]*`", " ", s)
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip()


def query(task):
    ps = (task.get("problem_statement") or "").strip()
    lines = [l for l in ps.splitlines() if l.strip()]
    return strip(lines[0])[:200] if lines else ""


def gold_test_tokens(task):
    """Distinctive identifiers from FAIL_TO_PASS -- DIAGNOSTIC ONLY, never an input."""
    toks = set()
    for entry in (task.get("FAIL_TO_PASS") or []):
        for part in re.split(r"[^\w]+", str(entry)):
            if len(part) >= 5 and not part.islower():
                toks.add(part)
            elif len(part) >= 8:
                toks.add(part)
    return toks


def main():
    os.chdir(SUITE)
    tasks = json.load(open("tasks/rep30_tasks.json"))["instances"]
    if not os.access(EG, os.X_OK):
        sys.exit(f"binary not executable: {EG}")

    hit = miss = noverify = 0
    print(f"{'instance':32s} {'lang':11s} {'VERIFY?':>7s} {'covers gold?':>12s}  derived command")
    for t in tasks:
        iid = t["instance_id"]
        wt = f"{WTROOT}/{iid}"
        if not os.path.isdir(wt):
            continue
        q = query(t)
        if not q:
            continue
        cmd = [EG, "search", "--query", q, "--repo", wt, "--format", "json",
               "--top-k", "5", "--cache-dir", f"{CACHE}/{iid}"]
        try:
            r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=900)
            d = json.loads(r.stdout or "{}")
        except Exception:
            d = {}
        vc = (d.get("verify_command") or "").strip()
        # every file the payload names, plus the verify command text
        surface = vc + " " + " ".join(
            (h.get("file_path") or "") + " " + (h.get("qualified_name") or "")
            for h in (d.get("results") or []))
        gold = gold_test_tokens(t)
        covers = bool(gold) and any(g in surface for g in gold)
        if not vc:
            noverify += 1
            v = "no"
        else:
            v = "yes"
        if vc:
            hit += 1 if covers else 0
            miss += 0 if covers else 1
        print(f"  {iid:30s} {t.get('language','?'):11s} {v:>7s} "
              f"{('YES' if covers else 'no'):>12s}  {vc[:60]}")

    tot = hit + miss
    print(f"\nVERIFY command derived at all: {tot}/{tot+noverify}")
    if tot:
        print(f"  names something from the gold test: {hit}/{tot} = {hit/tot*100:.0f}%")
    print(f"\nCEILING READ: even with every toolchain fixed, `non-covering` can only be cured on the")
    print(f"instances where the tool independently points at the right test. That is the number above.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()


**25% is reachable only at the very top of the effect range.** I'm stating that now rather than after the run, because it's what the pre-registration is for. The honest expectation is high-teens to low-twenties, with 25% as the optimistic edge.

The 12 recoverable instances split cleanly: 3 where no build manifest was found at all (micropython, lombok, django — pure toolchain, agents are on it), and 9 where test selection picked the wrong package (needs the graph's coverage edges, not the top-ranked symbol's directory).

FULLPF, the only full-payload cell, read **18.0% total** with *zero* validated VERIFY. So the full payload raises the floor `U` from ~10% to plausibly ~18%, and coverage adds on top:

```
U = 18% (full payload),    C=0.54  ->  24.5 - 33.0%   <- both levers, which is what MAXPF+coverage is
```

That is the coherent route to the goal, and it's the configuration already built. Caveat held honestly: FULLPF's 18.0% is n=11 with CI [−20.5, 38.4] — directional, not established.

## 7e. TWO TRAPS THAT WOULD HAVE SILENTLY RUINED A CELL

Both were caught by smoke-testing a config before spending on it. Both are the kind of thing that
produces a clean-looking number that is simply wrong, so they are worth more to you than any result
in this document.

**Trap 1 — the enrichment flags are unimplemented, and failing OPEN.** `tools/eg-q` shells out to
`_eglit.py`, `_egsiblings.py`, `_egcallees.py`, `_eganchor.py` for `EG_LITERALS`, `EG_SIBLINGS`,
`EG_CALLEES`, `EG_ANCHOR`. **All four files are absent from `tools/`.** Setting any to 1 makes the
search emit nothing: `prefetch.payload` is 0 bytes, the injected block is empty, and the eg arm runs
as a baseline **with a smaller prompt than the cells it is being compared against**. There is no
error — the pipeline just yields nothing. A $0.49 one-instance smoke test caught it; a ~$160 cell
would have reported a confident, meaningless number.
→ `tools/run_maxpf.sh` now pins all four off and appends any empty-payload instance to
`results/<TAG>.empty_payload` at run time.

**Trap 2 — the BINARY ships its own copy of the anti-harness clamp.** `tools/_pf_verify.py` sets
`ANTI_HARNESS = ''`, and I verified that before launching. It was not sufficient: with
`O35_VERIFY_ONLY=0` (full payload) the binary's *native* VERIFY block passes through unfiltered,
including:

> `run it ONCE after editing; if it fails, fix the code and re-run THIS command.`
> `do not build an alternative test harness, hand-assemble a classpath, or re-verify by reverting`
> `and reapplying the edit.`

The older cells carried that in 3–8 of 30 prompts. Delivering the full payload puts it in **~30/30,
against 0/30 baseline** — the exact one-armed-methodology asymmetry that moved a published −35% to
+9.1% when it was removed. Caught by reading the first live prompt, not the config.

The fix is a filter (`O35_STRIP_ADVICE=1`, `tools/eg-q`) that removes the generic *methodology*
sentences and keeps the derived *command* and its `targets` line. Verified: advice lines 3 → 0,
`VERIFY:` retained, payload 4594 → 4390 bytes.

**The rule this generalises to: verify fairness in the PROMPT THAT SHIPPED, never in the config that
was supposed to produce it.** A tool that emits its own advice can re-introduce an asymmetry you
already disabled one layer up.

**Ceiling measured while the cell ran** (`tools/verify_ceiling.py`): the tool derives a VERIFY
command on 30/30, but the command's scope contains the gold test on only **18/30 = 60%** — 11 whole
-suite (necessarily covering), 7 correctly scoped, 9 scoped to the *wrong* package, 3 with no build
manifest at all. And on **11 of those 12 failures the graph's `coverage_note` is empty**, so the
gap cannot be closed by wiring up information the tool already has — the coverage edges do not
exist there. With execution fixed to ~90%, coverage tops out near 0.60 × 0.90 ≈ **0.54**, which puts
validated-VERIFY alone at `10% + 0.54·d` → **16.5–25.1%**. 25% only at the top of the effect range.

Read it. It's a good plan, and one part of it is **exactly right in a way that solves the blocker my agents just hit** — so let me be concrete rather than defensive.

**What my agents just found (independently, JVM and JS):** `validated-fails` is *structurally unreachable* on these repos. In SWE-bench the gold test ships in `test_patch`, which is never applied to the pristine tree — so **no build-file-derived command can fail pre-fix**. The only instances that fire are ones where the repo's own suite is already broken for unrelated reasons. JVM agent: "all three repos are green at their base commits." JS agent: "firing rate is largely a function of how flaky a repo's own suite already is, not of command derivation quality." So the VERIFY-coverage lever I was chasing **cannot be raised by engineering**. That's a real dead end, found for $0.

**V6's S4 is the way out of it.** `entire graph verify` (db24f74) is *delta-not-state* — it compares post-edit against a **pre-edit baseline** instead of requiring a pre-fix failure. On a green repo that's the only primitive that can work. And it targets precisely the pool I measured today as the *only* CI-clean win: `AFTER|build/test`, −1,235 tok/sess [−1745,−724], with test/build at 10.0 calls/session.

And I've found why it has never fired. The harness already supports it (`O35_ADJUDICATED=1`, and it's **symmetric** — `ADJ_DIR` is TAG-scoped not arm-scoped, so both arms get the wrapper). But Round 16 gated it:

The Round-16 rationale for tightening was sound on its own terms — if the suite passes both before and after, the verdict is "NO EFFECT", zero *correctness* information. But my measurement says the win isn't correctness detection, it's **suppressing improvised harnesses and terminating the verify loop**, and a command that merely runs does that. Relaxing the gate to include `non-covering` (command runs and passes = a perfectly good delta baseline) takes adjudication from ~14% to ~60% of instances.

input.script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'eg-binary-defect-fixes',
  description: 'Diagnose and fix four measured entire-graph defects that cap the VERIFY lever',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Diagnose', detail: 'four read-only investigations of the graph source' },
    { title: 'Fix', detail: 'implement each fix in an isolated worktree, with tests' },
    { title: 'Verify', detail: 'adversarial review + integration assessment' },
  ],
}

const CONTEXT = `
REPO: /Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-graph  (Go, tree-sitter via CGO)
  build: go build -o entire-graph ./cmd/entire-graph
  test:  go test ./internal/sem/     (full suite ~44s, 1976 tests, MUST stay green)
  Logic lives in internal/sem (parsing/graph/search) and internal/cli.
  Current best commit: db24f74 (adds \`entire graph verify\`). Pinned-good older build: 94009ef.
  CONTRACT RULES that must not break: schema 1.x frozen and additive-only; provider is NO-EGRESS
  (never add network calls); compound-v1 symbol IDs stable across ordinary edits; unparseable files
  surface as machine-readable partial failures, never silent drops.

BENCHMARK CONTEXT (measured today, do not re-derive):
  30 SWE-bench Multilingual instances; clean worktrees at /tmp/recall_wt/<instance_id>.
  Task metadata (incl. gold patch + FAIL_TO_PASS) at
  /Users/suhaan/graphmark-bench/agentic-swebench/tasks/rep30_tasks.json
  Prebuilt graphs at /Users/suhaan/graphmark-bench/agentic-swebench/graphs/<iid>/
  Index cache at /Users/suhaan/graphmark-bench/agentic-swebench/.eg_cache/<iid>
  CACHE TRAP: the index cache is TREE-keyed, not binary-keyed. A/B two builds without a SEPARATE
  --cache-dir each and the second silently returns the first's results. This has already cost this
  project real money.

  MEASURED FACTS:
  - The tool derives a VERIFY command on 30/30, but the command's scope contains the gold test on
    only 18/30 (60%): 11 whole-suite, 7 correctly scoped, 9 scoped to the WRONG package, 3 with no
    build manifest. 60% is the hard ceiling on this benchmark's single biggest token lever.
  - On 11 of those 12 failures the search JSON's \`coverage_note\` is EMPTY.
  - Rank-1 is a gold file on only ~30% of instances (9/30).
  - 3 of the 10 most expensive instances have a TEST FILE at rank 1 (bat-2260, hugo-12204, fmt-2457).
  - caddy-5995: top-1 is modules/caddyhttp/replacer.go in 9/9 cells; gold is replacer.go at the
    REPO ROOT. Same-basename collision.

FAIRNESS RULE (absolute): gold patches / FAIL_TO_PASS may be read ONLY to SCORE a result after the
fact. They must NEVER be an input to ranking, derivation, or any heuristic you write. A fix that
consults oracle data is worthless and invalidates the benchmark.

OUTPUT STYLE: caveman-terse, data over prose. Always state n. Report honestly when something cannot
be fixed and why.
`

phase('Diagnose')

const DIAGS = [
  {
    key: 'coverage-edges',
    prompt: `INVESTIGATE: why is \`coverage_note\` empty for most instances, and can test<->code coverage
edges be derived more widely?

\`entire graph search --format json\` returns a \`coverage_note\` object (fields when populated:
symbol, total, peers, more, file_path). On apache__lucene-13170 it is populated and correct. On 11 of
12 instances where VERIFY test-selection fails it is EMPTY. This is the single highest-value defect:
coverage_note feeds the derived VERIFY command, which is the benchmark's biggest token lever.

Do this:
1. Find where coverage_note is produced in internal/sem (grep coverage, covering, peers). Report
   exact file:line and the derivation algorithm.
2. Determine the precise precondition that makes it empty: missing relation type, language gap,
   naming heuristic (TestFoo <-> Foo), test-file detection gap, or index profile?
3. Test empirically across at least 10 of the 30 worktrees with a SEPARATE --cache-dir. Table:
   instance, language, coverage_note populated?, why not.
4. Propose the smallest correct change and estimate how many of the 12 failing instances it fixes.
   Be concrete about the algorithm; do not hand-wave.
Report findings only. Do NOT edit code in this phase.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'test-rank',
    prompt: `INVESTIGATE: why do TEST FILES rank #1, and where is the demotion logic?

3 of the 10 most expensive instances have a test file as rank-1 (sharkdp__bat-2260 ->
tests/integration_tests.rs; gohugoio__hugo-12204 -> tpl/tplimpl/render_hook_integration_test.go;
fmtlib__fmt-2457 -> test/ranges-test.cc). When the payload points at a test instead of the code, the
injected "Top-ranked location" is wrong AND the derived VERIFY command scopes to the wrong place.

Do this:
1. Find the ranking pipeline in internal/sem (scoring, signal weights). Report file:line where a
   hit's score is assembled and whether any test-path penalty exists today.
2. There is a harness-side EG_DROP_TESTS flag and an _istest helper -- find the binary's own
   equivalent and report whether it is on by default.
3. Reproduce all 3 cases with the pinned binary (SEPARATE --cache-dir) and show the score breakdown
   for the test hit vs the correct code hit. Exactly which signal puts the test on top?
4. Propose the smallest change. CAUTION: tests are sometimes legitimately the right answer (the
   agent may need to read the covering test), so blanket exclusion is wrong -- propose a demotion
   that keeps them available but off rank 1, and say how to tell the two cases apart.
Report findings only. Do NOT edit code in this phase.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'basename-collision',
    prompt: `INVESTIGATE: the same-basename collision and path-prior defects generally.

caddyserver__caddy-5995: rank-1 is modules/caddyhttp/replacer.go in 9 of 9 cells. Gold is
replacer.go at the REPO ROOT (symbol Replacer.replace). Both share a basename. The problem statement
says "uri replace".

Do this:
1. Find how path signals contribute to ranking in internal/sem (grep path prior, path score,
   basename). Report file:line and the formula.
2. Reproduce on /tmp/recall_wt/caddyserver__caddy-5995 with a SEPARATE --cache-dir. Print top 5 hits
   with score breakdowns for a realistic agent query from the issue's first sentence (strip
   URLs/code spans; do NOT use the gold path).
3. Determine why the nested file outranks the root one: path-depth, directory-name match,
   symbol-count density, or something else?
4. Check whether this GENERALISES: scan the other 29 instances for cases where a gold file shares a
   basename with a higher-ranked non-gold file. Report how many. A one-instance fix is worth far
   less than a class fix -- say honestly which this is.
5. Propose the smallest correct change.
Report findings only. Do NOT edit code in this phase.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'missing-helpers',
    prompt: `INVESTIGATE: four helper scripts referenced but absent, and whether the binary can do their
job natively.

/Users/suhaan/graphmark-bench/agentic-swebench/tools/eg-q shells out to _eglit.py, _egsiblings.py,
_egcallees.py, _eganchor.py for EG_LITERALS / EG_SIBLINGS / EG_CALLEES / EG_ANCHOR. ALL FOUR ARE
ABSENT. Setting any flag to 1 makes search emit NOTHING (0-byte payload) with no error.

Documented jobs (from eg-q comments):
  EG_ANCHOR   -- resolve BARE locator hits: a naked path:line with no symbol and no body
  EG_SIBLINGS -- definition pointers for in-repo identifiers appearing in the payload
  EG_CALLEES  -- under each bodied hit, the in-repo symbols that body CALLS
  EG_LITERALS -- the SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL sweep

Do this:
1. Search git history in BOTH /Users/suhaan/devenv/entire-graph and /Users/suhaan/graphmark-bench for
   these filenames (git log --all --diff-filter=D --name-only; git show any deleting commit). Were
   they ever committed? Recover if so.
2. Independently: determine which jobs the BINARY already does natively. Inspect
   \`entire graph search --format json\` schema; check --reference-blocks (container-map,
   signature-types, type-card) and the SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL block. Which flags are redundant with
   native capability, and which are a real gap?
3. Measured relevance: 29% of the tool arm's residual greps searched INSIDE a file the payload
   already returned; 25% re-found a symbol the payload already contained. Worked examples the agents
   needed: enclosing symbol name for a bare path:line; member index of the payload file's class;
   overload set in a named header; import/package headers. Map each onto native capability or a gap.
4. Recommend: recover, reimplement natively in the binary, or drop. Justify with the measurement.
Report findings only. Do NOT edit code in this phase.`,
  },
]

const diagnoses = await parallel(DIAGS.map(d => () =>
  agent(CONTEXT + '\n' + d.prompt, { label: 'diag:' + d.key, phase: 'Diagnose' })
    .then(r => ({ key: d.key, report: r }))
    .catch(() => null)))

const good = diagnoses.filter(Boolean).filter(g => g.report)
log('diagnoses complete: ' + good.map(g => g.key).join(', '))

phase('Fix')

const fixes = await parallel(good.map(g => () => agent(CONTEXT + `
You are implementing a fix in an ISOLATED git worktree of entire-graph. Work from commit db24f74.

A diagnostic pass on "${g.key}" produced this report. Treat its file:line references as leads to
VERIFY, not as gospel -- re-check anything load-bearing before building on it:

--- DIAGNOSTIC REPORT ---
${g.report}
--- END REPORT ---

Do this:
1. Implement the smallest correct change the report recommends. If the report concluded NO fix is
   warranted or possible, do NOT invent one -- say so and stop. A confident wrong fix is far worse
   than none here.
2. Add a regression test in internal/sem that FAILS without your change and PASSES with it. PROVE
   it: run the test against the stashed and unstashed tree, paste both outcomes. A test that passes
   either way is worthless.
3. Run the FULL suite: go test ./internal/sem/ -- must stay green (1976 tests). Paste the tail.
4. Build the binary and re-measure the specific defect on the affected rep30 worktrees, using a
   SEPARATE --cache-dir per binary. Report before/after with n.
5. CRITICAL -- collateral damage: re-run search on at least 8 UNAFFECTED instances and confirm top-5
   hits are unchanged vs the pre-fix binary. Report any that moved. A fix that improves 3 instances
   and perturbs 20 is a net loss.

Report: the diff as a unified patch, test evidence, before/after measurement, collateral check, and
your own honest assessment of whether this should ship.`,
  { label: 'fix:' + g.key, phase: 'Fix', isolation: 'worktree' })
  .then(r => ({ key: g.key, report: r }))
  .catch(() => null)))

const shipped = fixes.filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.report)

phase('Verify')

const verdict = await agent(CONTEXT + `
Fix attempts were made in isolated worktrees. Reports:

${shipped.map(f => '=== FIX: ' + f.key + ' ===\n' + f.report).join('\n\n')}

Your job is ADVERSARIAL REVIEW plus integration assessment. Do NOT rubber-stamp.

1. For each fix, judge independently whether the evidence supports shipping:
   - does the regression test genuinely fail without the change (did they PROVE it)?
   - is the full suite green?
   - was the cache-dir trap respected (tree-keyed cache -- a shared --cache-dir invalidates any A/B)?
   - is the collateral check real or a token gesture?
   - did any consult gold/oracle data as an INPUT? That invalidates the fix outright.
2. Rank fixes by measured benefit per unit of risk.
3. Assess composition: do any two touch the same ranking path such that effects are not additive,
   or could cancel?
4. State plainly which subset to ship, and the combined expected effect on the scope-contains-gold
   ceiling (currently 18/30 = 60%) and rank-1 accuracy (currently ~30%). If the honest answer is
   "none of these move the ceiling", say exactly that.

Be skeptical. Most proposed levers on this benchmark have failed under replication -- ten
payload-quality metrics are already dead. Default to "not proven" when evidence is thin.`,
  { label: 'verify:adversarial', phase: 'Verify' })

return { diagnosed: good.map(g => g.key), fixed: shipped.map(f => f.key), verdict }

Workflow launched — diagnose → fix-in-isolated-worktrees → adversarial review, on all four graph-level defects.

Taking your point seriously: I'd been treating the binary as fixed and tuning around it, when the binary is where the actual ceiling lives. Every one of these caps the lever that pays:

| defect | measured impact |
|---|---|
| `coverage_note` empty | 11 of 12 test-selection failures → caps validated-VERIFY at 60% |
| test files at rank 1 | 3 of the 10 most expensive instances point at a test, not the code |
| basename collision | caddy top-1 wrong in 9/9 cells |
| 4 absent helper scripts | silently emit a 0-byte payload; `_eganchor` is 3 of the 8 worked examples |

Each fix agent must prove its regression test fails without the change, keep all 1976 tests green, use a **separate `--cache-dir`** (the tree-keyed cache trap), and run a collateral check on 8 unaffected instances — a fix that helps 3 and perturbs 20 is a net loss. Then an adversarial reviewer that's told to default to "not proven."

Diagnosed both: the "corrupt cc_out" was a **mid-write read**, not a defect (ruff parses fine now — `success`, 56 turns), and two 0-byte sessions died and will be auto-retried since the skip guard tests for non-empty.

One thing I have to flag against my own pre-registration. G7 said "swap < 80%"; swap is at **87.7%**. But checking back through the session, swap was **9,103 MB before I launched anything** — it's this machine's steady state, not something my parallelism caused, and free memory has stayed flat at 4.5–5.6 GB throughout. So the gate was miscalibrated rather than violated. I'm recording that explicitly instead of quietly passing it, and at scoring time I'll run the check that actually matters: **arm time-window overlap** — if both arms ran interleaved, load pressure is symmetric and cannot favour either.

Current state:

| | |
|---|---|
| Cell 1 (MAXPF, full payload) | eg 6/30, baseline 6/30 · 0 empty payloads · 2 dead sessions auto-retrying |
| Cell 2 (VERCOV, `entire graph verify`) | staged, unblocked by the `O35_ADJ_RUNNABLE` gate fix |
| Binary workflow | 4 diagnostics running → isolated-worktree fixes → adversarial review |
| VERIFY toolchain agents | 2 of 4 reported; both independently proved `validated-fails` is structurally unreachable |

The early paired numbers are on n=2 and I'm not reading them — partial cells are exactly how a 47-point swing got published once on this benchmark.

The one genuinely new thing since your last message: because `validated-fails` can't fire on a green repo, **`entire graph verify`'s record-baseline/compare design is not just an optimisation — it's the only mechanism that can work here at all**, and it had never run because its gate required the impossible state. That's now fixed and staged.

content.text:

This is the smoking gun, and it's the most important finding of the session. The eg lucene transcript:

```
 5. ./gradlew :lucene:analysis:opennlp:test --tests '...' --offline     <- the VERIFY command. FAILS (offline, no deps)
 6. find / -name "opennlp-tools*.jar" ...
10. CP="lucene/core/build/classes/java/main:lucene/analysis/common/..."  <- HAND-ASSEMBLES A CLASSPATH
11-24. javac/java Repro13170.java, compile, run, recompile ...           <- 15 turns building its own harness
25. ./gradlew ... --offline   (retry)
```

Compare that against the exact sentence I stripped for fairness:

> *"do not build an alternative test harness, **hand-assemble a classpath**, or re-verify by reverting and reapplying the edit."*

**The agent did precisely what the removed clamp forbade, step for step.** So the chain is:

1. The tool hands the agent a real test command it derived (`gradlew ...`).
2. That command **fails on the environment**, not on the patch — the checkout was never provisioned.
3. The agent then tries to repair the environment, hand-assembling a classpath for 15 turns.
4. The anti-harness clamp was suppressing step 3 — and it's **generic methodology that needs no graph**.

Which means the tool was creating the damage with (1)+(2) and then being credited for suppressing it with (3). Remove the one-armed instruction for fairness, and what's left is net harm. This matches the campaign's oldest scar — a published −35% that became +9.1% when two one-armed instructions were removed.

**Summary of what just happened, because it's the session's main result:**

I found the actual mechanism behind eg's measured savings, and it isn't retrieval. The tool derives a real test command, that command fails on the *environment* rather than the patch, the agent burns ~15 turns hand-assembling a classpath to repair it, and the anti-harness clamp was suppressing damage the tool itself created. Measured at n=4 with a monotone correlation: eg built 27 harness commands vs baseline's 13, and the single instance eg won (+38%) is the single instance where it built *fewer* than baseline (1 vs 3).

The clamp can't be part of a fair measurement — it's generic methodology given to one arm. So the honest fix is to stop shipping a command that can't run here, which is what `EG_VERIFY_MODE=off` does, and which the codebase had **already measured** in a comment table nobody had wired into a config: *real runner +4.6 turns, no VERIFY line −4.7 turns*.

fix(sem): extract TypeScript bodyless declarations (overloads, ambients)

`entityFromNode` gated `function_signature` and `method_signature` to Dart on the
grounds that TypeScript uses those node types for interface members. That is only
half true: tree-sitter-typescript emits `function_signature` for EVERY bodyless
function declaration -- overload signatures, `declare function`, ambients, `.d.ts`
-- and `method_signature` for class-body overload declarations as well as interface
members. All of them were silently dropped.

Consequence: vue's `renderList.ts` (five overload signatures + one implementation)
exposed a single symbol covering only the implementation's lines, so the typed half
of the file was invisible to search and no query phrased in terms of the declared
parameter types could retrieve it. Measured 1 symbol before, 6 after.

The fix is additive and narrowly gated:

- `function_signature` in TypeScript becomes a function (or a method when scoped).
  An overload set is where the parameter types and generics live; the implementation's
  own signature is usually the erased `(source: any, ...)` catch-all.
- `method_signature` becomes a method ONLY inside a `class_body`, via the new
  `typeScriptClassBodySignature` helper. Interface and type-literal members stay
  inventory-only on purpose: they declare a contract, not a definition, and emitting
  them would make every `x.m()` call name-resolvable to a bodyless interface member.
  That is not hypothetical -- extending this to interface_body/object_type members
  fabricates a CALLS edge in TestTypeScriptNamespaceCallSkipsParameterReceiverRoots,
  where a parameter named `B` shadows a namespace and `B.parse()` then binds to
  `Client.parse` instead of resolving to nothing.

Dart behaviour is unchanged; the existing Dart paths are reached only when the
language is not TypeScript.

Verified: full `internal/sem` suite green (1976 tests). Symbol output is
byte-identical to the pre-fix binary on eight non-TypeScript repositories
(django, axum, gson, carbon, bat, caddy, fmt, rubocop), so the change is
attributable to TypeScript alone.
EOF

## The bug

`entityFromNode` gated both `function_signature` and `method_signature` to Dart, with the comment that TypeScript uses those node types for interface members. That is only half true.

tree-sitter-typescript emits `function_signature` for **every bodyless function declaration** — overload signatures, `declare function`, ambients, `.d.ts` — and `method_signature` for class-body overload declarations as well as interface members. All of them were silently dropped from the graph.

Concretely, vue's `renderList.ts` has five overload signatures plus one implementation. It exposed **1 symbol**, covering only the implementation's lines. Lines 10–53 — the entire typed surface — were unindexed, so no query phrased in terms of the declared parameter types could retrieve the file. After the fix: **6 symbols**.

## The fix

Additive, `+54` lines, no deletions, narrowly gated:

- **`function_signature`** in TypeScript becomes a `function` (or a `method` when scoped). An overload set is where the parameter types and generics live; the implementation's own signature is usually the erased `(source: any, ...)` catch-all.
- **`method_signature`** becomes a `method` **only inside a `class_body`**, via the new `typeScriptClassBodySignature` helper.

Interface and type-literal members deliberately stay inventory-only. They declare a contract, not a definition, and emitting them would make every `x.m()` call name-resolvable to a bodyless interface member. That is not hypothetical — extending this case to `interface_body`/`object_type` members fabricates a CALLS edge in `TestTypeScriptNamespaceCallSkipsParameterReceiverRoots`, where a parameter named `B` shadows a namespace and `B.parse()` then binds to `Client.parse` instead of correctly resolving to nothing.

Dart behaviour is unchanged — the existing Dart paths are reached only when the language is not TypeScript.

## Verification

- Full `internal/sem` suite green (**1976 tests**).
- New regression test `parser_typescript_regression_test.go` (+124 lines) covering overload sets, `declare function`, class-body overloads, and the interface-member exclusion.
- **Attribution check:** symbol output is byte-identical to the pre-fix binary on eight non-TypeScript repositories — django, axum, gson, carbon, bat, caddy, fmt, rubocop. So the change is attributable to TypeScript alone and cannot perturb other languages.

## Scope note

Repo-wide symbol gain is modest (vuejs +1.0%, docusaurus +2.1%) — this is a correctness fix for a whole class of declarations, not a broad indexing win. Its practical effect is concentrated in TypeScript codebases that use overloads and ambient declarations heavily.

Two fairness bugs that invalidate cells, the mechanism behind the tool's measured savings, and the zero-cost tooling that found both.

## 1. Fairness: the binary ships its own anti-harness clamp

`_pf_verify.py` sets `ANTI_HARNESS=''`, so the harness copy is gone. That is **not sufficient**. With `O35_VERIFY_ONLY=0` (full payload) the **binary's native VERIFY block** passes through unfiltered, carrying:

> `run it ONCE after editing; if it fails, fix the code and re-run THIS command.`
> `do not build an alternative test harness, hand-assemble a classpath, or re-verify by reverting and reapplying the edit.`

Older cells carried that in 3–8 of 30 prompts. Delivering the full payload puts it in **~30/30, against 0/30 baseline**. It is generic agent methodology, needs no graph, and is the same one-armed-instruction class that moved a published −35% to +9.1% once removed.

New `O35_STRIP_ADVICE=1` filter in `eg-q` strips the methodology sentences and keeps the derived **command** and its `targets` line. Verified: advice lines 3 → 0, `VERIFY:` retained, payload 4594 → 4390 bytes.

**The rule this generalises to: verify fairness in the prompt that SHIPPED, never in the config that was supposed to produce it.**

## 2. Fairness: four enrichment flags fail OPEN

`eg-q` shells out to `_eglit.py`, `_egsiblings.py`, `_egcallees.py`, `_eganchor.py` for `EG_LITERALS` / `EG_SIBLINGS` / `EG_CALLEES` / `EG_ANCHOR`. **All four files are absent from `tools/`.**

Setting any to `1` makes the search emit nothing — `prefetch.payload` is 0 bytes and the eg arm silently runs as a **baseline with a smaller prompt than the cells it is compared against**. No error, anywhere. Caught by a $0.49 smoke test; it would have destroyed a ~$160 cell invisibly.

`run_maxpf.sh` pins all four off and appends any empty-payload instance to `results/<TAG>.empty_payload` at run time.

## 3. The mechanism: the tool was suppressing damage it caused itself

Measured on 4 Opus pairs, monotone correlation:

```
tool derives a real test command
  -> command fails on the ENVIRONMENT (checkout never provisioned), not on the patch
  -> agent spends ~15 turns hand-assembling a classpath to repair it
  -> the anti-harness clamp suppressed exactly that
```

| instance | eg harness cmds | base harness cmds | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| lucene | 14 | 1 | eg costs 211% |
| fastlane | 6 | 4 | eg costs 96% |
| django | 6 | 5 | eg costs 16% |
| scikit-learn | 1 | 3 | **eg saves 38%** |

The only instance eg won is the only one where it built *fewer* harnesses than baseline. On lucene the agent ran `./gradlew --offline`, it failed, and it then ran `find / -name "opennlp-tools*.jar"`, hand-built `cp.txt`, and compiled and ran `Repro13170.java` across 15 turns.

Since the clamp cannot be part of a fair measurement, the honest fix is to stop shipping a command that cannot run here. `EG_VERIFY_MODE=off` does that — and `eg-q`'s own comment table had already measured it (turns, base→eg): **real runner +4.6, parse-only +0.8, runner-absent −6.0, no VERIFY line −4.7.**

## 4. `O35_ADJ_RUNNABLE` — un-gating adjudication from an impossibility

Default **off**; Round 16 behaviour unchanged unless enabled.

Round 16 gates adjudication on `validated-fails`. That state is **structurally unreachable on this benchmark**: the gold test ships in `test_patch`, which is never applied to the pristine checkout, so no command derived from the repo's own build files can fail pre-fix. Every instance that does fire, fires on *unrelated pre-existing breakage* (docusaurus: 13 failures in 4 other packages, one snapshot hardcoding "Copyright © 2023"). Confirmed independently by two toolchain sweeps.

So `entire graph verify` — whose whole design is record-a-baseline-then-compare, the only primitive that works on a green repo — had **never once run in a cell**, because its gate required the impossible state.

`non-covering` means the command ran and passed, which is exactly a usable pre-edit baseline. Admitting it takes adjudication from ~14% of instances to the measured **~60%** ceiling (`verify_ceiling.py`). Symmetry is unaffected: `ADJ_DIR` is TAG-scoped, so both arms are offered the same wrapper.

## 5. Tooling (all zero-cost, offline)

| tool | what it establishes |
|---|---|
| `concentration.py` | where total-token saving lives; strictly-gated loader. Top-1 instance is 8.7% of tokens; neutralising **all** losers is worth **+0.35 pt** |
| `score_cell.py` | paired geomean + bootstrap CI + per-token-class split + pre-registered gates |
| `verify_ceiling.py` | legitimate validated-VERIFY ceiling: **18/30 = 60%** (11 whole-suite, 7 scoped-hit, 9 wrong package, 3 no manifest) |
| `verify_pool.py` | value of a validated command, **with** the baseline-length confound check |
| `confidence_calibration.py` | score-margin calibration **AUC 0.503** — no signal at all; lever killed for \$0 |
| `does_calling_help.py` | **97.6%** of eg sessions never query the graph — it is a prompt injection, not a tool call |
| `phases.py` | LOCATE/ITERATE/POST decomposition |
| `recall_agent_query.py` | agent-authored query recall without the permalink leak |
| `loadlog.sh` | per-minute load sampling so arm symmetry is **proven**, not assumed |

Harness also gains `SHARD`/`NSHARD` and `REVERSE` workers. The same shard count is used for both arms, so load pressure — a documented sign-flipping confound here — stays balanced.

## Status of the numbers

Cells are still running on the corrected config. **No savings claim is made in this PR.** What is established: the two fairness bugs are real, the VERIFY damage chain is measured, and `validated-fails` is unreachable by construction.
EOF

input.content:
Runbook · benchmark instrumentation · rev. 2026-08-05

Measuring a code-retrieval tool honestly

Every headline this benchmark ever retracted was retracted for a reason on this page. Read §1 and §3 before running anything; they are where the money and the credibility go.

§1 · The cost model

Cost is not "tokens." Solve for per-token prices from the recorded total_cost_usd by least squares over the three classes rather than assuming them.

modelcache_readcache_createoutputcost share cr/cc/out
Fable 51.0020.3149.6322 / 39 / 39
Opus 50.5010.1924.7326 / 38 / 36
Sonnet0.296.3314.7841 / 31 / 28
Haiku0.102.094.9646 / 28 / 25
trap

"95% of tokens are cache_read" is a token count, not a cost share. Output is priced 20–50× higher and is 25–39% of the bill. A tool that cuts reading and raises writing loses money. Fable is the clean case: turns fell 10%, cost rose 15%, because output rose 14.7%.

Always report cache_read / cache_creation / output separately. Which class moved is the finding.

Cost ≈ messages × context. At large context a message costs ~446k cache-read tokens. Count messages, not tool calls.

§2 · The measurement gate

a session counts  IFF  subtype == "success"  AND  patch.diff is non-empty
pairs drop SYMMETRICALLY — if either arm fails an instance, the instance
leaves BOTH arms

Omitting the subtype check once inflated a "strong strata 22.0%" reading to a true 13.3%, and let a session that finished cleanly and wrote no patch at all report as "saving 52.2%". A session that does no work always looks cheap.

Also check before trusting any per-instance delta: num_turns, result length, and whether subtype == error_max_turns — those are right-censored, so true cost is ≥ recorded. And cc_out.json can be corrupt; a zero-byte or mid-write read is not a failed session. Score from transcripts when in doubt.

§3 · Fairness — the failure mode that has invalidated the most results

Every withdrawn headline here came from asymmetric prompts, not from the tool. Diff the two arms' prompt.txt and account for every differing line.

differenceverdict
tool verb syntax, ranked payload, derived commandlegitimate capability the other arm cannot have
generic frugality, "few turns", "don't grep"fraud needs no tool
"do not build an alternative test harness…"fraud generic methodology
an eg-only verify.run wrapperfraud unless both arms get one
worktree path substitutionnoise harmless

A "−35%" once came from two extra instructions the tool arm had and the baseline did not. Removing them moved the same cell from −14.9% to +9.1%.

the rule

Verify fairness in the prompt that SHIPPED, never in the config that was supposed to produce it. A tool can emit its own advice and re-introduce an asymmetry you already disabled one layer up. This was found live: the harness clamp was set to '' and verified, and the binary's native copy sailed straight through into ~30/30 prompts.

Distinguish "the tool as shipped, including its recommended prompt" from "the tool's marginal value under one fixed contract." Both are real questions. Say which you measured.

§4 · Traps that produce a clean-looking wrong number

Flags that fail open

Four enrichment flags shell out to helper scripts that do not exist. Setting any to 1 makes the search emit nothing — a 0-byte payload, no error — and the tool arm silently runs as a baseline with a smaller prompt than its comparison group.

Tell: prefetch.payload is 0 bytes. Guard: fail any tool session with an empty payload at run time.

The tree-keyed index cache

The cache key is the tree, not the binary. A/B two builds without a separate --cache-dir each and the second silently returns the first's results. This has cost real money twice.

Transcript parsing

One API response spans several JSONL lines sharing a message.id. You must UNION the content blocks. Keeping "the longest line" drops tool_use and keeps empty thinking. Opus 5 thinking blocks are encrypted — 1094 of 1094 empty — so never analyse thinking text. A claim once sourced from it was measuring empty strings.

Load pressure flips the sign

Whichever arm runs starved of RAM or disk measures worse, and the direction inverts between cells. Run the same worker count per arm, sample load per minute, and prove symmetry rather than assuming it. The strong form: both arms on the same instance within seconds of each other.

Environment, not patch

A derived test command that fails because the checkout was never provisioned sends the agent off to repair the environment — hand-assembling a classpath for 15 turns. Measured: real runner +4.6 turns, no command at all −4.7 turns. Shipping a command you cannot run is worse than shipping none.

Shell and filesystem

pgrep -fc is invalid on macOS — it exits 2 and prints nothing, so || echo 0 reports a healthy run as dead. An unmatched glob aborts the whole command line in zsh, so a cleanup rm -rf silently never runs. The Go module cache is read-only; chmod -R u+rwX before removing.

§5 · The noise floor, and what it costs to claim

per-session replicate sd  s ≈ 0.276      arm×instance  τ ≈ 0.09
1 + 1 replicate   ±14.1%
3 + 3 trimmed     ± 6.4%
floor at n=30     ± 3.4%

TO CLAIM ≥25%  YOU MUST MEASURE  ≈ 31.4%

Same-instance spread across repeated cells is 45pt median, tail to 335pt. The cleanest demonstration available: two cells with byte-identical prompts, binary, flags, CLI version and zero attrition measured 15.2% and 3.6% — 11.6 points apart from nothing at all.

  • Never score a partial cell. One geomean moved 47 points between n=9 and n=25.
  • Never bucket one cell into sub-groups of 3–7 and read the differences. That is how two "levers" were produced and then retracted.
  • Compare configs with replicates of the same config, not two configs' point estimates.
  • Report bootstrap CIs. A point estimate of 25% with a CI spanning 5–45% is reported as exactly that — not as "goal met".
  • Trust deterministic offline replays far more than single-session attributions. 0/30 instances produce the same agent query twice.

§6 · The graveyard — do not re-propose

leverwhy it is dead
payload-quality metricsTen distinct metrics have failed as causal token levers, including editability, aim and line-coverage. Treat as law.
per-loser / per-repo repairNeutralising every losing instance is worth +0.35 pt. 93% of instances flip win/lose sign between cells; none loses consistently.
LOCATE-reduction elasticitycorr(LOCATE delta, token delta) = +0.188. One cell cut LOCATE by 4.74 calls and saved 7.1%; another made it worse and saved 15.2%.
confidence tier on score marginAUC 0.503. Mean margin is higher when rank-1 is wrong. No signal exists to gate on.
prefetching the query from issue textgold-visible@5 0.567 vs 0.715 for the agent's own query. 8 losses, 0 wins.
raising the turn capboth arms grow proportionally.
oracle config selection across cellsmin-of-k is invariant to label shuffling — the "oracle" exactly equals the null.
native MCP deliveryno schemas arrive, zero tool_use blocks. Also --safe-mode silently strips every MCP server.

Publish the retractions. A wrong note propagates.

§7 · Procedure

  1. Verify the data before analysing it

    Confirm repo clones, graphs and a patch.diff for every gated session. A driver that skips on the session log alone will skip forever a session whose patch vanished — and the lost instances skew toward the ones the tool won big, biasing against it. Keep the suite off volatile paths.

  2. Pre-register

    Write the prediction, the falsification band, and the gates to a file before the run. An out-of-sample prediction that survives is worth more than ten post-hoc explanations. Include one decisive internal test that is free of cross-cell confounds.

  3. Falsify offline first — it is free

    Replay recorded queries against the binary and assert the change does what you claim and that nothing else moved. Replay across every recorded query variant; the agent rephrases every run. Kill any lever whose addressable pool is smaller than ~5 points of total tokens — it cannot matter.

  4. Smoke-test the config on one instance

    Then read the shipped prompt: payload non-empty, no one-armed methodology, no oracle path, the flags you set actually took effect. A $0.49 smoke test has already caught two bugs that would each have destroyed a ~$160 cell invisibly.

  5. Run both arms interleaved

    Equal workers per arm, load sampled throughout. Then check ENOSPC from transcripts, not logfiles (one cell showed 1 hit in logs against 10 in transcripts), censoring symmetry, and arm time-window overlap.

  6. Score

    Paired geomean over instances + instance-level bootstrap, reported alongside total (Σ/Σ) — never instead of it. Then the per-token-class split. Then per-language. Then per-instance sorted by contribution.

  7. Decompose the transcripts — this is where the answers are

    Phase-split at the first and last edit. Attribute output tokens per tool. Count edits, distinct files, throwaway scripts. Classify every residual search: finding something new (recall), searching inside a file the payload returned, re-finding a symbol the payload contained, or env/build hunting.

§8 · Standing results

measured

Grep elimination is the strongest predictor found. corr(search ratio, log token ratio) ≈ +0.575 [+0.476, +0.672], n=113 Opus pairs, while corr(baseline greps, outcome) ≈ 0 — so it is not task difficulty leaking through. Fit: log(tokratio) = −0.635 + 0.475 × search_ratio.

measured

The tool is a prompt injection, not a tool call. 97.6% of tool-arm sessions never query the graph once. Whatever effect exists comes from the block appended to the prompt. Fixing invocation alone does not convert: raising usage from 0.042 to 1.75 calls/session added calls rather than replacing greps, and that cell still cost money.

structural

A "validated" test command is unreachable by construction here. The gold test ships in test_patch, never applied to the pristine tree, so no command derived from the repo's own build files can fail pre-fix. Every instance that fires does so on unrelated pre-existing breakage — firing rate measures how broken a repo's suite already is, not command quality. Record-a-baseline-then-compare is the only primitive that works on a green repo.

Discipline: keep an audit ledger tagging every claim solid / moderate / retracted, with its basis. When a result contradicts an earlier one, find the mechanism before believing either. Correct notes in place when falsified. Do not stop at a negative finding — but going deeper is not a licence to loosen the standard of evidence. Report the interval, report the retractions, and say plainly when a target was not reached.

input.content:
Runbook · four-arm token benchmark · rev. 2026-08-05

Fresh machine to a four-arm result

Everything needed to reproduce a 300-instance, four-arm token measurement from a bare checkout — and the guardrails that stop it producing a confident wrong number. Default scale is 300 × 4 arms; §7 scales it down to 100 or 30.

§0 · What is being measured

Four arms solve the same SWE-bench Multilingual instances with the same agent and prompt scaffold. The only difference is what code-context tooling each is handed.

armwhat it getsrole
baselinenothing — shell, read, editthe control; every ratio is against this
egentire-graph payloadtool under test
cmmcodebase-memory-mcpcomparator
graphifygraphify indexcomparator

Output is tokens and cost per instance, paired against the control. Resolve grading is a separate, optional stage (§9) and is not installed by default — every number is token-only until you install it, and must be labelled so.

§1 · Prerequisites

claude   >= 2.1.221   # record the version — it shifts results ~5 points between minor releases
gh                    # authenticated: gh auth status
go       >= 1.22      # CGO required (tree-sitter)
python3  >= 3.11
git, docker, uv

Hardware actually used: 48 GB RAM, ~8 concurrent sessions comfortably (≈1–2 GB resident each, plus whatever the repo's own build wants — a JDK or cargo build is the real consumer).

before you start

Reclaim disk first. A previous run filled the volume mid-batch and killed dockerd, losing a whole cell. Budget in §7; keep the suite off volatile paths like /private/tmp, which gets reaped.

§2 · Bootstrap

  1. Clone and create the environment

    git clone https://github.com/entirehq/graphmark.git
cd graphmark/agentic-swebench
uv venv .venv --python 3.11
uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python datasets tiktoken tabulate

  2. Build the tool binary and pin it by hash

    git clone https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph.git
cd entire-graph && go build -o entire-graph ./cmd/entire-graph
cp entire-graph  ../graphmark/agentic-swebench/bin/entire-graph-<sha>
shasum -a 256 ../graphmark/agentic-swebench/bin/entire-graph-<sha>

    entire graph version reports dev, so the sha256 is the only real pin. Record it in the run manifest. A binary swapped without a recorded hash has silently caused a −7.9 point regression to be attributed to a config.

  3. Build the graphs

    tools/batch_graphs_rep30.sh          # or batch_graphs_rep100.sh / batch_graphs.sh for 300
tools/build_graphify_graph.sh       # graphify arm only

    Roughly 5 s and ~7 MB per repo for entire-graph. Check graphify's output: it fails to build on ~9 of 30 instances (nodes=0), and a tool-build failure must remove the instance from all four arms symmetrically — never just from the arm that failed, or the arm whose tool is worst gets its own worst instances deleted.

§3 · Configure

Copy tools/run_maxpf.sh as your cell launcher. The settings below are not defaults — each one is the result of a measurement, and three of them are load-bearing for fairness.

settingwhy
PUBLISHED_EXACT=1Anthropic's published SWE-bench prompt, byte-identical across arms
EG_PREFETCH=1
EG_PREFETCH_IMPACT=1
EG_PREFETCH_TEST=1		deliver the payload that is computed anyway; without these it is written to disk and discarded
O35_VERIFY_ONLY=0inject the full ranked payload, not a single locator line
O35_STRIP_ADVICE=1fairness. Strips the binary's own generic methodology sentences, keeps its derived command
EG_VERIFY_MODE=offmeasured. A real runner command costs +4.6 turns; no command saves 4.7
EG_LITERALS/SIBLINGS/CALLEES/ANCHOR=0must stay 0. Their helper scripts do not exist; setting them to 1 emits an empty payload with no error
O35_QUERY_V2=0, O35_QUERY_V3=0V3 leaked the gold path out of GitHub permalinks, tool-arm only
GQ_SEARCH_CAP=0a frugality clamp on tool arms while the control greps uncapped
CC_MODEL, CC_MAX_TURNS=120assert the resolved model per session from modelUsage; mixed-model pairs are silent poison

§4 · Preflight — all of this is free, and all of it has caught a real bug

1  disk headroom  >= budget in §7          df -g $HOME
2  binary present and hash recorded
3  graphs built; graphify failures listed and symmetrically excluded
4  ANTI_HARNESS == '' in tools/_pf_verify.py
5  smoke ONE instance end to end (~$1), then READ THE SHIPPED PROMPT:
     prefetch.payload  > 0 bytes
     grep -c '^VERIFY:'                 -> expected for your config
     grep -c 'alternative test harness' -> 0
     grep -c 'FAIL_TO_PASS'             -> 0
     diff eg/prompt.txt baseline/prompt.txt  -> account for EVERY line
the rule

Verify fairness in the prompt that shipped, never in the config that was supposed to produce it. Found the hard way: the harness clamp was set to '' and verified — and the binary's own native copy sailed through into ~30/30 prompts against 0/30 control.

§5 · Run

Default: 300 instances × 4 arms. Workers are sharded; the same shard count must be used for every arm so load pressure stays balanced.

# 4 workers per arm, all four arms, 300-instance set
for arm in baseline eg cmm graphify; do
  for sh in 0 1 2 3; do
    nohup env ARM=$arm TAG=RUN300 SHARD=$sh NSHARD=4 \
      TASKS_FILE=$PWD/tasks/multilingual_300.json \
      bash tools/run_maxpf.sh > results/RUN300.$arm.s$sh.log 2>&1 &
  done
done

nohup bash tools/loadlog.sh results/RUN300.loadlog.tsv >/dev/null 2>&1 &   # prove symmetry

Instances are idempotent — a driver skips any instance with a non-empty cc_out.json — so workers can be added, killed and restarted freely, and REVERSE=1 lets a second worker walk the same arm from the far end.

health, while running
eg N/300  base N/300              per-arm completion
dead sessions per arm             0-byte cc_out with no .running marker
results/<TAG>.empty_payload       MUST stay empty
loadlog: eg_running == base_running   at every sample

The strong form of the symmetry check: both arms on the same instance within seconds of each other. Under that pattern, load pressure cannot favour either.

§6 · Chaining cells

Never run two cells concurrently. Load pressure is a documented sign-flipping confound — whichever arm is starved measures worse, and the direction inverts between cells. Chain instead:

cat > tools/chain.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.."
count(){ local a=$1 n=0; for f in results/$TAG_r1_$a/$a/*/cc_out.json; do [ -s "$f" ] && n=$((n+1)); done; echo $n; }
while :; do
  drivers=$(ps -A -o pid=,command= | awk '$2=="bash" && /run_maxpf/' | wc -l)
  [ "$drivers" -eq 0 ] && break
  sleep 60
done
# ... launch the next cell here
EOF

Same pattern for a second model: finish, then start. Comparing models needs the same machine state, not the same wall clock.

§7 · Scale, cost and time

Derived from measured Opus sessions (~$2.75 mean, ~2.4 M tokens) at 8 workers ≈ 0.6 completed sessions/minute. Cheaper models scale down roughly with the price table in §10.

setinstancessessions (4 arms)cost, Opuswall clock @8w@16wdisk
multilingual_300.json default3001,200~$3,300~33 h~17 h~250 GB
rep100_tasks.json100400~$1,100~11 h~6 h~85 GB
rep30_tasks.json30120~$330~3.5 h~2 h~25 GB
rep30, 2 arms only3060~$165~1.7 h~1 h~13 GB

Change scale by pointing TASKS_FILE at a different set — nothing else changes. Add replicates by re-running with a new TAG; the launcher's skip-guard means a repeated TAG resumes rather than redoes.

what n buys you
1 + 1 replicate   ±14.1%      3 + 3 trimmed   ±6.4%      floor at n=30   ±3.4%
TO CLAIM  >=25%   YOU MUST MEASURE  ~31.4%

30 instances cannot resolve a config difference under ~30 points. Measured directly: two cells with byte-identical prompts, binary, flags, CLI version and zero attrition read 15.2% and 3.6%. If your effect is smaller than that, go to 100 or add replicates — do not read a single 30.

§8 · Score

python3 tools/score_cell.py RUN300

The gate, applied identically to every arm:

count a session IFF  subtype == "success"  AND  patch.diff non-empty
drop pairs SYMMETRICALLY — if any arm fails an instance, it leaves ALL arms

Omitting the subtype check once inflated a 13.3% result to "22.0%", and let a session that finished cleanly and wrote no patch at all report as "saving 52.2%". A session that does no work always looks cheap.

Report paired geomean with a bootstrap CI and total (Σ/Σ) — never one instead of the other — then the split by token class. Cache_read, cache_creation and output move independently, and which one moved is the finding.

Integrity sweep before quoting anything

  • ENOSPC from transcripts, not *.log — one cell showed 1 hit in logs against 10 in transcripts
  • censoring (error_max_turns) symmetric between arms
  • arm time-window overlap ≥ 70%
  • corrupt/empty cc_out.json; per-instance prompt diff; foreign-cache markers

§9 · Resolve grading (optional, not installed)

uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python swebench
tools/assemble_preds.py && tools/run_eval_model.sh    # Docker only, $0 API

Power is ±12.5 pp at n=30×3, so pre-register a non-inferiority margin and state that anything smaller is undetectable at that size. Until this is installed, write "token-only" in the same sentence as every number.

§10 · Guardrails

modelcache_readcache_createoutputcost share
Fable 51.0020.3149.6322 / 39 / 39
Opus 50.5010.1924.7326 / 38 / 36
Sonnet0.296.3314.7841 / 31 / 28
Haiku0.102.094.9646 / 28 / 25

$/Mtok. "95% of tokens are cache_read" is a token count, not a cost share — output is priced 20–50× higher and is a quarter to two-fifths of the bill. A tool that cuts reading and raises writing loses money.

Traps that produce a clean-looking wrong number

  • Tree-keyed index cache. A/B two binaries without a separate --cache-dir each and the second silently returns the first's results.
  • Transcript parsing. One API response spans several JSONL lines sharing a message.id; UNION the content blocks. Keeping "the longest" drops tool_use. Opus thinking blocks are encrypted — 1094/1094 empty — so never analyse thinking text.
  • Environment, not patch. A derived command that fails because the checkout was never provisioned sends the agent to repair the environment — 15 turns hand-assembling a classpath.
  • Shell. pgrep -fc is invalid on macOS (exits 2, prints nothing, so || echo 0 calls a healthy run dead). An unmatched glob aborts the whole command line in zsh, so cleanup silently never runs. The Go module cache is read-only — chmod -R u+rwX first.

Do not re-propose

  • Payload-quality metrics — ten have failed as causal token levers. Treat as law.
  • Per-loser repair — neutralising every losing instance is worth +0.35 pt; 93% flip sign between cells.
  • LOCATE-reduction elasticity — corr(ΔLOCATE, Δtokens) = +0.188.
  • Confidence tier on score margin — AUC 0.503; the margin is higher when rank-1 is wrong.
  • Query prefetch from issue text — 8 losses, 0 wins against the agent's own query.
  • Oracle config selection — min-of-k is invariant to label shuffling; it equals the null exactly.

Standing results

  • Grep elimination is the strongest predictor. corr(search ratio, log token ratio) ≈ +0.575 [+0.476, +0.672], n=113, while corr(baseline greps, outcome) ≈ 0 — so it is not difficulty leaking through.
  • The tool is a prompt injection, not a tool call. 97.6% of tool-arm sessions never query it once.
  • A "validated" test command is unreachable by construction. The gold test ships in test_patch, never applied to the pristine tree, so nothing derived from the repo's build files can fail pre-fix. Every firing instance fires on unrelated pre-existing breakage.

Keep an audit ledger tagging every claim solid / moderate / retracted, with its basis. When a result contradicts an earlier one, find the mechanism before believing either. Correct notes in place when falsified. Do not stop at a negative finding — but going deeper is not a licence to loosen the standard of evidence. Report the interval, publish the retractions, and say plainly when a target was not reached.

It's operational now — clone → venv → build binary → build graphs → configure → preflight → run → score, with the 300/100/30 scale table (cost, wall-clock at 8 and 16 workers, disk), chaining, and the guardrails inline.

**Found it. The payload is charged rent on every turn, and the correlation is perfect:**

```
instance   payload delta   cache_read/turn      outcome
carbon        +5.2 KB      51.6K vs 50.0K  +3%   saving  1.8%   <- smallest payload, ONLY winner
caddy        +14.9 KB      49.4K vs 42.4K +17%   costing 0.1%
lucene       +11.2 KB      42.0K vs 31.0K +36%   costing 78.9%
ruff          +7.1 KB      45.9K vs 31.7K +45%   costing 43.8%
```

Bigger payload → bigger per-turn context penalty → worse outcome, monotonically. **A 15 KB payload re-read across 45 turns is ~170K tokens of pure rent** — and it buys nothing after turn 1, because the agent already read it.

This explains the whole campaign's shape: the RUNG2 family used a **one-line** locator and saved 9–15%. I replaced it with 15 KB of bodies and it started costing. I optimised the wrong direction.
